data.title: The War on the Walkman
data.author: mfiguiere
data.article_summary: 《The Forgotten War on the Walkman》一文回顾了1979年索尼Walkman面世后引发的争议。虽然Walkman如今被视为1980年代的象征，带来怀旧情感，但其诞生之初却遭遇不少批评。文化评论家认为Walkman加剧了个人主义，导致社会隔离，甚至有人将其比作“感官抑制剂”。批评者还担心Walkman影响驾驶和行人的安全，美国多个州因此立法限制使用头戴式耳机。新泽西州Woodbridge镇甚至禁止步行过街时佩戴Walkman耳机，违者可能面临罚款和监禁。一位抗议该法律的居民Oscar Gross虽有意上诉至最高法院，但在一名耳机佩戴者发生交通事故后放弃。文章提醒人们，新技术往往面临抵制，怀旧情绪常让人忘记曾经的争议。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：科技发展对社会互动和人际关系的影响，特别是耳机和移动设备的使用。

不同观点：
• **怀旧与趋势变化**：[wkat4242] 提到从轻便耳机到笨重耳机的趋势转变，并怀念寻呼机时代，认为那时的隐私性更好。
• **人际疏离**：[sevensor] 认为佩戴耳机使人更难与陌生人交流，可能加剧人际疏离。
• **音乐发现与选择**：[comrade1234] 强调流媒体时代音乐发现的多样性，并偏好由人类策划的音乐内容而非算法推荐。
• **科技对注意力的影响**：[MarkusWandel] 指出智能手机和无线耳机的普及导致人们对周围环境和社交互动的忽视。
• **历史对比与道德恐慌**：[xg15] 认为虽然新技术常引发道德恐慌，但其对社会结构的影响需要具体分析，未必与过去相同。
• **适应与生存**：[tempodox] 认为尽管技术变化迅速，人类社会依然适应并生存下来。
• **多功能设备的影响**：[tom89999] 指出手机等多功能设备增加了分心和干扰，影响个人专注力。
• **批判性视角**：[atorodius] 引用历史批判观点，认为耳机和移动设备可能鼓励个人从社会连接中抽离。
• **广告与内容选择**：[relaxing] 认为便携式录音机提供了无广告和用户选择的体验，与算法推荐的内容不同。
• **耳机与公共噪音**：[Lio] 更喜欢戴耳机的人的沉默，而不是公共场合大声播放低质量内容的人。
• **自由的代价**：[gwern] 引用悲剧故事，认为某些自由的代价是不可避免的。
• **历史反思**：[Nifty3929] 提醒人们在关注当前问题时也要反思历史。
• **未来展望**：[jb1991] 认为未来变化可能让当前的技术看起来微不足道。
• **同理心的交易性**：[deadbabe] 批评现代社会中同理心的交易性本质。

补充讨论：
• 评论中涉及多个历史和现代科技对比，强调技术对社会行为和心理的影响。
• 争议焦点在于科技是否真正导致人际疏离，以及如何平衡个人自由与社会责任。
• 不同用户对音乐发现和内容消费的偏好也反映了技术变化带来的多样性体验。

🗓️  On this day in 1979 the Sony Walkman was first released, marking its 46th anniversary
The Sony Walkman is now an icon of the 1980s, eliciting nostalgia for the ‘good old days’ of owning music, rather than renting it. Affection for the device is now universal, but that wasn’t always the case…
The sudden rise of headphone wearing pedestrians - spurred by Sony’s lightweight headsets (17% the weight of others) - caused unease about an unfamiliar new world quickly coming into view.
Some said it was a sign of a continued rise of Reagan and Thatcher style individualism. Cultural critic Allan Bloom deemed the Walkman
"a nonstop... masturbational fantasy”
in his 1987 book ‘The Closing of the American Mind.’ Neo-Luddite John Zerzan saw the Walkman as part of a modern trend that encouraged a
"protective sort of withdrawal from social connections"
and Thomas Lipscomb, chief of the Center for the Digital Future, equated it with the euphoric drug "soma," from Huxley's Brave New World, creating, as he put it,
"an airtight bubble of sound"
that was nothing but a
"sensory depressant."
In other words it all felt ‘a bit blackmirror’ as one might say today.
(A collection of quotes collected in this 1999 Reason Magazine
article
)
The Walkman, critics claimed, was more than just music to one's ears; it was a tool of societal disconnect and for government officials and law enforcement a danger on the roads, because it limited the hearing of drivers, cyclists and pedestrians.
After a number of accidents involving Walkman headphones, numerous states across the US swiftly put into effect or proposed restrictions, many related to headphone use while driving or cycling. Among them were statutes in California, Florida, Georgia, , Minnesota, Pennsylvania, Virginia, and Washington.
The New Jersey township of Woodbridge went a step further, forbidding not just driving or biking, but even crossing the street while wearing Walkman headphones.
The price for breaking this prohibition? A potential two-week stay in jail and a fine. The law made national and international news, including the BBC who got reactions on the street:
The day the law was put into effect - Oscar Gross - a retiree from a neighbouring town, was spurred into action. Seething, he approached Police Sergeant Lou Monzo, purposefully donned his headphones, and crossed the street.
The outcome of this small act of civil disobedience? Gross became the first person to receive a citation for wearing headphones (even though they weren’t plugged into anything.) Undeterred, he stated in an interview,
"I’m prepared to go to jail for 15 days just to prove a point."
Gross end up being interviewed for national outlets as did members of the Woodbridge town council. However, to his disappointment, Gross was not sent to jail. After the judge imposed a $50 fine, which was later suspended, a frustrated Gross said to a journalist:
"He didn't even give me the opportunity to say that I was willing to serve time in jail."
"No municipality has the right to tell somebody what they can wear." -
Oscar Gross
Oscar Gross was
preparing
to take the case all the way to the supreme court, but backed out after someone was killed crossing the street while wearing headphones. The kind of tragic anecdote that is the inevitable and unavoidable price of freedom.
This chapter in techno-pessimism is a good reminder that nostalgia tends to elicit amnesia about the resistance new technologies once faced. After all, who would have thought the “good old days” could ever have been considered a bad, brave new world?

data.title: AI is coming for agriculture, but farmers aren’t convinced
data.author: lr0
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了澳大利亚农业正面临技术变革，尤其是人工智能（AI）和数字化技术的应用。尽管全球已投入巨资开发如授粉机器人、智能土壤传感器和AI决策系统，但农民对这些技术的看法复杂。作者团队采访了数十位澳大利亚农民，发现他们对技术需求有深刻理解，但同时对科技公司过于理想化的承诺持谨慎态度。农民用“shit in, shit out”来表达对不可靠数据输入的担忧，并希望技术“更多自动化，更少功能”，即简单、可靠、能替代人力的工具。文章还通过农民对Suzuki Sierra Stockman车型的喜爱，强调未来农业技术应简单、可适应、可靠，就像过去的经典农用设备。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：未来农业与技术（尤其是自动化和人工智能）在农业中的应用

不同观点：
• Scoundreller认为，在澳大利亚等劳动力稀缺的地区，机器被创造来填补人力的空缺，暗示技术是为了应对高昂的劳动力成本。
• NoPicklez以Toyota Landcruiser 70系列为例，指出有些机器虽然价格高昂但没有过多的附加功能，胜在可靠耐用。
• bryanlarsen设想AI无人机可以减少对单一作物文化的依赖，转而采用多作物文化，通过小型无人机进行个体植物层面的操作，以替代昂贵的机械化大规模操作。
• euroderf希望有一种智能系统，可以利用传感器和图像数据帮助管理家庭菜园，反映了对自动化园艺管理的需求。
• conradfr指出，农民需要的技术不一定要有很多附加功能，而是能够可靠地减轻他们的工作负担。
• andrewrn分享了在草莓采摘机器人项目中的经验，认为尽管技术有潜力，但许多技术创业公司由于不切实际的期望和技术问题而失败，导致农民对新技术持怀疑态度。
• erikerikson区分了畜牧业与农业的差异，指出其研究主要集中在畜牧业生产者上，暗示农业技术需求可能因领域而异。
• zkmon提到在发展中国家，由于农民缺乏教育和资源，他们依赖化学品和低质量的杂交品种，导致食品质量下降，反映了对技术教育和资源分配的需求。
• frainfreeze以调侃方式表达了对未来农业技术发展方向的关注。
• Scoundreller再次提出，GMO技术初期也遇到过抵制，质疑未来是否会出现“无AI食品”，并将其与有机食品概念联系起来。
• theodric认为，农业自动化并非其主要需求，更需要帮助销售产品，反映出产品流通和市场需求的重要性。
• SideburnsOfDoom以幽默方式指出，农业中“投入”如肥料是预期且有益的，强调了农业中特有的自然循环过程。

补充讨论：
- 自动化和人工智能在农业中的实际应用场景与技术挑战（如草莓采摘机器人）。
- 农民对技术的实际需求与技术公司开发产品之间的差距。
- 农业技术在不同地区和文化背景下的不同需求和应用，尤其是在发展中国家。
- 未来农业技术可能引发的社会与市场反应，如对“无AI食品”的需求。

Australian farms are
at the forefront
of a wave of technological change coming to agriculture. Over the past decade, more than US$200 billion (A$305 billion) has been invested globally into the likes of pollination robots, smart soil sensors and artificial intelligence (AI) systems to help make decisions.
What do the people working the land make of it all? We
interviewed dozens of Australian farmers
about AI and digital technology, and found they had a sophisticated understanding of their own needs and how technology might help – as well as a wariness of tech companies’ utopian promises.
The future of farming
The supposed revolution coming to agriculture goes by several names: “
precision agriculture
”, “
smart farming
”, and “
agriculture 4.0
” are some of the more common ones.
These names all gesture towards a future in which the relationships between humans, computing and nature have been significantly reconfigured. Perhaps remote sensing technology will monitor ever more of a farm system, autonomous vehicles will patrol it, and AI will predict crop growth or cattle weight gain.
But there’s another story to tell about the way technological change happens. It involves people and communities creating their own future, their own sense of important change from the past.
AI, country style
Our research team conducted more than 35 interviews with farmers, specifically livestock producers, from across Australia.
The dominant themes of their responses were captured in two pithy quotes: “shit in, shit out” and “more automation, less features”.
“Shit in, shit out” is an earthier version of the “garbage in, garbage out” adage in computer science. If the data going into a model is unreliable or overly abstract, then the outputs will be shaped by those errors.
This captured a real concern for many farmers. They didn’t feel they could trust new technologies if they didn’t understand what knowledge and information they had been built with.
A different kind of automation
On the other hand, “more automation, less features” is what farmers want: technologies that may not have a lot of bells and whistles, but can reliably take a task off their hands.
Australian farmers have a ready appetite for labour-saving technologies. When human bodies are scarce, as they often are in rural Australia, machines are created to fill the void.
Windmills, wire fences, and even the iconic Australian sheepdog have been a crucial part of the technological narrative of settler colonial farming. These things are not “autonomous” in the same way as computer-powered vehicles and drones, but they offer similar advantages to farmers.
What these classic farm technologies have in common is a simplicity that derives from a clarity of purpose. They are the opposite of the “
everything apps
” that fuel the dreams of many Silicon Valley entrepreneurs.
“More automation, less features” is in this sense a farmer envisaging a digital product that fits with their image of a useful technology: transparent in its operations, and a reliable replacement for or an addition to human labour.
The lesson of the Suzuki Sierra Stockman
When speaking with one farmer about favoured technologies of her lifetime, she mentioned the Suzuki Sierra Stockman. These small, no-frills, four-wheel-drive vehicles became something of an icon on Australian sheep and cattle farms through the 1970s, ‘80s and '90s.
By the 1990s, the Suzuki Sierra Stockman had an iconic status among Australian farmers.
Turbo_J / Flickr
Reflecting on her memories of first using the vehicle, the farmer said:
Once I learnt that I could actually draft cattle out with the Suzuki, that changed everything. You could do exactly what you did on a horse with a vehicle.
It seems unlikely that Suzuki’s engineers in Japan envisaged their little jeep chasing cattle in the paddocks of Central West of NSW. The Suzuki was in a sense remade by farmers who found innovative uses for it.
Future technology must be simple, adaptable and reliable
The combustion engine was a key technological change on farms in the 20th century. Computers may play a similar role

data.author: zdw
data.article_summary:
Intel的Lion Cove P-Core是其最新的高性能CPU架构，相比前代Raptor Cove，提升了每周期执行指令数，重新设计了执行引擎并增加了一级数据缓存。在标准SPEC CPU2017测试中表现优异，尤其在IPC（每周期指令数）较高的子测试中。尽管在Arrow Lake桌面平台上能效更高且整体优于Raptor Cove，但游戏性能更受关注。

游戏负载的IPC较低，Lion Cove在游戏中的表现受限于前端和后端延迟。通过自顶向下分析发现，后端内存延迟是导致流水线槽利用率低的主要原因，L1.5缓存虽缓解了部分L2压力但命中率一般。尽管大部分L1未命中数据能在核内解决，但访问L3和DRAM的延迟较高，影响了性能。

Lion Cove is Intel’s latest high performance CPU architecture. Compared to its predecessor, Raptor Cove, Intel’s newest core can sustain more instructions per cycle, reorganizes the execution engine, and adds an extra level to the data cache hierarchy. The list of changes goes on, with tweaks to just about every part of the core pipeline. Lion Cove does well in the standard SPEC CPU2017 benchmark suite, where it posts sizeable gains especially in higher IPC subtests. In the Arrow Lake desktop platform, Lion Cove can often go head-to-head against AMD’s Zen 5, and posts an overall lead over Intel’s prior Raptor Cove while pulling less power. But a lot of enthusiasts are interested in gaming performance, and games have different demands from productivity workloads.
Here, I’ll be running a few games while collecting performance monitoring data. I’m using the Core Ultra 9 285K with DDR5-6000 28-36-36-96, which is the fastest memory I have available. E-Cores are turned off in the BIOS, because setting affinity to P-Cores caused massive stuttering in Call of Duty. In Cyberpunk 2077, I’m using the built-in benchmark at 1080P and medium settings, with upscaling turned off. In Palworld, I’m hanging out near a base, because CPU load tends to be higher with more entities around.
Gaming workloads generally fall at the low end of the IPC range. Lion Cove can sustain eight micro-ops per cycle, which roughly corresponds to eight instructions per cycle because most instructions map to a single micro-op. It posts very high IPC figures in several SPEC CPU2017 tests, with some pushing well past 4 IPC. Games however get nowhere near that, and find company with lower IPC tests that see their performance limited by frontend and backend latency.
Top-Down View
Top-down analysis
characterizes how well an application is utilizing a CPU core’s width, and accounts for why pipeline slots go under-utilized. This is usually done at the rename/allocate stage, because it’s often the narrowest stage in the core’s pipeline, which means throughput lost at that stage can’t be recovered later. To briefly break down the reasons:
Bad Speculation: Slot was utilized, but the core was going down the wrong path. That’s usually due to a branch mispredict.
Frontend Latency: Frontend didn’t deliver any micro-ops to the renamer that cycle
Frontend Bandwidth: The frontend delivered some micro-ops, but not enough to fill all renamer slots (eight on Lion Cove)
Core Bound: The backend couldn’t accept more micro-ops from the frontend, and the instruction blocking retirement isn’t a memory load
Backend Memory Bound: As above, but the instruction blocking retirement is a memory load. Intel only describes the event as “TOPDOWN.MEMORY_BOUND_SLOTS” (event 0xA4, unit mask 0x10), but AMD and others explicitly use the criteria of a memory load blocking retirement for their corresponding metrics. Intel likely does the same.
Retiring: The renamer slot was utilized and the corresponding micro-op was eventually retired (useful work)
Core width is poorly utilized, as implied by the IPC figures above. Backend memory latency accounts for a plurality of lost pipeline slots, though there’s room for improvement in instruction execution latency (core bound) and frontend latency as well. Bad speculation and frontend bandwidth are not major issues.
Backend Memory Access
Lion Cove has a 4-level data caching setup, with the L1 data cache split into two levels. I’ll be calling those L1 and L1.5 for simplicity, because the second level of the L1 lands between the first level and the 3 MB L2 cache in capacity and performance.
Lion Cove’s L1.5 catches a substantial portion of L1 misses, though its hitrate isn’t great in absolute terms. It gives off some RDNA 128 KB L1 vibes, in that it takes some load off the L2 but often has mediocre hitrates. L2 hitrate is 49.88%, 71.87%, and 50.98% in COD, Palworld, and Cyberpunk 2077 respectively. Cumulative hitrate for the L1.5 and L2 comes in at 75.54%, 85.05%, and 85.83% across the three games. Intel’s strategy of using a larger L2 to keep traffic off L3 works to a certain extent, because most L1 misses are serviced without leaving the core.
However, memory accesses that do go to L3 and DRAM are very expensive. Lion Cove can provide an idea of how often each level in the memory hierarchy limits performance. Specifically, performance monitoring events count cycles where no micro-ops were ready to execute, a load was pending from a specified cache level, and no loads missed that level of cache. For example, a cycle would be L3 bound if the core was waiting for data from L3, wasn’t also waiting for data from DRAM, and all pending instructions q

data.title: Lessons from creating my first text adventure
data.author: kqr
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了文字冒险游戏的制作难度以及作者的亲身经验。作者参加了ParserComp 2025比赛，提交了自己的文字冒险游戏《Lockout》。他指出，尽管与其他类型的游戏相比，文字冒险游戏制作相对简单，但实际仍然具有挑战性。作者前两次尝试因过于 ambitious 而失败，最终通过缩小游戏规模和专注细节完成了《Lockout》。文章还探讨了游戏的范围和细节平衡问题，分为广而简和窄而精两类。现代玩家更偏好细节丰富的游戏，而过于简略的游戏可能会让玩家感到沮丧。作者以《The Plot of the Phantom》为例，展示了广而简风格的游戏体验。总体而言，制作文字冒险游戏需要在广度和细节之间找到合适的平衡。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：文本冒险游戏的体验、技术问题及游戏设计改进建议

不同观点：

• [chrismorgan] 技术问题的反馈与解决方案：该评论者在玩游戏时遇到了技术问题，具体是由于自定义字体加载失败导致的网络错误。他们提出了两种解决方案，包括使用try-catch结构或追加.catch()方法。此外，评论者分享了一种通过用户样式表绕过问题的方法。

• [thrtythreeforty] 对Inform 7学习曲线的批评：该评论者表达了对Inform 7学习难度的不满，认为其语法不透明，学习曲线过高，尽管其外观看起来很有吸引力。

• [ianbicking] 对文本冒险游戏界面改进的建议：该评论者认为可以通过增加界面引导来改善玩家体验，例如通过加粗重要物品、标记出口目的地、使用颜色指示历史记录、简化物品管理和提供快速移动选项等方式来降低游戏的操作难度。

补充讨论：

• 游戏设计中的挑战：[ianbicking]指出游戏设计中存在一些挑战，如如何平衡界面引导与游戏谜题之间的关系，例如是否应将确定物品重要性作为谜题的一部分。

争议焦点：
• 文本冒险游戏的学习难度：[thrtythreeforty]认为Inform 7的学习曲线过高，而其他评论者未直接回应此问题，但[ianbicking]的建议部分回应了如何通过设计改进降低学习门槛。

44464536.article_content:
When I write about
the greatness of text adventures
, I pretend they are easy to
make. They are, compared to many other types of games, but it’s still a bit of a
lie. They’re hard to make.
I made one and submitted it to ParserComp 2025, and here’s what I learned.
My first text adventure: Lockout
Since ParserComp voting has opened, the game is now public, and
you can play it
in your browser
. The game itself reveals what it is about as you progress, so I
won’t write too much about it here. You should be able to finish it in 30–60
minutes. Don’t feel bad about needing hints, especially if you’re new to text
adventures.
Lockout
is my third attempt at making a text adventure. The first two failed
because of ambition.
Scope and richness of world modeling
It’s very easy to accidentally try to create too large a text adventure. My
first attempt was way too ambitious, and would have taken months to finish. I
still love the idea for that, but it had to go. I picked another idea that was
much smaller in scope, but it, too, grew too ambitious. I restarted one more
time, from an idea that was even more pared down, and I was actually able to
finish that game. With the minimalistic scope it took maybe fifteen hours of
active work to create most of the game, and then almost as much time again to
fix the 57 problems I received feedback on from beta testers.
1
1
This is a
large time investment for me, which makes it unlikely I’ll create another one
any time soon, even if I’d really like to.
Scope in text adventures is complicated, because there are two dimensions along
which scope can vary: breadth and detail.
A broad game might have many locations, items, and events, but each is
relatively sparsely implemented. Actions get generic responses, and items are
mainly generic scenery without interesting interactions. This is the style of
some of the earliest text adventures; they had to do it that way due to
technical limitations of the time.
A detailed game might have few locations, items, and events, but those that do
exist are modeled in high detail and interact realistically with each other.
Modern development tools afford insane levels of detail, and it’s up to the
author to set a reasonable limit to the detail included.
Lockout
is in the narrow-but-detailed category. Making a broad
and
detailed game takes a huge effort, so for the hobbyist it boils down to finding
the right tradeoff between breadth and detail.
For better or worse, the community encourages detailed games, and among modern
games, a text adventure that is broad and not detailed stands out as lacking in
implementation. A useful comparison to study this difference is
The Plot of the
Phantom
: a newly released game which was designed in the 1980’s, but
implemented using modern tools. It contrasts with
Lockout
in that it is mainly
in the broad-and-sparse camp, as the following interactions illustrate.
CAVE ENTRANCE
You stand at the base of a sandstone cliff, at the mouth of a large cave. Behind
you to the south, a misty Appalachian forest stretches in all directions. A
weathered sign made of pressure-treated lumber and painted in the style of
National Park signage stands to the right of the cave entrance.
The cave entrance is to the north.
Oh, wow, what sort of cave is this?
> look at cave
You can’t see any such thing.
Huh. Well, what can I find in the direction I came from?
> go south
You can’t go that way.
Why not? I suppose what remains is to enter the cave.
> enter cave
You can’t see any such thing.
Oh right, the cave doesn’t exist in the world, only in the description. Maybe I
have to go inside.
> go in
You can’t go that way.
I could have sworn … I guess I’ll go north to enter.
> go north
LARGE CAVERN
You step into a large open space, a cavern created by seeping
groundwater dissolving the sandstone over many decades. The sandy floor is
strewn with rocks and the damp ceiling hangs low, just a foot or two above your
head.
You’re not the first to find this place. Crumpled beer cans and cigarette butts
are everywhere, and the cold, blackend remains of a firepit sit in the cavern
center, and the eastern wall is blanketed with a remarkable amount of
multicolored graffiti.
To the north, a passage disapppears into the rock, while to the west you can see
a hole just barely wide enough to crawl through.
I’m worried about the safety of the ceiling. Can I get more information?
> look
at ceiling
You can’t see any such thing.
That’s odd. Let’s take some stuff we found here before we move on.
> get beer cans and cigarettes
That’s hardly portable.
This goes on for the rest of
The Plot of the Phantom
. There are a lot of things that appear to
exist, but when the player tries to examine them, they aren’t really there, or
they behave in unexpected ways.
Don’t get me wrong! I finished
The Plot of the Phantom
and I had a lot of fun
with it. You can make sparse games fun. However, this sort of sparsity does tend
to annoy modern players. One of the reasons is that when there are f

data.author: dshacker
data.article_summary:
文章讨论了微软与员工之间的“默契协议”如何发生变化。过去，微软以低于市场水平的薪酬雇用员工，但提供稳定性、合理的工作与生活平衡，尤其是几乎没有裁员。这种默契让员工能够计划他们的生活，依赖工作的稳定性。然而，近年来，微软裁员约30,000人，打破了这一长期传统。

文章指出，经济压力和保持竞争力的需求是原因之一，但微软在绩效管理上的问题也促使裁员变得比系统性解决个人表现问题更具吸引力。在过去，强制排名系统导致内部竞争和人才流失，而之后虽然取消了该系统，却出现了相反的问题：解雇表现不佳者变得极为困难。

此外，微软在绩效与薪酬之间的关联不够明显，表现优异者并未获得显著更高的报酬，导致“平庸通过”成为默认状态。文章总结，尽管微软有许多优秀的团队和管理人员，但这些系统性问题值得讨论和解决。

The broken Microsoft Pact: Layoffs and Performance Management
July 6, 2025 · 9 minute read
Categories:
career
leadership
Tags:
microsoft
career
layoffs
When you join Microsoft, you hear stories about people who’ve been there for
20 years
, who grew up with the company, who
never had to worry about sudden changes
(maybe except for 2008). The performance management system had its quirks, but there was an understanding that if you did solid work, you’d have a place.
But something shifted. Maybe it was the market, maybe it was the pressure to stay competitive with companies that move faster and pay more. The implicit agreement that made lower compensation feel acceptable started to
crack
.
For decades, Microsoft operated under an unspoken agreement with its employees—what I call
“the pact.”
The deal was simple: We’ll pay you 20-50% below market rate, but in exchange, you get stability, reasonable work-life balance, and most importantly,
no layoffs
. This wasn’t written in any employee handbook, but
everyone understood it
. It was the Microsoft way.
For many strong performing engineers, this was an attractive trade-off. You might not get rich as quickly as your friends at startups, but you could
plan your life around stability
. You could get a mortgage, start a family, and sleep well knowing your job
wasn’t going anywhere
.
According to layoffs.fyi, Microsoft has laid off around 30,000 people in the last two years. To put this in context: that’s roughly 13% of Microsoft’s workforce, and while the entire tech industry saw significant layoffs (Meta, Google, Amazon all made major cuts), Microsoft’s situation stands out because of their historical commitment to employment stability. Many people are confused about this departure from Microsoft’s traditional approach. As a former employee, I want to share my perspective on why this shift was almost
expected
. While economic factors certainly contributed, Microsoft’s performance management challenges made layoffs a more attractive option than addressing individual performance issues systematically.
Microsoft’s performance management has always been atrocious on both sides of the ruthlessness/leniency scale. In the Ballmer era, the forced stack ranking of employees. Essentially a system where managers had to grade their teams on a curve, with a predetermined percentage forced into “underperforming” categories regardless of actual performance, caused people to live in this fear environment. Even if you had a team of stellar performers,
someone had to be labeled as bottom 10%
. This led to internal competition, backstabbing, and people gaming the system by avoiding high-performing teams or sabotaging colleagues.
This caused great attrition and unfavorable business outcomes for Microsoft.  The system was so universally hated that when Satya Nadella became CEO in 2014, eliminating stack ranking was one of his first major moves. The opposite became true: it seems managers had to fight HR to get someone on their team out.
I personally saw the bad side of this. I had a co-worker who had
no productive outcomes for a year
, and it took
a year of continued documentation
to get him fired. This also caused a downstream effect on team morale, as he was still getting rewards and a salary similar to other people.
Great performance = mediocre pay?
Sadly, one of the tradeoffs you have to understand is that at the same level, over the same year, the difference in pay between someone at the highest level of performance versus someone who passably does their job
does not create enough differentiation
for most levels lower than principal, barring random exceptional one-off stock grants (which also don’t help retention, due to their randomness). This causes the system to not be a meritocracy, with
“passing by” being the default
.
Limitations and Context
I’ll acknowledge upfront that Microsoft is a massive, diverse company with thousands of managers and teams. My experiences reflect specific orgs, specific timeframes (2016-2022), and specific leadership chains. Your mileage may vary dramatically depending on your team, your manager, and your timing. I recognize that some teams and managers at Microsoft do provide strong performance differentiation, meaningful career growth, and excellent employee experiences.
However, these patterns were consistent enough across my tenure, conversations with colleagues from different orgs, and observations of broader company trends that I believe they represent systemic issues rather than isolated incidents. The goal isn’t to dismiss positive experiences but to highlight structural challenges that affect enough employees to warrant discussion.
At will employment
For me, coming from outside the US where employment contracts offer significantly more protection, at-will employment was a jarring concept. data.title: A New Postgres Block Storage Layout for Full Text Search
data.author: michaelmarkell
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了Postgres扩展pg_search将其存储从文件系统迁移到块存储的重大工程成就。pg_search是一个用于全文搜索和分析的Postgres扩展，这次迁移使其成为首个将外部文件格式移植到Postgres块存储的扩展。块存储是Postgres的存储API，支持WAL集成、崩溃恢复、MVCC以及缓存缓冲等功能。

迁移到块存储解决了多个技术挑战，如数据结构跨多块存储、索引空间管理以及并发读取等问题。块存储的优势包括减少磁盘I/O、提高读写吞吐量、简化WAL集成和物理文件管理。尽管面临Postgres单线程访问块存储的限制，但通过利用Postgres的并行工作机制，pg_search成功克服了这些挑战。

未来，团队将进一步讨论如何在更新频繁场景中保持MVCC安全，以及如何为分析工作负载定制块存储布局。

A New Postgres Block Storage Layout for Full Text Search
By Ming Ying on January 16, 2025
We recently completed one of our biggest engineering bets to date: migrating
pg_search
, a
Postgres extension for full text search and analytics, to Postgres' block storage system. In doing so,
pg_search
is the first-ever extension
1
to port an
external file format to Postgres block storage.
For context - block storage is Postgres’ storage API that backs all of Postgres’ tables and built-in index types. Prior to this migration,
pg_search
operated outside of block storage. This means that the extension created files which were not managed by Postgres and could read the contents of those files directly from disk.
While it’s not uncommon
2
for Postgres extensions to do this, block storage has enabled
pg_search
to simultaneously achieve:
Postgres write-ahead log (WAL) integration, which is necessary for physical replication of the index
Crash and point-in-time recovery
Full support for Postgres MVCC (multi-version concurrency control)
Integration with Postgres’ buffer cache, which has led to massive improvements in index creation times and write throughput
At first, we weren’t sure if reconciling the data access patterns and concurrency model of Postgres and
Tantivy
—
pg_search
's underlying search library — was possible without drastic changes to Tantivy
3
.
In this blog post, we’ll dive into how we architected
pg_search
's new block storage layout and data access patterns.
In the near future, we'll release two more posts: one to discuss how we designed and tested
pg_search
to be MVCC-safe in update-heavy scenarios, and another to dive into how we customized the block storage layout for analytical workloads (e.g. faceted search, aggregates).
What Is Block Storage?
The fundamental unit of block storage is a block: a chunk of 8192 bytes. When executing a query, Postgres reads blocks into buffers, which are stored in Postgres’ buffer cache.
DML (
INSERT
,
UPDATE
,
DELETE
,
COPY
) statements do not modify the physical block. Instead, their changes are written to the underlying buffers, which are later flushed to disk when evicted from the buffer cache or during a checkpoint.
If Postgres crashes, modifications to buffers that have not been flushed can become lost. To guard against this, any changes to the index must be written to the write-ahead log (WAL). During crash recovery, Postgres replays the WAL to restore the database to its most recent state.
What Is
pg_search
?
pg_search is a Postgres extension that implements a custom index for full text search and analytics. The extension is powered by Tantivy, a search library written in Rust and inspired by Lucene.
Why Migrate To Block Storage?
A custom Postgres index has two choices for persistence: use Postgres block storage or the filesystem. At first, using the filesystem may seem like the easier option. Integrating with block storage requires solving a series of problems:
Some data structures may not fit within a single 8KB block. Splitting data across multiple blocks can create lock contention, garbage collection, and concurrency challenges.
Once a block has been allocated to a Postgres index, it cannot be physically deleted — only recycled. This means that the size of an index strictly increases until a
VACUUM FULL
or
REINDEX
is run. The index must be careful to return blocks that have been tombstoned by deletes or vacuums to Postgres’ free space map for reuse.
In update-heavy scenarios, the index can become dominated by space that once belonged to dead (i.e. deleted) rows. This may increase the number of I/O operations required for searches and updates, which degrades performance. The index must find ways to reorganize and compact the index during vacuums.
Because Postgres is single-threaded, multiple threads cannot concurrently read from block storage
4
. The index may need to leverage Postgres’ parallel workers.
Once the index overcomes these hurdles, however, Postgres block storage does an incredible amount of heavy lifting. After a year of working with the filesystem, it became clear that block storage was the way forward.
Being able to use the buffer cache means a huge reduction in disk I/O and massive improvements to read and write throughput.
Postgres provides a simple, battle-tested API to write buffers to the WAL. Without block storage, extensions must define custom WAL record types and implement their own WAL replay logic, which drastically increases complexity and surface area for bugs.
Postgres handles the physical creation and cleanup of files for us. The index doesn’t need to clean up after aborted transactions or
DROP INDEX
statements.
Tantivy’s File-Based Index Layout
The first challenge was migrating
Tantivy’s
file-based index layout to block storage. Let’s quickly examine how Tantivy’s index is structured.

data.article_summary:
本文探讨了Python中`super()`函数在基础类中的不常见用法以及mixin的应用。通常，`super()`用于子类调用父类的初始化方法，尤其在多重继承时至关重要。有趣的是，在基础类中也调用`super()`可以支持协作式多重继承，确保方法解析顺序正确。文章通过`BaseEstimator`和`ServingMixin`的例子说明，如果在基础类中不使用`super()`，多重继承时可能导致父类初始化被跳过，属性丢失。修正方法是在基础类中调用`super()`，确保所有父类方法都被正确调用。

此外，文章介绍了mixin的使用场景，mixin是一种提供可选功能的多重继承形式，常用于如Scikit-learn等库中，以实现功能的复用和模块化。例如，通过mixin可以为类添加如接受头支持、用户代理、认证等功能。

不同观点：
• **关于`super()`的使用**：
  - [zahlman] 认为在设计框架时，应该默认调用`super()`，特别是在使用mixins或者希望他人继承你的类时。这有助于处理方法解析顺序（MRO）。

• **关于`__init__.py`的使用**：
  - [zahlman] 指出，创建空白的`__init__.py`文件已经成为标准，因为这在使用打包工具时很有帮助。但预先从`__init__.py`中导入可能导致额外的初始导入时间。

  - [zahlman] 提到，相对导入在有经验的开发者中是常见的做法，但不应预先从`__init__.py`中导入，以免增加不必要的导入时间。

争议焦点：
• **`super()`的MRO机制是否增加了不必要的复杂性**，尤其是在多重继承的场景中。

To learn how to build more maintainable and usable Python libraries, I’ve been reading some of the most widely used Python packages. Along the way, I learned some things about Python that are off the beaten path. Here are a few things I didn’t know before.
Using
super()
in base classes
Python’s
super()
lets us inherit base classes (aka super or parent classes) without having to explicitly refer to the base class. It’s usually used in the
__init__
method. While this might be simply a nice-to-have in single inheritance, multiple inheritance is almost impossible without
super()
.
However, one interesting use of
super()
is calling it in the
base
class. I find noticed this in requests’
BaseAdapter
.

When to use a Mixin
A mixin is a class that provides method implementations for reuse by multiple child classes. It is a limited form of multiple inheritance, and is a parent class that simply provides functionality for subclasses, does not contain state, and is not intended to be instantiated. Scikit-learn uses mixins liberally where they have
ClassifierMixin
,
TransformerMixin
,
OutlierMixin

from

AcceptMixin

Request
(
AcceptMixin
,
BaseRequest

pass

data.title: Show HN: Modernized file manager and program manager from Windows 3.x
data.author: electroly
data.article_summary: Heirloom apps项目提供了现代化的Windows经典应用程序，包括Heirloom File Manager和Heirloom Program Manager。File Manager是Windows File Manager的衍生版本，支持高DPI屏幕、回收站、书签、拖放操作以及创建和提取zip压缩文件。Program Manager则是经典Program Manager的重制版，用作启动快捷方式的Start菜单替代品。这些应用程序免费且开源，File Manager基于Microsoft Corporation的许可，而Program Manager则基于Brian Luft的许可。项目包含7个版本，最新版为2025年7月发布的12.1.0，主要使用C++编写。

不同观点：
• [timbit42] 认为Windows 3.x中最糟糕的是Program Manager和File Manager，并推荐使用IBM的Workplace Shell for Windows替代，该工具可以将PM和FM替换为类似于OS/2 Workplace Shell的外壳，且该工具是开源的，并提供了安装链接。

• [JdeBP] 从代码角度讨论了Windows 3.x相关项目的源代码，特别是对heirloom项目的提交进行了评价，指出该项目虽然部分现代化，但仍使用WTF-16而不是UTF-8。

44485286.article_summary: Heirloom apps项目提供了现代化的Windows经典应用程序，包括Heirloom File Manager和Heirloom Program Manager。File Manager是Windows File Manager的衍生版本，支持高DPI屏幕、回收站、书签、拖放操作以及创建和提取zip压缩文件。Program Manager则是经典Program Manager的重制版，用作启动快捷方式的Start菜单替代品。这些应用程序免费且开源，File Manager基于Microsoft Corporation的许可，而Program Manager则基于Brian Luft的许可。项目包含7个版本，最新版为2025年7月发布的12.1.0，主要使用C++编写。

data.title: Neanderthals operated prehistoric “fat factory” on German lakeshore
data.author: hilux
data.article_summary: 一项最新研究显示，12.5万年前的德国中部尼安德特人使用了一种先进的食品加工方法，通过水和热系统性地从大型动物骨骼中提取脂肪。这一发现出自在Neumark-Nord 2考古遗址，表明尼安德特人对营养、计划和资源管理有更先进的认识。研究表明，他们不仅砸碎骨头取髓，还将其粉碎并煮沸以获取富含营养的骨脂。这一行为显示出尼安德特人有组织、战略性地管理资源，并理解脂肪的营养价值。该遗址出土了至少172只大型哺乳动物的遗骸，表明这种骨脂生产活动规模巨大，推翻了此前认为只有晚期智人才能做到的看法。这一发现改变了我们对尼安德特人饮食和适应能力的理解。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：尼安德特人提取脂肪的技艺及其相关科学和历史背景

不同观点：
• **关于煮沸技术的可能性**：jbotz指出传统观点认为人类在陶器发明之前无法煮沸东西，但实际上可以通过动物皮或桦树皮等可燃材料进行煮沸，只要水位保持足够高。这种观点得到了实验验证的支持。
• **对煮沸技术的挑战和协作的看法**：freetime2认为虽然打碎骨头提取骨髓并不新奇，但在没有陶器的情况下煮沸骨头是一个挑战，可能需要大量的协作和计划。
• **历史和气候背景的讨论**：pbmonster提到在不同间冰期动物分布不同，如在柏林发现大量犀牛和大象遗骸，突显了环境对古人类活动的影响。
• **语言能力的争议**：Roark66质疑尼安德特人在没有语言能力的情况下如何进行复杂的合作活动，反驳了尼安德特人因缺乏复杂语言能力而被智人竞争淘汰的观点。
• **其他煮沸方法的介绍**：octaane补充了通过挖洞、加热石头或倒热水等方式煮沸提取脂肪的方法，提供了具体例子如美国原住民使用的方法。

补充讨论：
• **对发现的新闻报道的批评**：poulpy123认为关于尼安德特人理解脂肪营养价值的描述过于夸张，实际上这是进化驱动的觅食行为，与其他食肉动物类似。
• **尼安德特人作为人类的地位**：samuell强调尼安德特人是人类的一部分，引用了诺贝尔奖获得者Svante Pääbo的DNA测序研究。
• **对AI生成图像的关注**：qoez指出文章中的图片疑似为AI生成，并对细节进行了分析。
• **幽默和文化参考**：tpoindex提供了Gary Larson的漫画以幽默角度看待脂肪提取，FooBarBizBazz则开玩笑地将“脂肪工厂”比作制作汤。
• **个人口味反应**：meindnoch简单表达了对该话题的厌恶。

争议焦点：
• 尼安德特人是否具备复杂的语言能力以及这种能力对其社会活动的影响。
• 关于尼安德特人理解和利用脂肪营养价值的描述是否过于拟人化。

44460498.article_content:
Neanderthals in central Germany 125,000 years ago employed an advanced method of food preparation, according to a recent study: systematically stripping fat from the bones of large animals using water and heat. The practice, uncovered at the Neumark-Nord 2 archaeological site, shows that Neanderthals had a much more advanced conception of nutrition, planning, and resource management than previously believed.
Artistic impression of activities at the “Fat Factory” site. Credit: Scherjon, LEIZA-Monrepos
The research, published in Science Advances, was conducted by international researchers from MONREPOS (Leibniz Centre for Archaeology), Leiden University in the Netherlands, and the State Office for Heritage Management and Archaeology of Saxony-Anhalt. The study indicates that Neanderthals, in addition to smashing bones to access the marrow—a behavior shared by their earliest African ancestors—also crushed them into fragments and boiled them to obtain bone grease, a nutrient-rich resource.
“This was intensive, organized, and strategic,” said Dr. Lutz Kindler, the study’s lead author. “Neanderthals were clearly managing resources with caution—planning hunts, transporting carcasses, and rendering fat in a task-specific area. They understood both the nutritional value of fat and how to access it efficiently.”
Excavations at the Neumark-Nord 2 site. Credit: Wil Roebroeks, Leiden University
At least 172 large mammals, such as deer, horses, and aurochs, were butchered here. The production of bone grease, which required huge quantities of bone to be worthwhile, was previously considered to be something limited to Upper Paleolithic modern humans. This find pushes back the timeline by thousands of years and represents a fundamental shift in our knowledge of Neanderthal diet and adaptation.
From complete bones to tiny fragments. Credit: Kindler, LEIZA-Monrepos
The Neumark-Nord complex, discovered in the 1980s by archaeologist Dietrich Mania, is a full interglacial ecosystem. Excavations from 2004 to 2009 revealed several zones with various Neanderthal activities: deer hunting and light butchering in one, straight-tusked elephant processing in another, and fat removal in a third, specialized area. Remarkably, cut-marked remains of 76 rhinos and 40 elephants were also discovered at nearby sites like Taubach.

June 11, 2025
43,000-year-old Neanderthal fingerprint discovered on stone is the world’s oldest
May 30, 2025
“What makes Neumark-Nord so exceptional is the preservation of an entire landscape, not just a single site,” said Leiden University’s Prof. Wil Roebroeks. “We are seeing a range of Neanderthal behaviors within the same landscape.”
Massive bone processing. At the Neumark-Nord 2 site, near the margin of a shallow pool, there is a dense concentration of bones from more than 170 larger mammals (highlighted in blue), mixed with flint
artifacts
(red) and hammer stones (red). Credit: Kindler, LEIZA-Monrepos
The activities of the Neanderthals at Neumark-Nord not only demonstrate high sophistication but were also likely to have long-term environmental impacts. Prof. Roebroeks warned that their mass hunting of slow-reproducing species undoubtedly left a significant impact on fauna in the region during the Last Interglacial period.
The finds depict the Neanderthals as more capable and more intelligent than the stereotype of the brutish caveman. The “fat factory” at Neumark-Nord reveals a species that could plan for the future, manage its environment, and maximize nutrition in resource-poor environments.

LEIZA

data.title: Fictional K-pop bands zoom to top of US music charts
data.author: ranit
data.article_summary: Netflix动画电影《KPop Demon Hunters》大获成功，其虚构乐队的歌曲在美国音乐榜单上击败了BTS和Blackpink。电影中的男团Saja Boys的歌曲《Your Idol》登上美国Spotify榜首，女团Huntr/x的《Golden》则位居第二。这部电影由Sony Pictures Animation制作，讲述了女团Huntr/x秘密猎杀恶魔、保护粉丝的故事，而她们的对手Saja Boys则是由恶魔之王Gwi-ma派遣来窃取粉丝灵魂的。电影原声带进入了Billboard 200的前十，其中《Golden》将作为正式单曲发行并角逐奖项。这一成功得益于包括Teddy Park和Lindgren在内的顶尖制作团队。与此同时，BTS即将复出，Blackpink也将开始其首次全球巡演。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于2025年一部由K-pop歌曲作为原声的电影的成功及其背后的原因分析

不同观点：
• **sho_hn**：认为文章忽略了Twice成员参与演唱的因素，指出这些歌曲拥有固有观众群，并非凭空成功。他将此比作Mariah Carey为动画电影献唱，并批评BBC缺乏相关细节。
• **pjc50**：认为“虚拟乐队”这个说法有点标题党，实际上这是电影原声带，每隔几年就会有这样的电影进入排行榜。同时指出电影由于索尼和Netflix的大量资源支持，对西方观众很具吸引力。
• **modernerd**：对K-pop在2025年吸引了他感到意外，认为Demon Hunters在美国榜单上的成功是合理的。他赞赏电影的动画质量和原声带的优秀制作，指出歌曲旋律优美且充满个性，虽然有些俗气但鼓舞人心。
• **Copenjin**：认为K-pop是高度商业化的音乐类型，歌曲由专门的工作室制作，针对特定观众群。他觉得如果是由VTuber或完全计算机生成的歌曲登顶会更有趣。
• **voidUpdate**：指出虚拟乐队如Gorillaz早已存在并取得成功，K-pop在全球的流行也是不可避免的趋势，如K/DA的例子。

补充讨论：
• **sho_hn**：提到韩国近年来尝试过CG流行偶像和CG广告代言，尽管 vocals 仍由人类表演者提供，但通过AI生成语音模型进行活动和采访。
• **xhkkffbf**：认为虚拟乐队早就存在，如Archies或Sabrina and the Pussycats，虚拟乐队的再次流行只是旧事重演。
• **Neywiny**：提到他曾误以为一些长时间的音乐视频是由AI制作，感到失望，因为缺乏对训练材料的归属说明。不过，这次电影原声带的成功并非依赖AI。
• **ourmandave**：对讨论与Ticketmaster附加费问题无关表示不满。
• **specproc**：表示不喜欢这些K-pop歌曲自动出现在他的YouTube播放列表中。
• **mensetmanusman**：质疑是否所有乐队都是虚拟的。
• **SethMurphy**：引用This is Spinal Tap，暗示对乐队虚拟化的幽默看法。

争议焦点：
• 虚拟乐队的定义及其与传统乐队的区别。
• K-pop和虚拟乐队成功背后的原因，包括固有观众群和市场商业化因素。
• AI在音乐制作中的作用及归属问题。

总结：评论者对虚拟乐队、K-pop成功及AI在音乐中的角色各持不同观点，讨论涉及商业化、市场趋势及技术影响等多方面。

Fictional K-pop bands beat BTS and Blackpink in US charts
3 days ago

Netflix
KPop Demon Hunters is currently the most streamed movie on Netflix globally
A hugely popular K-pop musical animation has seen songs by its fictional bands top US music charts, beating real-life K-pop groups.
KPop Demon Hunters is currently the most streamed movie on Netflix globally, clocking up more than 33 million views in just two weeks.
On Friday the song Your Idol by a boy band in the film, Saja Boys, topped the US Spotify chart. This makes them the highest charting male K-pop group in US Spotify history - surpassing kings of K-pop BTS.
Golden, a track by the film's fictional girl group Huntr/x, hit number two on the chart, surpassing Blackpink as the highest-charting female K-pop group.
The film's soundtrack shot into the top 10 of the Billboard 200 in the US, making it the highest debut for a soundtrack so far this year.
Golden is being released as an official single by Republic Records, and Netflix is submitting it for awards consideration,
according to Variety.
KPop Demon Hunters follows the adventures of superstar band Huntr/x.
The three members of the all-female group - Rumi, Mira, and Zoey - are secretly "badass demon hunters" who protect their legions of fans from supernatural dangers.
During Huntr/x concerts, their music is used to protect the human world from the forces of darkness.
But rival band the Saja Boys, who are demons in disguise, are their arch enemies.
Jinu, Abby, Romance, Baby, and Mystery have been sent by demon king Gwi-ma to steal the souls of Huntr/x's fans.
KPop Demon Hunters, which was produced by Sony Pictures Animation, was directed by Maggie Kang and Chris Appelhans and was based on a story by Ms Kang.
Its success should perhaps not be too surprising as top producers including Teddy Park, who has worked with Blackpink, and BTS collaborator Lindgren were part of the team that created the album.
Netflix
The Saja Boys are demons sent by their king Gwi-ma to steal the souls of music fans
The popularity of KPop Demon Hunters comes as South Korean mega-stars
BTS are set to make their highly-anticipated comeback
.
The seven-strong group announced this week that it will head to the US this month to start working on new music.
The band is due to release a new album and go on tour next year after all of its members completed their mandatory military service.
Meanwhile, Blackpink is set to start its first all-stadium world tour on 5 July.
The band, which has not released an album together since 2022's Born Pink, is due to reveal a new song at the start of the Deadline World Tour.

44462770.article_summary: Netflix动画电影《KPop Demon Hunters》大获成功，其虚构乐队的歌曲在美国音乐榜单上击败了BTS和Blackpink。电影中的男团Saja Boys的歌曲《Your Idol》登上美国Spotify榜首，女团Huntr/x的《Golden》则位居第二。这部电影由Sony Pictures Animation制作，讲述了女团Huntr/x秘密猎杀恶魔、保护粉丝的故事，而她们的对手Saja Boys则是由恶魔之王Gwi-ma派遣来窃取粉丝灵魂的。电影原声带进入了Billboard 200的前十，其中《Golden》将作为正式单曲发行并角逐奖项。这一成功得益于包括Teddy Park和Lindgren在内的顶尖制作团队。与此同时，BTS即将复出，Blackpink也将开始其首次全球巡演。

data.title: The era of full stack chip designers
data.author: bharathw30
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：芯片设计的复杂性以及全栈芯片设计的可行性和挑战

不同观点：
• doitformango：认为全栈芯片设计涉及大量复杂步骤，包括RTL验证、模拟IP授权、合成、布局布线、功能验证等，通常需要大量人员和时间。重新设计现代ISA可能需要数十年的时间，单人难以完成。
• GianFabien：指出芯片制造的开发预算高达七至八位美元，且缺乏如软件开发那样丰富的资源供AI训练。芯片设计的自动化仍面临巨大挑战。
• plekter：认为RTL并非堆栈的顶端，上层还有游戏、游戏引擎、驱动程序、编译器、操作系统抽象等复杂部分。每个部分都有其复杂性，且上下层相互影响。
• jauntywundrkind：提到OpenROAD等开源项目，尽管初期有大量关注和 hype，但后续发展相对安静，希望有更多关于其演变的可见性。
• doix：指出全数字芯片设计中模拟部分被抽象掉，而在混合信号世界中，单人完成全栈设计曾经是节省成本的做法，但如今情况可能有所不同。
• MarkusWandel：认为自己属于"全栈"芯片设计师，经历过从原理图捕获到门级紧急修复，但现在Catapult C成为新的主流工具。
• nsteel：认为团队中几乎每个人都是"全栈"设计师，但对此标签并不认同，且担心全栈设计可能导致雇佣水平较低的员工。
• shitpostbot：指出芯片设计中RTL和物理设计之间的交接存在效率问题，双方缺乏对彼此工作的了解，导致性能和功耗上的损失。改善双方的沟通和协作可以带来更好的硬件设计。

补充讨论：
• leptons：对文章中关于"AI"的主题表示调侃，暗示对AI在芯片设计中的作用持怀疑态度。

争议焦点：
• 芯片设计中全栈设计的可行性和实际意义，特别是在现代复杂芯片设计中是否可能以及是否有必要。
• RTL设计和物理设计之间的协作效率问题，如何改善以提高整体设计质量。

data.title: François Chollet: The Arc Prize and How We Get to AGI [video]
data.author: sandslash
data.article_summary: 本文简要列出了与YouTube及其相关服务有关的一些重要信息和资源。内容包括关于YouTube的介绍、新闻发布、版权声明、联系方式、创作者信息、广告、开发者条款、隐私政策、安全指引、YouTube功能测试、NFL Sunday Ticket等服务，以及Google LLC的版权信息（© 2025）。文章提供了用户和创作者可能需要的关键链接和法律声明。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕ARC评估测试与AGI（人工通用智能）之间的关系，以及AGI定义和实现路径的讨论。

不同观点：
• **ARC测试是否能代表AGI能力：**
  - **qoez**: 认为ARC评估测试主要考察模式匹配能力，不能证明系统具备真正的AGI。类似于人类有多种智力类型，仅仅在智商测试中表现优异并不代表真正的聪明。
  - **bogtog**: 支持qoez的观点，指出模型在处理字符网格等任务时表现不佳，与人类通过直觉解决问题的能力形成对比。

• **AGI的定义：**
  - **lawlessone**: 提出AGI应具备持续感知和自我更新的能力，类似于生物大脑，而当前的LLM（大型语言模型）只在推理时短暂激活。
  - **visarga**: 认为 intelligence（智能）是搜索、探索和学习的结合，不是单独存在于模型或环境中，而是两者互动的结果。

• **AGI的实现路径：**
  - **TheAceOfHearts**: 提到Chollet讨论的连续学习能力对AGI的重要性，强调系统需要能够保存和应用经验教训。
  - **chromaton**: 强调当前AI系统在接受指令并根据世界状态生成新输出方面的不足，认为这方面的基准测试对AGI进展至关重要。

• **对AGI研究的社会影响和态度：**
  - **jacquesm**: 对AGI的社会影响持谨慎态度，认为当前世界面临多重危机，推迟AGI的实现可能对人类更有利。
  - **khalic**: 认为对AGI的追求可能会导致许多问题，暗示这种追求可能带来不良后果。

• **对Chollet个人转变的质疑：**
  - **hackinthebochs**: 质疑Chollet对AGI态度的转变，从曾经反对AGI概念到如今推动相关数据集，是否与资金投入增加有关。

补充讨论：
• **其他工具和基准测试的建议：**
  - **modeless**: 提到PuzzleScript游戏，建议可能可以用来创建AGI基准测试。

• **对讨论环境的关注：**
  - **ltbarcly3**: 提到讨论区存在大量的反对和标记行为，甚至一些有思考性的评论也被标记。

• **对内容可访问性的需求：**
  - **vixen99**: 询问是否提供文字版本以方便听力不便的用户。

争议焦点：
• 主要集中在ARC评估测试是否能有效衡量AGI能力，以及AGI的定义和实现路径上。部分评论者质疑当前AI模型是否具备真正的通用智能，并对AGI研究的社会影响表示担忧。

data.author: wglb
data.article_summary: 研究人员在路德维希-马克西米利安大学（LMU）与巴格达大学的合作中，重新发现了失传千年的《巴比伦赞歌》。该楔形文字泥板描述了巴比伦的辉煌和居民生活，提供了对巴比伦城市社会的新见解。赞歌由250行组成，赞颂了巴比伦的建筑、自然景象以及居民对外国人的尊重。尤为特别的是，它详细描述了自然现象，这在现存的 Mesopotamian 文学中十分罕见。通过人工智能平台，研究团队还识别出另外30份与该赞歌相关的抄本，揭示了该文本在当时的广泛传播。赞歌的部分内容描述了幼发拉底河及其对巴比伦的贡献。这一发现为理解巴比伦文化和历史提供了重要资料。

不同观点：
• octopoc：介绍《文明的陷落》播客中关于亚述的章节，提到美索不达米亚城市的多元信仰，每个城市有其专属神祇，城际战争被视为神祇间的竞争，类似于现代体育团队的竞争。

• yayitswei：对比古代巴比伦与中世纪欧洲的识读能力，指出巴比伦有制度化的儿童教育，而中世纪欧洲的识字率下降，识读成为专门技能，质疑现代所谓的指数增长。

• dr_dshiv：关注未翻译的楔形文字文本，指出其中大部分尚未被翻译，建议创建资源来追踪这些古典文本，并认为这些文本应成为人工智能训练的核心部分。

The GIST
Hymn to Babylon, missing for a millennium, has been discovered
by
Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich
edited by
Stephanie Baum
, 																								reviewed by
Robert Egan
Editors' notes
This article has been reviewed according to Science X's
editorial process
and
policies
.
Editors
have highlighted
the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility:
fact-checked
trusted source
proofread
The cuneiform tablet with the newly discovered hymn. Credit: Anmar A. Fadhil, Department of Archaeology, University of Baghdad, with the permission of the Iraqi Museum and the State Board of Antiquities and Heritage
In the course of a collaboration with the University of Baghdad, LMU's Enrique Jiménez has rediscovered a text that had been lost for a thousand years. A paper on this discovery is
published
in the journal
Iraq
.
"It's a fascinating hymn that describes Babylon in all its majesty and gives insights into the lives of its inhabitants, male and female," says Jiménez.
Babylon was founded in Mesopotamia around 2000 BCE. Once the largest city in the world, it was a cultural metropolis in which works were written that form part of our global literary heritage today.
Babylonian texts were composed in cuneiform writing on
clay tablets
, which have survived only in fragments. One of the goals of the collaboration with the University of Baghdad is to decipher hundreds of
cuneiform tablets
from the famous Sippar Library and preserve them for posterity. Legend has it that Noah hid them here from the floodwaters before boarding the ark.
In the Electronic Babylonian Library Platform, Enrique Jiménez is digitizing all cuneiform text fragments that have been discovered worldwide to date and using
artificial intelligence
to decipher fragments that belong together.
"Using our AI-supported platform, we managed to identify 30 other manuscripts that belong to the rediscovered hymn—a process that would formerly have taken decades," says Jiménez, Professor of Ancient Near Eastern Literatures at LMU's Institute of Assyriology. Thanks to these additional texts, the scholars were able to completely decipher the hymn of praise on the clay tablet, parts of which were missing.
Hymn offers new insights into Babylonian urban society
These numerous additional copies suggest that the text was very widespread at the time.
"The hymn was copied by children at school. It's unusual that such a popular text in its day was unknown to us before now," says Jiménez.
The paean presumably comes from the start of the first millennium before Christ and comprises 250 lines.
"It was written by a Babylonian who wanted to praise his city. The author describes the buildings in the city, but also how the waters of the Euphrates bring the spring and green the fields. This is all the more spectacular as surviving Mesopotamian literature is sparing in its descriptions of natural phenomena," observes Jiménez.
The information about the women of Babylon, their role as priestesses and the associated tasks, has also astonished experts, as no texts describing these things were previously known. In addition, the hymns provide insights into coexistence in urban society. For example, the inhabitants are described as being respectful to foreigners.
The ruins of the ancient city of Babylon are located some 85 kilometers south of the Iraqi capital of Baghdad. They are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Excerpt from the newly discovered hymn
The following lines are from the newly discovered hymn. They describe the river Euphrates, on whose shore Babylon lay at that time:
The Euphrates is her river—established by wise lord Nudimmud—
It quenches the lea, saturates the canebrake,
Disgorges its waters into lagoon and sea,
Its fields burgeon with herbs and flowers,
Its meadows, in brilliant bloom, sprout barley,
From which, gathered, sheaves are stacked,
Herds and flocks lie on verdant pastures,
Wealth and splendor—what befit mankind—
Are bestowed, multiplied, and regally granted.
More information:
Anmar A. Fadhil et al, Literary Texts From The Sippar Library V: A Hymn In Praise Of Babylon And The Babylonians,
Iraq
(2025).
DOI: 10.1017/irq.2024.23

Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich

data.title: The Cat's Meat Man: Feeding Felines in Victorian London
data.author: ohjeez
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了维多利亚时期伦敦的“猫食贩”（cat’s meat man），他们靠贩卖便宜的内脏和马肉为城市里的猫提供食物。随着猫从捕鼠动物转变为家庭宠物，猫食贩应运而生。他们推着车在街道上叫卖，顾客包括普通家庭和流浪猫。亨利·梅修（Henry Mayhew）的《伦敦劳工与伦敦穷人》记录了这一群体，指出当时伦敦有上千名这样的贩子，服务约30万只猫。尽管工作辛苦，一些猫食贩通过努力可以获得稳定收入，甚至有人担任主日学校教师。此外，文章还提到猫食贩与“开膛手杰克”受害者及名人路易斯·韦恩（Louis Wain）的关系。这一职业在19世纪末逐渐女性化，一些寡妇使用旧婴儿车贩卖猫食。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：历史职业的消失及其背景，特别是与动物相关的职业以及历史上伦敦底层劳动者的生活。

不同观点：
• vintagedave：提到《杜利特医生的故事》中的"猫肉贩子"角色，并指出一些职业在二战前后消失的现象，例如伦敦的荷兰鳗鱼贩子。
• ggm：推荐Henry Mayhew的书，详细描述了19世纪伦敦底层劳动者的生活，包括食物贩卖和特殊行业，如“纯”狗粪用于皮革鞣制，并指出这些记录可能影响了后来的社会政策。
• dctoedt：对"猫肉贩子"这一名称产生歧义理解，幽默地猜测其销售的是“猫肉”。
• ashoeafoot：联想到作家Terry Pratchett，暗示该评论内容与Pratchett作品风格或主题的关联。
• JamesAdir：对vintagedave分享的内容表示感谢，并称赞其为“瑰宝”。
• enraged_camel：转向推荐关于伊斯坦布尔流浪猫的纪录片《Kedi》，与主题相关但更侧重现代社会中人与猫的关系。
• SideburnsOfDoom：补充历史背景，指出在20世纪中期之前，宠物绝育并不普遍，可能导致流浪动物问题。

补充讨论：
• 评论中对历史上特定职业消失的原因及其社会影响进行了探讨，尤其是vintagedave和ggm提供的背景信息。

The Cat’s Meat Man
Feeding Felines in Victorian London
By
Kathryn Hughes
As cats evolved from feral ratters into beloved Victorian companions, a nascent pet-food economy arose on the carts of so-called “cat’s meat men”. Kathryn Hughes explores the life and times of these itinerant offal vendors, their intersection with a victim of Jack the Ripper, and a feast held in the meat men’s honor, chaired by none other than Louis Wain.
Published
February 12, 2025
Scroll through the whole page to download all images before printing.
Photograph by Francis James Mortimer of an itinerant vendor of meat for cats and dogs, ca. 1900 —
Source
.
On January 10, 1901, twelve days before Queen Victoria did the unthinkable and died, 250 cat’s meat men sat down to a slap-up dinner at a restaurant in Holborn, on the edge of central London. A cat’s meat man was an itinerant vendor who pushed a cart of cheap offal and horsemeat around residential streets while calling out something that sounded like “
CA-DOE-MEE!
” Sometimes he stopped at a house and delivered a pre-ordered package of meat, often threaded onto a long skewer. At the same time, his shout was the signal for householders and domestics to come out onto the pavement and buy their pets’ food straight from the barrow. For all that cats were supposed to cater for themselves by catching kitchen pests, urban owners increasingly found the money from the household budget to supplement their board.
Within minutes of the cat’s meat man embarking on his circuit, the barrow would be surrounded by felines, some of whom had perfectly good homes to go to and others who did not but still hoped that a sliver of flesh might fall their way. Although there were plenty of grim jokes circulating about how cat’s meat men supplied the toughest meat they could get away with, the fact was that many of these rough diamonds were known for their tender hearts. It was not unusual to spot a cat’s meat man slipping scraps to the hopeful strays that wound around his ankles. He was their guardian, their special friend. Sometimes he could even bring about fairy-tale transformations: no less a lady than the Duchess of Bedford had recently adopted a stray that had been rescued by her local London cat’s meat man.
During the middle years of Victoria’s reign, the cat’s meat man, in his livery of blue apron, shiny black hat, and corduroy trousers, had become a gift to investigative journalists of an anthropological turn. In his
London Labour and the London Poor
(1851), Henry Mayhew plunges deep into their visible yet still mysterious world. According to Mayhew, there were a thousand such traders in London, serving about 300,000 cats, one for every house (allowing for multiple cats in some homes, plus strays). This sounds lucrative, but when Mayhew pumps his informants for details, he finds a story of dogged hard work. One carrier told him that he seldom went less than thirty, and frequently forty miles, through the streets every day.

The best districts were among the houses of tradesmen, mechanics, and labourers. The coachmen in the mews at the back of the squares were particularly good customers. “‘The work lays thicker there’, said my informant. ‘Old maids are bad, though very plentiful, customers. They cheapen the carriers down so, that they can scarcely live at the business. They will pay one halfpenny and owe another, and forget that after a day or two.’” Cat ladies, as ever, were to blame for imperilling capitalism and the men who served it.
Over the next two decades, as magazines increasingly included articles about cat’s meat men, further details emerged. While mostly respectable, they were well down the pecking order. Some were “born into the trade” but others went into it at the scrag end of their working lives. Two common scenarios were butchers who had failed in business and lost their shop, or carriage painters whose health had been broken by the noxious paints they had been inhaling for decades. By the end of the century, it was not unusual to see women, often widows, in charge of a round. Some used old prams from which to sell their wares.
Those cat’s meat men who could keep away from the pub had a decent chance of building up a nice little surplus that allowed them to lead stable lives. Some were even Sunday School teachers. data.title: Deno 2.4
data.author: hackandthink
data.article_summary: Deno 2.4 恢复了 `deno bundle` 命令，用于创建单文件 JavaScript 捆绑包，支持服务器和浏览器平台，兼容 npm 和 JSR 依赖，并通过 esbuild 实现自动树摇和压缩。此外，新增 `--unstable-raw-imports` 标志，允许直接导入文本和二进制文件，简化非 JavaScript 文件的处理。同时，捆绑功能也支持与 `deno compile` 结合使用，可将资源嵌入最终编译的二进制文件中。其他更新包括内置 OpenTelemetry 稳定化、使用 `--preload` 修改环境、更简单的依赖管理等。`deno bundle` 目前为实验性功能，未来计划增加运行时 API 和插件支持。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Deno 的使用体验、兼容性、技术实现、安全性以及在生产环境中的应用挑战

不同观点：
• [outlore] 赞赏 Deno 的设计理念，如 Deno.json、JSR、现代导入方式和 Deno Deploy，但在使用 Next.js 时遇到问题，部分功能（如类型）偶尔出现细微错误。相比之下，Bun 虽然不如 Deno “干净”，但使用起来更简单直接，不过 Bun 也存在如无法在 Vercel 上运行等问题。

• [voat] 强调 Deno 的 Node 兼容性，认为 `compat` 环境变量会促进 Deno 的采用，并建议创建类似 `denon` 的命令来简化兼容模式的使用。

• [aseipp] 欣赏 Deno 在脚本粘合代码中的表现，特别是在 gRPC 支持推出后会更具吸引力，但对于机器学习等特定领域仍会选择 Python。

• [blinkingled] 指出 Deno 在 FreeBSD 上仍然不可用，因为 Rust V8 绑定尚未移植到该平台。

• [impulser_] 对 Deno 选择 esbuild 而非即将推出 v1 版本的 Rust 基础工具 Rolldown 感到意外。

• [eranation] 认为 Deno 在生产环境中未广泛使用的原因是缺乏标准化的漏洞数据库，且由于没有集中式包管理器，使得管理依赖变得更加复杂。

• [mcraiha] 对 `bundle` 子命令的回归表示欢迎，认为这省去了使用变通方法的麻烦。

• [duesabati] 高度评价 Deno，认为它是 Node 应有的样子，但担心 Deno 在面对竞争时会为了追逐短期热度而失去耐心，做出一些不理智的决策。

• [deafpolygon] 表示一直听到对 Deno 的积极评价，可能会因此开始尝试使用 JavaScript。

• [bflesch] 对 Deno 的安全性表示关注，特别指出 `curl mywebsite.com/foo.sh | sh` 这种安装方式存在较大的供应链攻击风险，认为这种做法过于追求便利而忽视了安全性，建议使用如 `npm install -g deno` 这样更安全的安装方式。

补充讨论：
• Deno 的安装和使用过程中，安全性成为一个值得关注的问题，特别是在处理外部脚本时。
• 讨论中涉及到 Deno 与 Node 的兼容性问题，以及如何通过工具和命令简化这种兼容性转换。
• 技术实现上，对 Deno 选择的打包工具（esbuild 而非 Rolldown）存在争议，部分用户对 Deno 在特定平台（如 FreeBSD）的支持表示担忧。
• 生产环境中 Deno 的应用受限于漏洞数据库和包管理器的不足，这对大规模采用构成一定挑战。

deno bundle

supports both server-side and browser platforms, works with npm and JSR
dependencies, and includes automatic tree shaking and minification via esbuild.

--minify

--platform
browser

--platform
browser

bundle.js

=
external app.jsx
Bundling JavaScript with React for the client.

deno bundle
, which
was
subsequently deprecated
.

could build

uses
esbuild

44488107.article_summary: Deno 2.4 恢复了 `deno bundle` 命令，用于创建单文件 JavaScript 捆绑包，支持服务器和浏览器平台，兼容 npm 和 JSR 依赖，并通过 esbuild 实现自动树摇和压缩。此外，新增 `--unstable-raw-imports` 标志，允许直接导入文本和二进制文件，简化非 JavaScript 文件的处理。同时，捆绑功能也支持与 `deno compile` 结合使用，可将资源嵌入最终编译的二进制文件中。其他更新包括内置 OpenTelemetry 稳定化、使用 `--preload` 修改环境、更简单的依赖管理等。`deno bundle` 目前为实验性功能，未来计划增加运行时 API 和插件支持。

主要讨论点：Morph工具的开发者体验（dev UX）、速度与质量的权衡、隐私问题以及与其他类似工具的比较。

不同观点：
• 关于速度与质量的优先级：
  - [deepdarkforest] 认为质量比速度更重要，尤其是在代码生成质量方面。即使编辑速度有200-300ms的差异，也不会成为开发者体验的瓶颈。
  - [elzbardico] 则以讽刺的口吻表示，开发者可能不得不面对大量AI生成的有问题的代码，暗示速度和质量同样重要。

• 功能性与使用场景：
  - [scottpersinger] 建议开发一个能智能合并代码的AI工具，认为这将显著提升开发速度。
  - [nico] 提出希望有一个浏览器扩展，可以连接ChatGPT和VSCode，从而实现代理编码。

• 工具性质与技术细节：
  - [Workaccount2] 询问Morph是否为整合其他LLM输出的工具，而不是一个LLM本身。
  - [simonw] 分享了使用Morph与Datasette工具集成的技术细节，但也提出了关于XML样式标签可能引起混淆的担忧。

• 隐私与数据使用：
  - [laborcontract] 对隐私政策表示关注，特别是付费用户的数据保留和使用问题，并询问是否可以选择不让数据用于模型训练。

• 与其他工具的比较：
  - [bijection] 询问Morph与Relace的比较，指出两者功能相似。
  - [seanw265] 询问Morph与其他模型（如Relace和Llama via Cerebras）在输出准确性上的比较。
  - [lastdong] 询问Morph是否类似于Gemini Diffusion。

补充讨论：
• [amelius] 建议可以让LLM直接输出patch文件，以简化代码更新流程。
• [handfuloflight] 询问如何将Morph引入Claude Code。
• [callamdelaney] 简单表示对该工具的需求。
• [rs186] 认为大公司可能很快会推出类似功能，并对Morph的API部分表示困惑，质疑开发者是否愿意将代码发送到另一个端点。

争议焦点：
• 速度与质量的优先级问题：一部分人认为质量更重要，而另一部分人则关注速度对开发体验的影响。
• 隐私问题：用户对数据使用和隐私政策的关注，特别是付费用户的数据处理方式。

这些观点反映了用户对Morph工具的功能、性能和隐私问题的多方面考虑，以及与其他类似工具的比较和竞争情况。

data.title: Solving Wordle with uv's dependency resolver
data.author: mildbyte
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一种利用Python的依赖解析工具`uv`来解决Wordle（单词猜谜游戏）的创新方法。作者之前曾用Poetry的依赖解析器解决过数独问题，而现在利用`uv`工具尝试解决Wordle。文章详细分析了Wordle的规则和反馈机制，将其转化为Python包的依赖关系问题。通过将每个可能的单词表示为一个包，每个字母位置表示为具有多个版本的包，并根据Wordle的反馈（绿色、黄色）设置依赖约束，作者设计了一个能够自动猜测正确单词的系统。文章还提供了具体的实现步骤和代码示例，最终可以在GitHub上获取该解决工具并运行。这种方法展示了利用软件工具解决非传统编程问题的创造性思路。

Solving Wordle with uv's dependency resolver
7th Jul 2025
•
12 min read
•
Tags:
programming
,
tech
,
why
,
disgusting hacks
Table of Contents
Introduction
Background: Sudoku and Python dependency resolution
What is Wordle
Analysis
Basic building blocks
Greens and yellows
Python dependency rules?
Possible position packages
Feedback packages
Putting this all together: the cursed neural network
Implementation
Package examples
--find-links and wheels
Harness
Bonus round: more efficient guessing
Blooper reel
GitHub
Introduction
In a previous life, I wrote a
Sudoku solver that relied on Poetry's dependency resolver
. We ended up selling that startup to EDB (not because of the Poetry hack), which means that they now own this IP. And, since then, Python packaging has advanced, with
uv
taking the world by storm.
This means that it's time for a refresh. Can we use
uv
instead of Poetry? And can we solve a Wordle instead of a Sudoku?
For the impatient: you can get the solver from
my GitHub
. Run
uv run main.py run
and watch it go.
Background: Sudoku and Python dependency resolution
The short summary of the Sudoku + Poetry post is that unlike Rust or JavaScript, a single Python project cannot use more than one version of a specific Python package. This means that we can easily represent a Sudoku grid as 81 Python packages, each with 9 possible versions. If a certain cell has a specific number (version), cells in the same row, column and a 3x3 square it belongs to cannot have that same number.
We can encode these rules as version constraints on other packages representing our cell's neighbours.
Once we have our 81 packages, all that remains is encoding our problem by making another package, specifying the precise versions of the cells where we already have numbers, leaving the rest as wildcards, and then letting Poetry generate a lockfile that will assign each number (version) to every cell (package), thus solving the puzzle.
What is Wordle
This
is Wordle.
You have six attempts to guess a five-letter word. On each guess, you get what I'll be calling "feedback": each letter in your guess becomes green (correct letter in the correct position), yellow (correct letter, wrong position) or nothing (wrong letter).
In this post, I'll represent it as a string
YGG..
, meaning that the feedback we got for our answer is:
Yellow at position 1
Green at positions 2 and 3
Blank or "dot" at positions 4 and 5
Analysis
It is said that if you ask an LLM to think really hard about its answer and write down its thinking before giving the final response, then it can successfully count the number of r's in the word
strawberrry
and help you sell more inference tokens.
Let's do exactly that and break this down.
Basic building blocks
Let's start simple. The solution to a Wordle is a five-letter word, and we'd like our system to choose one possible word given all information that we feed into it. We can encode this as a single Python package with multiple possible versions, where each version represents a single word. This is a useful building block.
The other building block is that each position can only have one letter in it. We can easily represent this as five "position" packages, each of which can have 26 versions. If the position package 1 has version 2, that means "B" is in that position.
We can then draw dependencies between a specific version of our "word" package to specific versions of our "position" packages. If our word is
STALL
, then it'll depend on:
position package 1, version 19 (S)
position package 2, version 20 (T)
position package 3, version 1 (A)
position packages 4 and 5, version 12 (L)
Greens and yellows
However, this is not enough. We need to encode some more complex facts about the solution in Wordle than we did with Sudoku. For example, let's assume that we guessed
CHILD
and the feedback we got is
..YG.
. This means:
The fourth letter is L
The third letter is not I
But there is at least one I somewhere in the word
None of the letters are C, H or D
Is this correct though? There is a bit of nuance here.
Let's try again, this time with a different guess but the same word. We try
ATOLL
(it's not an optimal play, but as a demonstration) and get
...GY
. Here, we can't just say that there is an L somewhere in the word (because there already is). We have to say that there is at least one L in the first, second or third position.
Now let's say we guess
LILLE
and get
.GGG.
. What does this mean? Just because L in the first position gave us a dot doesn't mean there are no Ls in the word at all (there clearly are). Instead, we need to say that the first and the fifth position don't contain an L.
One thing that stems from this is that the feedback we get for a specific letter in a specific position will change based on other letters in our guess. For example, let's say the real world is
BUNNY
. If we guess
NNNON
, we'll get
YYG.Y
. And if we then guess
NNNNN
, we'll get
..GG.
. Because we discovered all Ns in the word, the first, secon
44476382.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一种利用Python的依赖解析工具`uv`来解决Wordle（单词猜谜游戏）的创新方法。作者之前曾用Poetry的依赖解析器解决过数独问题，而现在利用`uv`工具尝试解决Wordle。文章详细分析了Wordle的规则和反馈机制，将其转化为Python包的依赖关系问题。通过将每个可能的单词表示为一个包，每个字母位置表示为具有多个版本的包，并根据Wordle的反馈（绿色、黄色）设置依赖约束，作者设计了一个能够自动猜测正确单词的系统。文章还提供了具体的实现步骤和代码示例，最终可以在GitHub上获取该解决工具并运行。这种方法展示了利用软件工具解决非传统编程问题的创造性思路。

data.title: I used o3 to profile myself from my saved Pocket links
data.author: noperator
data.article_summary: 文章主要描述了Pocket应用即将关闭，作者在迁移保存的近900篇文章时，对这些数据进行了分析。通过使用工具xsv，作者提取并检查了文章的标题、网址、添加时间、标签和状态等信息。作者还尝试利用这些保存的网址，通过AI助手o3进行个人画像分析。o3根据文章内容推断作者可能为30-40岁的男性，居住在美国弗吉尼亚州沿海地区，拥有计算机科学学位，担任高级软件工程师，年收入约15万美元，已婚并有多个年幼的孩子。此外，o3还推断出作者的政治倾向、风险承受能力和学习风格等特征。文章最后总结了作者的核心人口统计信息和生活模式。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：使用AI分析个人数据（如Pocket存档、浏览历史、聊天记录等）以构建个人兴趣和行为档案的可行性、挑战和潜在应用。

不同观点：
• **elcapitan**：对Pocket存档的分析显示99%的文章是"未读"的，质疑是否能从中推断出除囤积链接外的其他个人特质。
• **saeedesmaili**：尝试使用不同AI模型分析Pocket数据，发现Opus 4在预测个人信息方面表现最好，但所有模型在职业角色预测上都不准确，因为个人兴趣和职业需求不一致。
• **jackdawed**：认为利用AI分析个人数据是一个有潜力的实验，可以构建用户行为图谱，但面临上下文窗口大小和数据源整合的挑战。提出未来可能出现基于个人数据的内容推荐系统，优化用户效用而非广告收入。
• **fudged71**：关注RSS feeds和ChatGPT/Gemini/Claude聊天历史的元分析，计划开发一个动态更新的"世界模型"以过滤和排序个人信息。
• **nsypteras**：曾编写脚本分析HN用户的评论历史以推断个人信息，如位置、政治倾向、职业等，认为这是一个有趣的实验。
• **asveikau**：对基于宗教信仰推断政治倾向的结果表示惊讶，特别是对美国东北部天主教徒的普遍政治倾向提出看法。
• **Alifatisk**：开发了一个分析groupchat的工具，利用本地LLM对聊天内容进行用户画像，认为有改进空间。
• **frou_dh**：建议使用AI/NLP对"稍后阅读"列表进行分类，以方便删除不再感兴趣的内容。
• **rhcom2**：使用Claude对Pocket导出的链接进行标记，效果良好。
• **cainxinth**：利用LLM分析评论历史以识别潜在的网络"钓鱼 troll"，认为LLM能提供快速总结，但最终判断仍需人工。
• **animesh**：基于与AI的聊天记录进行自我分析，认为系统提示旨在让用户感觉良好，但结果有时过时或不准确。
• **hubraumhugo**：创建了一个分析HN账户的工具，认为结果有趣且偶尔吓人。

补充讨论：
• **数据整合与隐私**：讨论中涉及多源数据（如Pocket存档、YouTube观看历史、聊天记录）的整合问题，同时关注用户隐私和计算挑战。
• **AI模型的局限性**：多个评论指出当前AI模型在职业角色预测和个人兴趣推断方面的局限性，特别是当个人行为和职业需求不一致时。
• **未来应用潜力**：提出未来可能出现基于个人数据的内容推荐或行为分析系统，强调这些系统应优化用户效用而非商业利益。

争议焦点：
• **AI分析结果的准确性和实用性**：不同用户对AI分析结果的准确性和实用性存在不同看法，尤其是对职业角色和个人兴趣的预测。

Experiment
#
Recalling Simon Willison’s recent
geoguessing challenge
for o3, I considered, “What might o3 be able to tell me about myself, simply based on a list of URLs I’ve chosen to save?” I opened a temporary chat with o3 (doesn’t use ChatGPT’s memory feature) and prompted:
I’m going to share a list of articles that I’ve saved to Pocket, a read-it-later app. I want you to use that information to “profile” me. Tell me everything about myself that you can possibly infer from this data set. Here’s an example of possible dimensions of that profile, but feel free to include other things that you can infer: age, sex, geographic location, education level, industry/field of work, job level/seniority, income bracket, political orientation, risk tolerance, learning style, information diet, relationship status, parental status and kids’ ages, health concerns, major life transitions, seasonal patterns in interests, etc.

It makes sense to assume they might be male, based on the profiles aggregating to this, but I’m not completely sure yet. I’ll keep this in mind!

They seem to have a self-directed learning style and a moderate to high risk tolerance in investments. They’re likely married with multiple young kids.

• **AI模型的局限性**：多个评论指出当前AI模型在职业角色预测和个人兴趣推断方面的局限性，特别是当个人行为和职业需求不一致时。
• **未来应用潜力**：提出未来可能出现基于个人数据的内容推荐或行为分析系统，强调这些系统应优化用户效用而非商业利益。

争议焦点：
• **AI分析结果的准确性和实用性**：不同用户对AI分析结果的准确性和实用性存在不同看法，尤其是对职业角色和个人兴趣的预测。

data.title: When Figma starts designing us
data.author: bravomartin
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了Figma这一设计工具对设计领域的影响，特别是其推动设计向工程化工作方式靠拢的趋势。作者回忆了2013年首次接触Figma的经历，并反思了Figma的一些功能，如智能组件、变量、自动布局和交互原型等，认为这些功能虽然提升了与工程的一致性，但也限制了设计的创造性和可能性。例如，自动布局功能虽然便于结构化设计，但也限制了设计师自由尝试不同的布局和组合。此外，开发者模式虽然旨在连接设计和工程实现，但可能导致过度打磨设计而忽视在代码中快速迭代的重要性。作者担心这种过早优化和结构化的设计方式会导致设计空间的缩小和创意的限制，呼吁设计师警惕这种转变，保持设计的灵活性和探索性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Figma作为设计工具的适用性和其对设计工作流程的影响

不同观点：
• miiiiiike认为Figma在实现设计系统方面不够强大，特别是在处理多断点、容器查询、模式和变体时表现不佳。他指出Figma的变量管理功能存在问题，且容易遇到性能问题。他认为Figma过于注重设计师的需求，而忽略了工程师的实际需求，最终选择在代码中实现设计系统。

• Lalabadie支持miiiiiike的观点，认为Figma过度关注实施阶段，而忽视了早期探索和研究阶段的需求。他怀念Photoshop的探索性工作流程，认为Figma在初期设计阶段存在冲突。

• bbx则对Figma和Auto Layout功能持积极态度，认为它们解决了设计中重复性和布局问题，提供了更高的效率和灵活性。
• drewbeck认为工具对工作流程有影响，但组织和领导层才是决定工作流程的关键因素。他指出Figma提供了自由选择的功能，而非强制使用某些特性。
• asoneth指出设计和开发中存在探索性设计和已确立模式的区别，认为Figma适用于大多数企业和消费者产品设计，而探索性设计需要更广泛的工具和技能。
• zelphirkalt批评设计师对HTML和CSS等基础知识的缺乏，认为这导致了许多糟糕的网站设计，并期望设计师具备更新的前端知识。
• jjcm作为Figma的设计系统PM，部分认同miiiiiike的观点，但强调Figma旨在提供自由和结构化设计之间的平衡，并指出Figma的功能是可选的，而非强制性的。

补充讨论：

• ranie93将讨论引向Jira和组织目标的票务化，指出其负面影响。
• dmix指出设计师对网页设计理解不足是问题的根源，强调拥有实际网站制作经验的设计师的重要性。

• Figma是否过度关注实施阶段而忽视早期探索阶段。
• Figma的功能是否对设计过程产生了过多的限制，还是提供了更多的效率和灵活性。
• 设计师是否需要更深入的前端知识以更好地进行设计工作。

44479502.article_content:
I first encountered Figma in 2013, when Dylan Field demoed an early prototype
to me at O’Reilly’s Foo Camp. I remember the pen tool feeling surprisingly
elegant, but I missed the bigger picture: the radical implications of a design
tool that ran in the browser. A decade later, Figma is a core part of our
creative process, and without it, we wouldn't have been able to build a fully
remote design practice. That’s probably why Dylan is a near-billionaire and
I’m not.
However, over the course of the last five years, I’ve grown increasingly
worried about what Figma is doing to the field of design by pushing designers
toward an engineering-centric way of working. This can be seen in their
feature releases: Smart Components, Variables, Auto Layout, and Interactive
Prototypes. These features are often celebrated as steps toward parity with
engineering, but in practice, they encourage a mode of working that narrows
the field of possibility at precisely the moment when it should be expanding.
A concrete example is Auto Layout. It may seem harmless at first to introduce
a DOM-like layout mechanism in a design tool, and it certainly has advantages
in mature design files where the structure rarely changes. But many design
teams today use Auto Layout to create full page designs of their digital
products from the get-go. In practice, this locks the design in place and
severely limits the possible expressions. You can’t drag things around freely
or try odd combinations of layouts. You can’t simply paste something into a
frame without it snapping to the bottom of the stack. The result is that
designers are nudged into thinking like engineers during the earliest stages
of exploration just when they should be working messily, freely, and loosely.
It might feel convenient at first, but it comes at a cost. Have you ever
opened a Figma file and tried to make a small change, only to find yourself
wrestling with the layout? I’ve encountered this more often than I’d like, and
it seems to be increasing in frequency.
Another feature is Dev Mode, which, in theory, is the missing bridge between
the design specification and the technical implementation. However, it
enforces a mindset where designers polish designs far away from the technology
they are designing for, and where enormous amounts of time are spent on
building complex prototypes, only for them to be discarded and rebuilt in
code. This is all done in the name of making something ready for development.
This is contrary to my belief that any digital design process should start
with rough sketches, but move quickly into code and iterate from there. Those
sketches might even be done in code. A design is never “ready for dev”,
because a lot of what we consider to be design decisions – interaction,
animation, loading of data – can really only be prototyped in code. “Ready for
dev” implies that the creation is done and that the developer is merely there
to execute the designer’s vision, implicitly preventing them from questioning
any of the decisions when the rubber hits the road.
These are just two examples, but it illustrates a worrying trend towards a
premature optimization of design. These features encourage designers to make
decisions too early, to over-structure ideas before they’ve had a chance to
unfold. The result is a narrowing of the design space, where the flexibility
needed for creative discovery is replaced by enforced consistency and
structure. This comes on top of the incredible number of
structured tasks
that most modern design teams adhere to. This inevitably contributes to the
growing monoculture in digital design where everything starts to look and feel
the same, not because of shared intent, but because of shared constraints.
I’ve spent the last 15 years advocating for deeper collaboration between
designers and engineers, so it might seem contradictory to critique a tool
that brings those disciplines closer together. But interdisciplinary work
doesn’t mean collapsing into one way of thinking. The goal isn’t for designers
to adopt engineering practices, but to bring distinct perspectives through an
interdisciplinary way of collaborating.
Figma is extremely powerful, but it is bending us toward a way of working that
prioritizes structure over spontaneity. As designers, we should remain alert
to this shift, not because Figma is inherently bad, but because the values it
encodes can quietly reshape our practices. The best design work rarely starts
with order. It starts with questions, with play, with a lot of mess. We need
tools that make room for that. Because if everything is neatly aligned from
the beginning, we may never discover what lies just outside the grid.
