🚀🤖 Overclocking LLMs
We present qualitative examples showing how the uncovered mechanism can be leveraged to speed up a reasoning model's thought process.
Your browser does not support the video tag.
From 6 men and 4 women, how many ways can a 3-person committee be formed with at least one woman?
Your browser does not support the video tag.
A family group went fishing. Among them were two fathers and two sons. They caught three whole fish and gave one entire fish to each person. How many of the fishermen had no children of their own?
Your browser does not support the video tag.
Find the intersection of the two lines given by the equations: $2x + 3y = 6$ and $x - y = 1$.
Method
This work investigates how large reasoning models internally track their thinking progress and how such processes can be monitored and controlled. We focus on reasoning models that explicitly segment their computations using
<think>
and
</think>
tokens (e.g., DeepSeek-R1), allowing us to study the internal dynamics of the "thinking phase."
1. Monitoring the Thinking Phase
We hypothesize that hidden states encode a token's relative position within the thinking phase. To test this, we collect hidden representations from the final layer of the model for each token in a thinking trajectory $T = w_1w_2...w_N$. Each token is paired with a normalized position:
$$p_j^{(k)} = j / N_k$$
This creates a dataset $D = \{ (h_j^{(k)}, p_j^{(k)}) \}$, where $h \in \mathbb{R}^d$ is the hidden state and $p \in (0, 1]$ is the relative position. We learn a regression function:
$$\theta^* = \arg\min_\theta \sum (f_\theta(h) - p)^2$$
We compare a linear regressor (TPV: Thinking Progress Vector) with a 2-layer FFN and find no improvement from the latter, favoring the simpler TPV model. For improved temporal modeling, we also train a single-layer GRU on full token sequences:
$$D' = \{ (h_1, ..., h_N), (p_1, ..., p_N) \}$$
The GRU outperforms TPV, especially in generalizing from MATH-500 to GSM8K in both fine-tuned and zero-shot setups.
2. Controlling the Thinking Phase
To explore whether TPVs are causally involved in reasoning, we intervene on hidden states during decoding:
$$h^\alpha = h + \alpha\theta \quad \rightarrow \quad \theta^T h^\alpha = \theta^T h + \alpha||\theta||^2$$
This intervention occurs after attention layers to isolate its effect to a single token step. We refer to this manipulation as "
overclocking
" when $\alpha > 0$. Empirically, overclocking results in more concise and decisive reasoning while maintaining correctness.
Findings
Original trajectories often exhibit repetition and hesitation.
Overclocked outputs are shorter and more linear in progress prediction.
In some cases, the token count reduces by up to 6× while yielding the same correct answer.
Conclusion
These findings suggest that models internally track thinking progress

data.title: LISPy things you can do in 64K bytes of core
data.author: smartmic
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了在极小内存限制下运行LISP系统的历史和技术细节，特别是仅用64K内存的LISP实现，称为Kilo LISP。文章比较了早期计算机如IBM 704和PDP-1上的LISP实现，IBM 704有1,183,608位核心内存，而PDP-1仅有4096字内存。Kilo LISP占用约13K内存，剩余空间可容纳8192个cons单元。文章还展示了在这些系统上运行的LISP示例代码，并提到尽管早期计算机速度很慢，但如今可以在智能手机上模拟这些古老系统。文章重点关注内存使用而非运行速度。

主要讨论点：20世纪8位计算机时代，不同编程语言在编程教育中的适用性及优缺点

不同观点：
• PaulHoule认为，在8位计算机时代，BASIC是初学者编程的主流语言，但其使用GOTO和GOSUB存在缺陷，尤其是GOSUB不支持参数和局部变量，限制了编程的灵活性。
• 一些人不满BASIC作为入门语言，原因是GOTO语句导致程序结构不清晰，但PaulHoule指出GOSUB的局限性其实更严重。
• Pascal语言受到静态类型语言爱好者的欢迎，但由于6502等处理器的寄存器和寻址模式有限，编译Pascal代码非常困难。
• Logo语言因其Lisp风格和图形功能吸引了一部分人，特别是在MIT等学术机构中，被认为具有较强的教育价值。
• FORTH语言未被广泛视为教育语言，但其利用堆栈的方式和自定义控制结构的能力，吸引了部分有抱负的程序员，被视为介于BASIC和汇编之间的一种语言。

补充讨论：
• 到1983年左右，即使是廉价的计算机也能支持64KB内存，这为使用更多种类的编程语言（如C语言）提供了可能，但BASIC因其根深蒂固的地位依然占据主导。
• PaulHoule提到，理论上可以在6502处理器上运行Lisp，但未详细说明其实际可行性和流行程度。
• 争议焦点在于BASIC的简易性和普及性与其结构上的局限性之间的平衡，以及其他语言（如Pascal、Logo、FORTH）在教育中的潜在优势与实际应用中的困难。

LISPy things you can do in 64K bytes of core
where "in 64K bytes" shall mean 64K bytes for the LISP system, the
runtime stack, and the cons pool! This is the amount of space your
LISP system would get on a basic DEC PDP-11 or in a tiny-model PCDOS
program. It is probably a little less space than the first
implementations of LISP could use.
The IBM 704 electronic data processing machine at M.I.T., on which
LISP was first implemented in 1960, had 32K words of 36-bit core
memory,
[1]
which in this case really means one tiny
ferrite ring
per bit. So there was a total of 3632768=1,183,608 tiny little
toroids housed in a not so tiny steel frame. The 704 required a
rather spacious room with reinforced floors and industrial air
conditioning. The total weight of a typical installation was around
10 metric tons.
The LISP system itself occupied 12K words of core and one word would
hold a complete cons cell,
[1]
so the machine offered a little
less than 20K cells of space to LISP. But then, the IBM 704 at the M.I.T.
was quite a well-equipped machine. Many 704 installations included
as little as 8Kwords or even 4Kwords of memory
[2]
— too
little to run a LISP system. Here is a LISP1.0 sample program from
[1]
:
DEFINE
(( (SUBST (LAMBDA (X Y Z) (COND ((ATOM Z) (COND ((EQ Y Z) X)
(T Z))) (T (CONS (SUBST X Y (CAR Z)) (SUBST X Y (CDR Z))))))) ))
()
Note that programs were usually typed on as few lines as possible,
because they had to be punched to punched cards or typed in at a
teletype which echoed its input on paper. The operator (DEFINE),
the arguments (in double parentheses in the case of DEFINE), and
an environment had to be supplied to the LISP system in three
separate expressions.
There were smaller computers running LISP, though. In 1964 there
was PDP-1 LISP, which was an implementation for DEC's PDP-1 computer
and it ran on systems with as little as 4096 words of 18-bit storage,
where the system itself used around 2000 words.
[3]
Even on the
PDP-1 a cons cell would fit in a single word, so some 2000 cells
were available to the system. Here is a PDP-1 LISP sample program
from
[3]
— yes, PDP-1 LISP used lower case:
(rplacd (quote r1) (quote (expr (lambda (m l) (cond ((null l) m)
(t (r1 (cons (car l) m) (cdr l))))))))
(rplacd (quote reverse) (quote (expr (lambda (l) (r1 nil l)))))
The LISP system that will be used in the following is
Kilo LISP
,
which is a portable implementation written in ANSI C (C89) that can
compile to a tiny model PCDOS executable that runs in 64K bytes of
memory. The LISP system itself occupies about 13K bytes, leaving
enough space for 8192 cons cells, where each cell allocates 5 bytes
(16 bits car, 16 bits cdr, and 3 bits tag, the latter rounded up
to 8 bits). Here is a sample program:
(setq assoc
(lambda (x a)
(cond ((null a) nil)
((eq x (caar a)) (car a))
(else (assoc x (cdr a))))))
The Kilo LISP system offers less than half as many cons cells as a
big IBM 704 installation and about four times the space of a minimal
PDP-1. Of course, ancient computers were slow: the IBM 704 had a
clock speed of 40kHz (0.04 MIPS) and the PDP-1 operated at 150kHz
(0.15 MIPS), but then the LISP systems on those machines were
carefully hand-crafted assembly language programs and their hardware
would typically execute one instruction per clock cycle.
Today you can probably emulate an IBM 704 and a PDP-1 on a cheap
smartphone, both running at a multiple of the speed of the original
hardware, while playing your favorite jump-and-run game. So while
a 704 or a PDP-1 could probably run all of the following example
programs, they would certainly take their time. The rest of this
essay will concentrate on the memory aspect and ignore run times.
Here is a
first impression
of what ancient LISP feels like.

主要讨论点：20世纪8位计算机时代，不同编程语言在编程教育中的适用性及优缺点

不同观点：
• PaulHoule认为，在8位计算机时代，BASIC是初学者编程的主流语言，但其使用GOTO和GOSUB存在缺陷，尤其是GOSUB不支持参数和局部变量，限制了编程的灵活性。
• 一些人不满BASIC作为入门语言，原因是GOTO语句导致程序结构不清晰，但PaulHoule指出GOSUB的局限性其实更严重。
• Pascal语言受到静态类型语言爱好者的欢迎，但由于6502等处理器的寄存器和寻址模式有限，编译Pascal代码非常困难。
• Logo语言因其Lisp风格和图形功能吸引了一部分人，特别是在MIT等学术机构中，被认为具有较强的教育价值。
• FORTH语言未被广泛视为教育语言，但其利用堆栈的方式和自定义控制结构的能力，吸引了部分有抱负的程序员，被视为介于BASIC和汇编之间的一种语言。

data.title: Ask HN: How did Soham Parekh get so many jobs?
data.author: jshchnz
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对Soham事件的多角度分析，包括招聘流程、多重就业现象以及企业责任

不同观点：
• **Soham技术能力强，但表现不佳**：
   - gargoyle9123：Soham在面试中表现出色，技术能力强，但实际工作表现不佳，频繁找借口，甚至撒谎。
   - dazzeloid：尽管Soham同时在多个公司工作，但在我们公司工作期间表现良好，直到被发现。

• **多重就业现象的普遍性与合理性**：
   - Tade0：多重就业在行业中较为常见，特别是在大公司中，因为员工的超额表现不会带来显著的收益。altairprime：多重就业如同婚姻中的不忠，有时是无可厚非的。
   - robswc：Soham的简历和工作记录显示出巨大的红旗，但他在面试中却屡屡成功，令人不解。

• **招聘流程的缺陷与改进建议**：
   - ungreased0675：公司往往追逐顶尖人才，但实际上只需要普通工程师。招聘过程应该更加务实。
   - tabs_or_spaces：Soham事件反映出招聘方的无能，应该承认并改进招聘流程。
   - isatty：仅凭面试中的Leetcode表现来判断候选人是不合理的。

• **法律与道德问题**：
   - jsbg：Soham可能在就业资格上存在问题，公司未做充分的背景调查，这本身就是一个巨大的红旗。
   - dalemhurley：存在讨论多重就业策略的社区，这对那些真诚工作的员工不公平。

补充讨论：
• **招聘中的文化与心理因素**：
   - jm20：在当前就业市场中，许多优秀的求职者难以获得面试机会，而Soham却能屡次成功，可能与其面试技巧和自我推销能力有关。

• **企业结构与流程的影响**：
   - jm20：初创公司往往缺乏严格的筛选流程，这在一定程度上为多重就业者提供了机会。
   - jcadam：大公司的结构和流程有助于防止此类现象的发生。

• **Soham的自我推销能力**：
   - bibek_poudel：Soham擅长通过邮件和沟通展示自己的能力和兴趣，这也是他能成功通过面试的原因之一。

争议焦点：
• **Soham是否应被视为受害者或欺骗者**：
   - 一部分评论认为Soham技术能力强，但在实际工作中表现不佳，属于欺骗行为。
   - 另一部分评论则认为公司招聘流程不完善，应对其成功多重就业负责。

总的来说，讨论围绕Soham技术能力与实际工作表现的矛盾、多重就业现象的普遍性与合理性、以及公司在招聘和背景调查中的责任展开。

data.title: Local-first software (2019)
data.author: gasull
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了云应用和传统本地应用的优缺点，特别关注创作过程中的协作与数据所有权问题。云应用如Google Docs、Figma、Slack等提供了无缝协作和跨设备访问的优势，但用户对数据的控制权受限于服务提供商，存在数据无法完全自主掌控的风险。相比之下，传统本地应用允许用户完全拥有和管理自己的数据，但缺乏云应用的协作便利。文章提出，理想的解决方案应结合云应用的协作优势和传统应用的数据所有权优势，使用户既能方便地跨设备协作，又能真正拥有自己的数据。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：本地优先软件的优点、实现方式、技术挑战及商业模式

不同观点：
• DataDaoDe支持本地优先软件模型，认为用户应能够一次性购买软件并永久使用，而不必依赖云服务和订阅费用。他强调数据隐私和本地操作的优点，并认为这种模型能带来更好的用户体验和激励结构。
• samwillis提到本地优先软件社区和相关会议（如Local-first Software conference），强调社区对同步引擎和开发工具的关注，并提供了相关资源链接。
• the_snooze指出，任何具有在线依赖的系统都需要持续的维护和费用，认为本地优先（或本地唯一）的设计才能确保长期可靠性。
• ashdev分享了自己开发本地优先应用Brisqi的经验，强调真正的本地优先应用应完全离线工作，云同步应作为次要功能而非必要条件。
• montereynack介绍了他们在工业设备领域应用本地优先原则的案例，强调本地处理对工业自动化等领域的重要性。
• GMoromisato不同意避免中心化架构的技术折中方案，认为应通过商业模式创新来解决云供应商问题，如通过标准化合同和许可证来保护用户权益。
• GregorStocks对CRDTs在复杂冲突解决中的有效性提出质疑，认为在实际应用中（如编辑操作）自动解决冲突的承诺难以实现。
• monkeyelite认为并非每个应用都需要自己的同步平台，建议利用文件系统和现有解决方案（如git、box）来实现同步。
• ibizaman介绍了自己的开源项目，目标是让自托管变得更加容易，并与现有的解决方案（如YUNoHost）进行比较。
• davepeck表示虽然本地优先模式在理论上很好，但在实践中面临很多技术挑战，如同步引擎和冲突解决等。
• hkt认为自托管和本地优先软件对普通用户来说过于复杂，建议通过合作社模式来实现中心化运营和民主治理。
• dtkav提出需要为本地优先技术找到可行的商业模式，并介绍了自己在Relay项目中的尝试。
• rshemet提到本地优先在AI时代的应用，介绍了自己在Cactus项目中的实践，强调私有和离线AI的重要性。
• hemant6488分享了自己在SoundLeaf项目中的经验，强调一次性购买和无数据收集的优点。

补充讨论：
• 本地优先软件的技术挑战主要集中在同步、冲突解决和离线功能实现上。
• 商业模式的讨论中，有人建议通过标准化合同和许可证来保护用户权益，有人则尝试通过分离计算和控制平面来实现可持续的商业模式。
• 自托管和本地优先软件在工业和AI领域的应用案例也被提及，展示了其在特定行业中的潜力和价值。
• 社区对本地优先软件的支持和资源共享为开发者提供了重要的学习和实践机会。

44473135.article_content:
Motivation: collaboration and ownership
It’s amazing how easily we can collaborate online nowadays. We use Google Docs to collaborate on documents, spreadsheets and presentations; in Figma we work together on user interface designs; we communicate with colleagues using Slack; we track tasks in Trello; and so on. We depend on these and many other online services, e.g. for taking notes, planning projects or events, remembering contacts, and a whole raft of business uses.
We will call these services “cloud apps,” but you could just as well call them “
SaaS
” or “web-based apps.” What they have in common is that we typically access them through a web browser or through mobile apps, and that they store their data on a server.
Today’s cloud apps offer big benefits compared to earlier generations of software: seamless collaboration, and being able to access data from any device. As we run more and more of our lives and work through these cloud apps, they become more and more critical to us. The more time we invest in using one of these apps, the more valuable the data in it becomes to us.
However, in our research we have spoken to a lot of creative professionals, and in that process we have also learned about the downsides of cloud apps.
When you have put a lot of creative energy and effort into making something, you tend to have a deep emotional attachment to it. If you do creative work, this probably seems familiar. (When we say “creative work,” we mean not just visual art, or music, or poetry — many other activities, such as explaining a technical topic, implementing an intricate algorithm, designing a user interface, or figuring out how to lead a team towards some goal are also creative efforts.)
Our research on software that supports the creative process is discussed further in our articles
Capstone, a tablet for thinking
and
The iPad as a fast, precise tool for creativity
.
In the process of performing that creative work, you typically produce files and data: documents, presentations, spreadsheets, code, notes, drawings, and so on. And you will want to keep that data: for reference and inspiration in the future, to include it in a portfolio, or simply to archive because you feel proud of it. It is important to
feel ownership
of that data, because the creative expression is something so personal.
Unfortunately, cloud apps are problematic in this regard. Although they let you access your data anywhere, all data access must go via the server, and you can only do the things that the server will let you do. In a sense, you don’t have full ownership of that data — the cloud provider does. In the words of a
bumper sticker
: “There is no cloud, it’s just someone else’s computer.”
We use the term
“ownership”
not in the sense of intellectual property law and copyright, but rather as the creator’s perceived relationship to their data. We discuss this notion in
a later section
.
When data is stored on “someone else’s computer”, that third party assumes a degree of control over that data. Cloud apps are provided as a service; if the service is unavailable, you cannot use the software, and you can no longer access your data created with that software. If the service shuts down, even though you might be able to export your data, without the servers there is normally no way for you to continue running your own copy of that software. Thus, you are at the mercy of the company providing the service.
Before web apps came along, we had what we might call “old-fashioned” apps: programs running on your local computer, reading and writing files on the local disk. We still use a lot of applications of this type today: text editors and IDEs, Git and other version control systems, and many specialized software packages such as graphics applications or CAD software fall in this category.
The software we are talking about in this article are apps for creating documents or files (such as text, graphics, spreadsheets, CAD drawings, or music), or personal data repositories (such as notes, calendars, to-do lists, or password managers). We are not talking about implementing things like banking services, e-commerce, social networking, ride-sharing, or similar services, which are well served by centralized systems.
In old-fashioned apps, the data lives in files on your local disk, so you have full agency and ownership of that data: you can do anything you like, including long-term archiving, making backups, manipulating the files using other programs, or deleting the files if you no longer want them. You don’t need anybody’s permission to access your files, since they are yours. You don’t have to depend on servers operated by another company.
To sum up: the cloud gives us collaboration, but old-fashioned apps give us ownership. Can’t we have the best of both worlds?
We would like both the convenient cross-device access and real-time collaboration provided by cloud apps, and also the personal ownership of your own data embodied by “old-fashione

data.title: Valve conquered PC gaming – what comes next?
data.author: HelloUsername
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Valve的成就、现状以及未来的发展方向

不同观点：
• Shorel认为，Valve在PC游戏面临衰退时坚持捍卫了PC游戏，而不是像其他公司一样转向主机市场。Valve通过Steam和其他努力拯救了PC游戏产业，而微软和其他公司只是 opportunistic（机会主义）的追随者。
• everdrive和jbreckmckye都担心Valve在Gabe Newell离开或公司上市后可能会变质，导致PC游戏市场被“掠夺者”破坏。他们认为Valve保持私有化和独立性是其服务质量的关键。
• DrNosferatu建议Valve应扩展SteamOS以支持更多硬件，并提供简化的Linux桌面环境，以吸引更多用户从Windows转向SteamOS。
• senko对Valve的当前状态感到满意，认为Valve已经在市场上占据主导地位，不需要做出重大改变。
• vlade11115指出，Epic Games Store等竞争对手虽然投入大量资金，但仍无法与Steam竞争。他认为微软的Game Pass是Valve面临的最大威胁。
• haunter希望对Valve涉及的皮肤赌博和战利品箱系统进行强有力的监管，认为这是Valve带来的负面影响。
• skizm和0xTJ讨论了Valve的垄断地位及其潜在的法律风险，同时提到Valve平台的成功是基于其优质的用户体验。
• ChrisNorstrom持有双重观点，一方面担心Valve过于舒适可能导致创新不足，另一方面也认可Valve在硬件领域的扩展努力。
• ThrowOregonAway认为Valve通过Steam Deck在移动游戏领域取得了成功，并对比了任天堂的失败策略。
• luqtas批评了Steam的高抽成和低可见性问题，希望有一种去中心化的游戏分发方式。
• webdevver预测整个游戏行业将像电影行业一样萎缩，认为社交媒体才是未来的主要盈利领域。

• Valve在PC游戏市场的地位及其面临的潜在威胁，特别是微软的Game Pass。

• 对Valve现有商业模式的批评，特别是对皮肤赌博和平台抽成的担忧。
• 关于游戏行业整体趋势的讨论，包括行业萎缩的可能性和社交媒体的崛起。

data.title: Eastern Baltic cod grow much smaller than they did due to overfishing
data.author: littlexsparkee
data.article_summary: 一项发表在《Science Advances》期刊的新研究显示，波罗的海东部鳕鱼因数十年过度捕捞而发生进化，体型大幅缩小。过去鳕鱼可长达三英尺，但到2019年，其体型缩小了一半以上，平均鳕鱼如今可置于人手心。研究分析了1996年至2019年鳕鱼的耳石和DNA，发现大体型相关的基因变异逐渐减少，表明过度捕捞改变了鳕鱼的遗传构成，使其趋于小型化。尽管海洋温度上升也有影响，但主要驱动因素是人类活动。这种进化变化可能导致物种适应环境的能力下降，恢复需要很长时间，甚至可能无法实现。这项研究突显了跟踪物种基因池的重要性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：有关波罗的海鳕鱼种群变化及其背后的生态和进化问题，以及对渔业和环境保护的影响。

不同观点：
• ryao：反对基于“小鱼以后会长大”的前提而放生小鱼的做法，认为这样会放走基因不良的成年小鱼，损害基因库。并质疑这一发现是否会影响渔业中的保育规则。
• olelele：指出波罗的海由于农业革命后的污染，鱼类体内含有重金属和毒素，瑞典当局建议每月只吃一次，孕妇和有健康问题的人不应食用。并提到污染导致海底大面积死亡区。
• rr808：提到毛利渔民曾选择吃中等大小的鱼，留下最大的鱼，因为它们是最优的繁殖者，但未提供具体参考。
• yard2010：将问题引向蚊子的抗药性问题，认为与环境问题相比，蚊子的威胁更令人担忧。
• littlexsparkee：指出文章标题缩略后仅适用于东波罗的海鳕鱼，而非所有鳕鱼。
• skeledrew：不同意文章的措辞，认为鳕鱼并非主动变小，而是达尔文“适者生存”的结果，小鳕鱼能逃脱渔网并繁殖。并指出大鳕鱼的回归需要数千年的自然演化。
• veidelis：引用拉脱维亚新闻，提到波罗的海鳕鱼繁殖问题与海水盐度不足有关。
• gouthamve：推荐一本关于鳕鱼捕捞历史的书，认为过度捕捞导致鳕鱼数量减少。
• lambdasquirrel：引用Philip Glass的交响乐句，表达对生态灾难的感慨。
• sharpshadow：提到无象牙大象的例子，暗示人类活动对动物进化的影响。
• ivanbalepin：提到有人收集东波罗的海鳕鱼的耳石，期待未来能发明新的使用方法。
• jongjong：认为进化可以很快发生，不一定要经过数百万年，举例说明捕食者行为的改变能迅速影响可见特征。
• thaumasiotes：传统方法是捕雄留雌，以避免雌性被淘汰，但可能会看到雄性进化得更像雌性。
• weregiraffe：质疑按重量捕鱼时，鱼的大小是否重要，认为一吨鳕鱼就是一吨鳕鱼。
• macinjosh：询问是否有“传统”鳕鱼被圈养或DNA样本保存，建议通过基因技术将缺失基因重新引入基因库。

补充讨论：
• 讨论涉及鳕鱼基因库保护、进化速度、环境保护与人类活动的影响等多方面。
• 争议焦点包括是否应放生小鱼以保护基因库，以及人类活动（如污染和过度捕捞）对鱼类种群的长期影响。
• 不同评论者从生态学、进化生物学、历史和个人经验等角度提供了多样化的见解。

44474759.article_content:
A catch of Baltic Sea cod in 1987 shows fish that grew more than three feet long, with Finnish fisheries biologist Eero Kalevi Aro.
Jesper Bay of the Danish Institute for Fisheries and Marine Research, March 1987
A new study reveals that decades of overfishing have altered the evolution of cod in the eastern Baltic Sea.
The research, published in the journal
Science Advances
on June 25, aimed to answer a question that had puzzled scientists for decades: What’s behind the dramatic size change in eastern Baltic cod?
Study lead author Kwi Young Han holds a fully grown cod in two hands.
Thorsten Reusch, GEOMAR
These fish used to be enormous. In 1996, the biggest Baltic cod grew more than three feet long. By 2019, however, their sizes had been cut in half, and the cod’s weight was but a fraction of its previous glory. Now, the average cod can sit in a person’s cupped hands.
For decades, fishers in the Baltic Sea caught cod relentlessly, using large nets. Smaller fish could escape more easily, presenting an external pressure to remain smaller. But directly connecting the population’s decrease in size to evolution—and not other environmental factors, such as pollution or temperature change—is notoriously difficult for scientists.
Regulators banned fishing of eastern Baltic cod in 2019 due to a population collapse, but their size still shows no signs of bouncing back. In the new study, scientists find that overfishing did not merely remove the biggest individuals—it changed the genetic composition of the cod population, predisposing them to remain small.
“Human harvesting elicits the strongest selection pressures in nature,”
Thorsten Reusch
, a marine ecologist at the GEOMAR Helmholtz Center for Ocean Research Kiel in Germany and co-author of the paper, tells Emily Anthes of the
New York Times
. “It can be really fast that you see evolutionary change.”
Did you know? Shrinking body size
In animals, shrinking body size is a known response to warming, with populations of
birds, frogs and mammals
reportedly growing to smaller sizes over time as climate change raises temperatures. Individual clownfish have been found to
shrink during ocean heat waves
.
To uncover the reason behind the dramatic drop in cod size, researchers analyzed 152 fish otoliths—tiny, bone-like structures found in the inner ear—that were collected from eastern Baltic cod harvested between 1996 and 2019. Otoliths can act as records of a fish’s annual growth, serving as biological timekeepers, like tree rings.
The researchers then sequenced the DNA of each fish and searched for areas of the genome and genetic variants that were associated with the growth rate. In the end, the team revealed that over time, variants related to a larger body size had become less common. This suggests an external pressure was guiding the cod’s evolution.
“What we are observing is evolution in action, driven by human activity,” Reusch tells the
Guardian
’s Hannah Devlin. “This is scientifically fascinating, but ecologically deeply concerning.”
Though warming ocean temperatures may also be a factor in driving smaller cod sizes, the dramatic decrease in size is far greater than what scientists expect could have been caused by temperature shifts alone, according to the
New York Times
.
Scientists say that this evolutionary change in cod can carry consequences. The genetic variants associated with a faster growth rate might already be lost from the population, according to a
statement
. This decrease in genetic diversity might make it harder for a species to adapt to environmental changes in the future.
“Evolutionary change unfolds over many generations,” says Reusch in the statement. “Recovery takes far longer than decline, and it may not even be possible.”
Stefano Mariani
, a marine biologist at Liverpool John Moores University in England who was not involved in the research, tells the
Guardian
the work is a “milestone” in showing that human activity can speed up evolution. This, he adds, highlights the importance of tracking not only a species’ numbers, but also its gene pool.

data.title: The chemical secrets that help keep honey fresh for so long
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 蜂蜜因其特殊的化学性质和制作过程，具有极强的抗变质能力。蜜蜂在酿蜜过程中，通过去除花蜜中的水分并使用酶提高酸度，使得蜂蜜的含水量降至15%-18%，同时糖分高度浓缩。这种低水分高糖的环境抑制了微生物的生长。密封的蜂蜜限制了氧气接触，进一步防止变质。虽然蜂蜜可能会结晶，但在适当保存下不会变质。然而，开封后接触空气和污染物可能导致变质。这种抗腐能力使得蜂蜜被视为一种“神奇”的食品，类似于现代食品科学中的“低水分活性”保存法。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：蜂蜜的防腐特性及其背后的科学原理

不同观点：
• YeGoblynQueenne认为，尽管打开的蜂蜜罐会暴露在空气中，并可能受到污染（如沾有细菌的勺子），但蜂蜜不会变质。他们基于个人经验指出，即便蜂蜜中混入了其他食物残渣，蜂蜜依然不会腐败，只是外观可能变差。
• Jun8将蜂蜜的防腐特性与Nutella等其他低水分活度（aw）的食物进行比较，指出这些食品因低aw而能长期保存，并提供了FDA对水分活度的定义链接。
• bjelkeman-again补充说明蜂蜜中常见的乳酸菌具有抗微生物效果，能够抑制其他细菌的生长，并提供了相关研究链接。
• cypherpunks01提到蜂蜜中可能含有少量Clostridium botulinum细菌，这种细菌会导致肉毒中毒，因此不应喂给婴儿。

44463429.article_content:
The chemical secrets that help keep honey fresh for so long
6 days ago
Share
Save
Veronique Greenwood
Share
Save
Getty Images
Honey is a natural sweetener, and bacteria loves to feast on sugar. But honey is remarkably resistant to spoilage. What's behind its ability to beat the bugs?
Most jarred delights have a limited shelf life – they're just one mucky spoon dip away from growing a luscious crop of mould or a thriving colony of bacteria. But there are certain foods with peculiar staying power, capable of staying edible for years.
Honey is one of these magical substances. In a sealed environment, while the golden stuff may crystallise, turning thick and chunky,
it will not go off
. This persistent ability to resist decay is down to honey's chemistry, and the way in which it is made.
When we say that food has spoiled, what we actually mean is that
something else
has got to it first, something microscopic. Bacteria, fungi, and moulds
are present
in at least low numbers in many foods, and a number of the procedures humans use to preserve food are designed to discourage these creatures consuming it.
Alamy
Honey may crystallise when it is in a sealed jar, but it does not go off (Credit: Alamy)
Many of these microorganisms tend to prefer moist conditions, higher (but not too high) temperatures, a mellow pH, and plenty of oxygen around to use in their metabolism. Dehydrating meat or fruit, then, deprives them of water. Cooking food to a high heat and then moving it into the fridge for storage first kills off many bugs and puts a damper on the growth of any left behind. Suspending food in a pickling mixture wards off all but the most acid-loving creatures. Sealing something in a jar limits the oxygen they have access to.
We are always fighting a losing battle against these organisms
Even food that's been put through a gauntlet of preservation procedures usually has a limited shelf life, as you might know if you have ever opened a jar of butterscotch sauce from the back of grandma's fridge, sealed in 1985, to find a thick carpet of fuzz within. (Don't ask me how I know.)
We are always fighting a losing battle against these organisms, and whether it's a whiff of vinegar that tells us the
Lactobacillus
has had its way with the orange juice, or black mould spots on the inside wall of the peanut butter jar, the signs of their presence are often unsubtle, and unavoidable.
But honey is an unusual case, and here is why. It's made by honeybees from flower nectar, and starts out as a warmish, watery, sugary fluid, the kind of thing that seems like it would be the purest bacteria bait. The bees
concentrate the nectar
on the way to the hive, removing some of the water, use enzymes to raise the acid content in the fluid discouraging some forms of microorganisms from growing, and break down the sugars into simpler ones, then decant the stuff into honeycomb chambers.
Getty Images
Sealing honey in jars adds to the purifying procedures bees carry out, which massively reduces the water content (Credit: Getty Images)
Next, they do something remarkable: they start to fan the
honey with their wings
. The fanning slowly evaporates the remaining water, like an oscillating fan evaporating sweat from your skin, so a substance that was once about
70% or 80% water
sees that number drop and drop and drop.
Fully ripened honey typically has a water content between about
15% and 18%
. In fact, the proportion of sugar molecules to water is so enormous that it would not be physically possible to dissolve that much sugar into that much water, without a process like the one honeybees use.
More like this:
•
Bee gold: Why honey is an insect superfood
•
How to make fruit and vegetables last longer
•
The food that could last 2,000 years
There is plenty of sugar there, and of course microorganisms would love to have a go at it. But with so little water – and the acidity providing an additional disincentive – they simply can't survive. Seal honey in a jar, to limit the availability of oxygen, and there's another barrier to growth.
This is a state known as "low water activity" among food scientists, and in fact, lowering a substance's water activity is a common trick to preserve processed foods. It is possible to keep
moist food from spoiling as long as the water molecules are tied up in interactions with salt or sugar
, for example.
This doesn't mean that honey can withstand all challenges to freshness. Once a jar of honey is open, its surface is being regularly exposed to the air, and dipping licked spoons in will bring bacteria and moisture that weren't there when the jar was sealed.
But take charge of the situation by adding water, add your own specially chosen microorganism, and you get
mead
– a type of spoilage that few would argue with on a hot day, sitting in the shade.
--
If you liked this story,
sign up for The Essential List newsletter
– a handpicked selection of features, videos and can't-miss news, delivered to your inbox twice a week.

data.title: Running a Certificate Transparency log
data.author: Metalnem
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍运行一个证书透明度日志（Certificate Transparency log, CT log）的重要性及其实施方法。CT技术通过确保证书颁发的透明性来增强网络安全，目前缺少足够的独立日志运营者。文章提到，得益于新的静态CT API和Sunlight实现，现在运行CT日志变得更加便宜和简便。运行一个CT日志需要一台服务器、ECC内存、2-3 Gbps出站带宽，以及3-5 TB的存储空间。日志运营者需遵守Google和Apple的CT日志政策，并参与社区交流。文章鼓励有兴趣的人参与，并提供了相关资源和支持渠道。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Certificate Transparency (CT) 日志系统的改进、存储责任分配、审计问题、去中心化存储的可能性以及对集中化机构的不信任。

不同观点：
• **支持Sunlight和static-ct-api的创新**：
  - **agwa**认为，传统的CT日志依赖数据库，复杂且昂贵，导致运营困难和失败频发。Sunlight和static-ct-api提供了新的解决方案，简化了系统并降低了成本，令人兴奋。

• **关注下游技术CRLite的进展**：
  - **baobun**指出，Mozilla在CRLite方面的进展值得更多关注，提供了另一种改进SSL/TLS信任机制的途径。

• **质疑CT日志服务器存储责任**：
  - **torbid**质疑为什么CT日志服务器要负责存储，建议让发布者自己存储数据，日志服务器只负责签名和密钥管理。这样可以减少服务器重启时的数据丢失风险。

• **关注证书系统的审计问题**：
  - **tonymet**提出，目前缺乏对证书颁发机构（CA）系统的业余或专业审计，消费者和发布者往往忽视证书问题。SSL/TLS在防止窃听方面做得很好，但在建立信任和身份方面仍有不足。

• **建议使用去中心化存储**：
  - **ncrmro**建议将CT日志存储在Arweave这样的区块链存储系统上，通过费用支持存储扩展，解决长期存储问题。

• **对带宽需求的质疑**：
  - **gslin**对运行CT日志所需的带宽（2-3Gbps）表示怀疑，认为需要进一步确认是否真的需要如此高的带宽。

• **对集中化CA的不信任**：
  - **udev4096**不支持帮助集中化的CA，认为DANE（DNS-Based Authentication of Named Entities）才是未来，去中心化的信任机制更为理想。

• **对Google政策的不满**：
  - **johnklos**批评Google在CT日志运营中要求提供联系人信息，认为这是不公平的，自己不愿意向Google提供联系信息。

• **对CT系统技术实现的疑问**：
  - **cypherpunks01**询问CT系统如何实现仅追加条目和公开透明的时间戳记录，并质疑是否可以使用区块链技术来实现这一目标，或者数据量是否过大。

补充讨论：
• **链接分享**：
  - 多个评论中提供了相关技术的链接和资源，如CRLite的演示视频和相关研究文档。

• **对技术细节的关注**：
  - 评论中对CT日志的存储、带宽需求、技术实现等细节有较多讨论，反映了技术社区对实际操作问题的关注。

争议焦点：
• **存储责任的分配**：
  - **torbid**认为CT日志服务器不应负责存储，而应由发布者负责，但这一观点未得到其他评论的直接回应。

• **对集中化机构的信任**：
  - **udev4096**和**johnklos**对集中化CA和Google的政策表示不满，反映出去中心化和隐私保护在这一技术社区中的重要性。

44494430.article_content:
7 Jul 2025
You Should Run a Certificate Transparency Log
Hear me out. If you are an organization with some spare storage and bandwidth, or an engineer looking to justify an
overprovisioned homelab
, you should consider running a Certificate Transparency log. It’s cheaper, easier, and more important than you might think.
Certificate Transparency
(CT) is one of the technologies that underpin the security of the whole web. It keeps Certificate Authorities honest, and allows website owners to be notified of unauthorized certificate issuance. It’s a big part of how the WebPKI went from the punchline of “weakest link” jokes to the robust foundation of the security of most of digital life… in less than fifteen years!
CT is an intrinsically distributed system: CAs must submit each certificate to two CT logs operated by third parties and trusted by the browsers. This list is, and has been for a couple years, uncomfortably short. There just aren’t as many independent log operators as we’d like. Operating a log right now would be an immense contribution to the security of virtually every Internet user.
It also comes with the bragging rights to claim that your public key is on
billions
of devices.
Where’s the catch? Well, until recently running a log was a pain, and expensive. I am writing this because as of a few months ago,
this has changed
!
Browsers now accept CT logs that implement the new
Static CT API
, which I designed and productionized in collaboration with Let’s Encrypt and the rest of the WebPKI community over the past year and a half. The key difference is that it makes it possible to serve the read path of a CT log exclusively through static, S3 and CDN friendly files.
Moreover, the new
Sunlight
implementation, sponsored by Let’s Encrypt, implements the write path with minimal dependencies and requirements. It can upload the Static CT assets directly to object storage, or store them on any POSIX filesystem.
You can learn more if you are curious in
Let’s Encrypt’s retrospective
, in the original
Sunlight design document
, or in the summarized
public announcement
.
Geomys
, my open source maintenance firm,
operates a pro-bono Sunlight-backed trusted Static CT log for $10k/year
, including hardware amortization, colocation, and bandwidth. I’m sure it can be done for cheaper.
The shopping list
Ok, so what does it take to run a CT log in 2025
4
?
Servers: one. No need to make the log a distributed system, CT itself is a distributed system.
If you want to offer redundancy you can run multiple logs.
The uptime target is 99%
3
over three months, which allows for nearly 22h of downtime. That’s more than three
motherboard failures
per month.
CPU and memory: whatever,
as long as it’s ECC memory
. Four cores and 2 GB will do.
Bandwidth: 2 – 3 Gbps outbound.
Storage: you have two options.
3 – 5 TB of usable redundant filesystem space on SSDs
1
.
3 – 5 TB of S3-compatible object storage, and 200 GB of cache on SSD.
Static CT logs are just flat static files, which you can serve with any HTTP server
2
from disk, or expose as a public object storage bucket.
People: at least two. The Google policy requires two contacts, and generally who wants to carry a pager alone.
That’s pretty much it!
Durability is the first priority: it’s really important that you never lose data once it’s fsync’ed to disk or PUT to object storage, since your log will have signed and returned SCTs, which are promises to serve the certificates it received. This means for example that backups are useless: they would rollback the log’s state.
In terms of ongoing effort, a log operator is expected to read the
Google
and
Apple
CT Log policies, monitor the ct-policy@chromium.org mailing list, update the log implementation from time to time, and rotate log temporal shards every year. (For example, we just stood up 2027 shards of our log.)
Given the logs lifecycle, you should plan to stick around for at least three years.
Sign me up!
If you want to become a CT log operator, first of all… thank you!
The
Sunlight README
was rewritten recently to get you up and running easily. Sunlight is highly specialized for Certificate Transparency and the WebPKI, and it’s designed to help you operate a healthy, useful CT log with minimal configuration.
The community is eager to welcome new log operators. You can post questions, reports, and updates on the
transparency.dev Slack
,
ct-policy mailing list
, or
Sunlight issue tracker
. I encourage you to reach out even just to share your plans, or to ask any questions you might have before committing to running a log.
You might also want to follow me on Bluesky at
@filippo.abyssdomain.expert
or on Mastodon at
@filippo@abyssdomain.expert
.
The picture
I
systematically
make the mistake of reaching a beautiful spot with my motorcycle, watching the sunset, and
then
realizing “oh, shoot, now it’s dark!” This time, the motorcycle didn’t start, too, and it was the first ride of the season in January. Got to read
A Tour of WebAuthn

data.title: The Miyawaki Method of micro-forestry
data.author: zeristor
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了宫脇方法（Miyawaki Method）这一微型森林种植技术，该方法通过种植本地树种，在短时间内打造密集的小型森林，已在全球范围内受到广泛关注。文章探讨了宫脇方法的创始人宫脇昭博士的遗产，以及该方法在不同地区的应用实例，如横滨国立大学和温哥华的Strathcona公园。尽管宫脇方法在绿化爱好者和政府中颇受欢迎，但专业生态学家对其效果的评价较少。文章还引用了多篇相关文献和案例研究，讨论了该方法的成功和争议。最后，文章邀请读者支持相关播客，以获取更多内容。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Miyawaki方法及其在植树和生态恢复中的应用

不同观点：
• **lordswork**：详细介绍了Miyawaki方法的关键步骤，如大量添加有机物质、混合种植本地植物、高密度种植和厚覆盖层，认为该方法能比传统方法更快地形成生物多样性丰富的森林。
• **PaulHoule**：认为Miyawaki方法在某些生态系统中有效，但并非所有地方都适用，尤其是在热带地区，如果植物选择不当，可能会失败。
• **goda90**：认为任何形式的植树造林都是好的，但也要注意大片连续森林生态系统的重要性，因为森林的分割可能威胁到某些物种的生存。
• **thimkerbell**：提到相关播客，但认为文字记录不够简洁。
• **zeristor**：引用了一个播客内容，指出Miyawaki方法在绿色空间爱好者、产业和政府中受欢迎，但专业或学术生态学家对其效力评论较少。
• **leke**：推荐了《一根稻草的革命》这本书，认为其关于自然农法和哲学的观点值得参考。
• **shermantanktop**：提到一个关于Crowther实验室的节目，指出其中讨论了不可持续的造林活动，但也提到了树根与地下生物群的资源交换。
• **J7jKW2AAsgXhWm**：分享了在伯克利看到的Miyawaki微型森林的例子，认为虽然初期热情高涨，但可能有更简单的方法获得类似好处，且这些森林因过于密集而难以进入。
• **contingencies**：简要总结为“种植本地植物”。

补充讨论：
- Miyawaki方法的适用性和局限性在不同生态系统中的表现是一个争议焦点。
- 讨论中提到了与其他方法（如自然农法、传统造林）的对比。
- 强调了生态系统连续性和大型森林对某些物种的重要性。
- 还涉及了公众和专业学术界对Miyawaki方法的不同关注程度。

Cover artwork by Ale Silva
Summary
The Miyawaki Method of micro-forestry is a viral sensation: sprouting tiny, dense, native tree cover in neighbourhoods all around the world. With the promise of afforestation at a revolutionary speed, this planting technique has become the darling of green-space enthusiasts, industry, and governments alike — yet few professional or academic ecologists have commented on its efficacy, or even seem to have heard of it!
In this episode, we debate the legacy of Dr. Akira Miyawaki: the man, the myth, and the method.

data.title: New sphere-packing record stems from an unexpected source
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 数学家Boaz Klartag在短短几个月内解决了球体堆积问题的一个重大开放性问题，取得了显著突破。这一问题涉及如何在最小的空间内最有效地堆积球体，尤其在高维度上非常复杂。尽管早期的研究如Hermann Minkowski和Claude Ambrose Rogers提出了不同的方法，但Klartag通过重新审视并改进Rogers的椭球体方法，在任意高维度上实现了更高效的堆积。他的研究复兴了一个被忽视的技术，并可能接近最优解，引起了数学界广泛关注。这一突破结束了该领域多年的停滞，提供了新的研究方向。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：高维空间中的球体堆积问题及其应用和意义

不同观点：
• Someone和theteapot关注高维空间中球体堆积的奇特性质，并强调其数学上的复杂性和难度。Someone提到在高维空间中，即使是最优秀的数学家也只能在100维空间中填充不到1%的体积。
• clickety_clack和fcanesin讨论了数学及相关工作的现实应用和职业发展。clickety_clack强调了向非专业人士解释工作的困难，fcanesin则建议数学家应在相邻领域进行二次博士研究以拓宽知识面。
• Scene_Cast2和dsp_person探讨了球体堆积理论在实际问题中的应用。Scene_Cast2指出理论方法在处理真实数据时效果不佳，而dsp_person则关注其在通信系统中的潜在改进。
• vanderZwan和adityaathalye强调了凸形算法在不同领域中的广泛应用。vanderZwan提到凸包算法在图像处理中的应用，adityaathalye则讨论了LLM技术在跨领域问题解决中的潜力。

补充讨论：
• NooneAtAll3和theteapot提出关于最优球体堆积在不同维度上如何超越已知最佳堆积的问题，显示出对具体维度细节的关注。
• layer8和teleforce提到球体堆积问题在物理学和密码学中的实际应用，强调了其在提高通信系统安全性和能效方面的潜力。
• tomrod和bGl2YW5j表达了对纯数学研究的欣赏和热爱，认为这种研究本身具有价值和吸引力。
• deadbabe提出使用蒙特卡洛方法解决球体堆积问题的可能性，暗示了计算方法在这一领域的潜在应用。
• readthenotes1通过跨学科的例子，强调了跨领域知识在解决复杂问题中的重要性，呼应了adityaathalye的观点。

争议焦点：
• 理论方法在实际应用中的局限性。Scene_Cast2指出理论在高维数据处理中效果不佳，而有些人则认为这些理论在特定应用中仍有巨大潜力（如dsp_person和teleforce的观点）。
• 跨学科知识在解决数学问题中的作用。adityaathalye和readthenotes1认为跨领域知识有助于解决复杂数学问题，而clickety_clack和fcanesin则关注职业发展和专业深度的必要性。

New Sphere-Packing Record Stems From an Unexpected Source
By
Joseph Howlett
July 7, 2025
After just a few months of work, a complete newcomer to the world of sphere packing has solved one of its biggest open problems.
Comment
Save Article
Read Later
DVDP for
Quanta Magazine
Introduction
By
Joseph Howlett
Staff Writer
July 7, 2025
View PDF/Print Mode
geometry
mathematics
randomness
sphere packing
All topics
In math, the search for optimal patterns never ends. The sphere-packing problem — which asks how to cram balls into a (high-dimensional) box as efficiently as possible — is no exception. It has enticed mathematicians for centuries and has important applications in cryptography, long-distance communication and more.
It’s deceptively difficult. In the early 17th century, the physicist Johannes Kepler showed that by stacking three-dimensional spheres the way you would oranges in a grocery store, you can fill about 74% of space. He conjectured that this was the best possible arrangement. But it would take mathematicians nearly 400 years to prove it.
In higher dimensions, mathematicians still don’t know the answer. (With the strange exceptions of
dimensions 8 and 24
.) Over the years, they’ve come up with better packings. But these improvements have been small and relatively rare.
Now, in a
short manuscript
posted online in April, the mathematician
Boaz Klartag
has bested these previous records by a significant margin. Some researchers even believe his result might be close to optimal.
A newcomer to this area of study, Klartag achieved his packing method — which works in all arbitrarily high dimensions — by resuscitating an old technique that experts had abandoned decades earlier. The work taps into several long-running debates about the nature of optimal packings in high dimensions. Should they be ordered or disordered? And how snug can they possibly get?
“This is really an amazing breakthrough,” said
Gil Kalai
, a mathematician at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem. “It’s something that’s excited mathematicians for nearly 100 years.”
Twin Pictures
In 1905, the mathematician Hermann Minkowski established an intuitive way to think about packed spheres. Start with a repeating arrangement of points in space, called a lattice. Then draw a sphere around each point. In this way, the problem of finding an optimal sphere packing in a given dimension actually becomes a problem about finding a lattice whose points are arranged as efficiently as possible. In two dimensions, for instance, the optimal lattice is “hexagonal,” and yields a packing that looks like this:

But in 1947, a mathematician named Claude Ambrose Rogers offered a different perspective. Start with any lattice, he said — even a suboptimal one. Rather than draw a sphere around each point, draw an oblong shape called an ellipsoid around one point, so that its surface touches but doesn’t extend past other points in the lattice.
Rogers came up with an algorithm that used this ellipsoid as a starting point to then construct a dense sphere packing. Here’s how it worked:
The advantage of Rogers’ method was that you didn’t have to start with a particularly efficient lattice to get an efficient sphere packing. You just had to choose the right ellipsoid. But this introduced a new complication. Unlike a sphere, which is completely defined by a single number — its radius — an ellipsoid is defined by several axes of different lengths. The higher the dimension, the greater the number of directions you can stretch your ellipsoid in, and the more options you have for what your starting ellipsoid will look like.
“In higher dimensions, you have no idea how to grow it. You have too much freedom,” Klartag said.
Mathematicians ultimately returned to Minkowski’s approach, choosing to focus on finding the right lattices. They became more specialized in lattice theory and moved away from Rogers’ focus on geometry.
This strategy led to improvements in high-dimensional sphere packing. But for the most part, they only improved on Rogers’ packing by a relatively small margin. Mathematicians still hoped for a bigger leap.
For decades, they didn’t get it. It would take an outsider to end the stagnation.
An Outside Perspective
Klartag, a mathematician at the Weizmann Institute of Science, was always intrigued by lattices and sphere packing. He just never had the time to learn much about them. He works in geometry, not lattice theory, and he usually studies convex shapes — shapes that don’t jut inward. These shapes involve all sorts of symmetries, particularly in high dime

data.title: Tyr, a new Rust DRM driver targeting CSF-based ARM Mali GPUs
data.author: mfilion
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了Collabora开发的全新基于Rust的DRM驱动程序——Tyr，主要针对CSF架构的Arm Mali GPU。Tyr是Panthor（一个成熟的C语言驱动）的Rust移植版本，由Collabora、Arm和Google联合开发。其目标是最终实现与Panthor相同的用户空间API，作为Vulkan驱动PanVK的替代品。尽管Tyr尚处于早期阶段，但Collabora计划在未来几周发布一系列博客文章，详细介绍Tyr的内部工作原理。

当前，Tyr的开发在下游分支进行，以加快原型开发速度。然而，为了避免与上游更改的冲突，Collabora决定将Tyr的部分代码逐步提交到上游。首次提交的代码能够启动GPU并在RK3588系统芯片上探测设备，但完整功能仍需进一步开发。

Collabora希望通过开放开发和与上游社区的合作，推动Rust在Linux内核中的应用和发展。

Introducing Tyr, a new Rust DRM driver
Daniel Almeida
July 07, 2025
Share this post:
Reading time:
The last year has seen substantial progress on the DRM infrastructure required to write GPU drivers in Rust. While a great part of it was fueled by the development of Nova (the new driver for GSP-based NVIDIA GPUs), and by AGX (the driver for the GPUs on Apple's M-series chip that preceded Nova), a few components were being worked on to cater to a then undisclosed driver that was being prototyped behind the scenes. A driver that we now introduce to the community at large in a very early stage.
Tyr is a new Rust-based DRM driver for CSF-based Arm Mali GPUs, making Collabora the first consultancy to formally join the Rust-for-Linux initiative, a testament to our commitment to advancing Rust development within the kernel community. It is a port of Panthor - which is a mature driver written in C for the same hardware - and a joint effort between Collabora, Arm, and Google.
In this sense, Tyr aims to eventually implement the same userspace API offered by Panthor for compatibility reasons, so that it can be used as a drop-in replacement in our Vulkan driver, called PanVK. We foresee Panthor being used - and of course supported - for a relatively long time, as it is a mature driver with a large adoption in the ecosystem. It will probably take a couple of years for Tyr to fully pick up.
Over the course of the next few weeks, we will be releasing a series of blog posts that explain in detail the inner workings of Tyr and its components. This will be a walk-through for GPU drivers on Linux, so stay tuned! For now, we will address why we are submitting a patch to add an initial version of Tyr upstream and what exactly is contained in that submission.
What's the purpose of the current upstream submission?
This question will be easier to answer once we discuss how GPU drivers work. As we uncover the components that make up a kernel-mode driver and how they interact with the rest of the kernel, it will become clear that we simply cannot write a Rust GPU driver with the infrastructure that is currently available upstream. We will discuss, for example, the central role of the Micro Controller Unit (or MCU) within the Arm Mali architecture and then explain why we cannot make it boot without landing some pre-requisite code first, as well as discuss various other components that also cannot be written before landing even more code.
The issues outlined above led us to develop Tyr on a downstream branch. Doing so lets us prototype much faster, which is the reason why we are much further ahead in our downstream code. In fact, we are able to submit small parcels of work to the GPU already.
We will also address this later, but I believe that we will achieve a working driver in our downstream code soon, for a given definition of "working" anyway. In any case, our downstream branch will be invaluable to test the surrounding, work-in-progress code that is needed to support not only Tyr, but also other Rust DRM drivers.
Unfortunately, reconciling the current development model with upstream has been somewhat challenging recently, so a change in the overall strategy that we have been using to develop Tyr was needed.
By submitting small parts of the driver upstream iteratively, we hope to evolve alongside Nova and
rvkms
, which should help us avoid regressions from upstream changes that might otherwise break our code simply because we weren't part of the upstream conversation yet. This approach also lets us prove that work-in-progress abstractions actually function correctly on real hardware with a real driver, rather than just in theory.
Perhaps most importantly, having Tyr as a concrete user of these abstractions gives the community a compelling reason to work on and review them. After all, it's much easier to motivate development when there's an actual driver that depends on the code. Lastly, developing code in the open and with the upstream community also aligns with our philosophy here at Collabora overall.
What's in the current upstream submission?
The
current submission
can power up the GPU and probe the device on an RK3588 system-on-chip. This lets us read a few sections of ROM in the GPU, which in turn lets us provide this information to userspace by means of a
DRM_IOCTL_PANTHOR_DEV_QUERY
call.
This is all that can be done for now, at least until the MCU can be made to work. More on that will be discussed during the subsequent posts.

data.title: How did X-Rays gain mass adoption?
data.author: tinymagician
data.article_summary: X-rays gained mass adoption due to the rapid dissemination of Wilhelm Röntgen's discovery in the late 19th century, with extensive literature and media coverage fueling public interest. Despite initial skepticism and concerns about risks like skin burns, physicians quickly embraced X-rays as a revolutionary diagnostic tool. Early pioneers like William Rollins also addressed safety concerns, contributing to the technology's widespread use. However, challenges such as high costs, image quality issues, and privacy concerns were also raised. The comparison to cell-free DNA technology highlights that new technologies often face similar hurdles, including safety debates and public fascination, which are crucial for driving adoption. Ultimately, X-rays became widely adopted due to their ability to solve practical medical problems and the enthusiasm of early adopters.

How did X-Rays gain mass adoption?
And what we can learn from this process to understand why cell-free DNA adoption has not skyrocketed yet
Adith Arun
Jul 07, 2025
Share this post

At the University of Würzburg, Wilhelm Röntgen took the first X-Ray (XR) and presented his work “
On a New Kind of Rays
” in December 1985 which was printed in January 1986. In January 1986, it was reprinted in English in Nature, The Electrician, Lancet, and BMJ. A lot of literature was written about XR’s in the months to follow.
News outlets
from across the world picked up on this story writing that “a professor from Wurzburg had successfully used a new type of light to take a photograph of a set of weights without opening the wooden box in which the weights were kept” and able to "take a picture of the human hand showing the bones without the flesh”. Critics were loud. Otto Lummer, Rontgen’s colleague, said Rontgen had “
otherwise always been a sensible fellow and it’s not carnival season yet
”. For example, William Morton (US physician and professor of electrotherapeutics) published
The X ray or Photography of the invisible and its value in surgery
. Arthur Wright at Yale
reproduced X-Rays
in January of 1986, Francis William published the
first clinical report
(using some of Edison’s work),
Rontgen published
on better tube design and image quality, and
Tesla
made tweaks to the tube to improve performance. There were 49 monographs and 1044 research papers on XRs in 1896 alone. Physicians championed this. For example, William Stubenbord started using XR techniques in April of 1896 and
presented to his local society in June
. Representative comments include:
At present we can detect deformities in bones and the bony pelvis; we can note the growth of bones and the malacosteon conditions important to the obstetrician; we can clearly see the shoulder-joint, the ribs, the vertebrae, the union of the pubes, the hip-joint and the curvatures of the spine. We can describe fractures of bones and readily distinguish them from dislocations, determine how to set them, and even watch their reunion without removing the splints and bandages. We can watch the absorption of a bone and readily find imbedded foreign substances. We can detect the presence of puss, watch the heart beating, see the form of the liver, the lungs, the kidneys and the spleen. I have seen with the fluoroscope the fetus in utero at the seventh month.
What is required are Crookes' tubes, a Ruhmkorff coil or a static machine, a fluoroscope, plate-holder, sensitized plates and other photographic apparatus. ... The expense of the machine costs only about $400 while a good coil is valued at from $200 to $600. But, of course, this need not be considered by physicians, since all are wealthy
This Substack is reader-supported. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.
Subscribe
These comments represent the instant click that many physicians felt when working with and look at XRs. It was a tool to answer their own personal curiosities about the human body and get answers to questions they spent much time thinking about and treating. And, for physicians like Stubenbord, they did not think about XRs in terms of return on investment - they had the money and this was a cool tool to try out at the very least.
During the initial wave of XR interest, there were physicians and scientists thinking about the risks associated with XRs too. Exceedingly painful
dermatitis (more like a severe burn) caused by XR
use was described in 1896.
Codman
(MGH surgeon) recognized the potential for XR to diagnose and study injuries and disease though he also paid close attention to reported injuries. In 1896, 55 were reported but by 1901 only 1 was reported. He felt the decline in reported occurred because people chose not to publish unless they exhibited unusual features, a reasonable conclusion.
William Rollins
(scientist and dentist) published over 200 papers from 1896-1903 urging minimum exposure, lead enclosures, and goggles to minimize risks. He became the father of radiation protection.
Radiologist Alan Hart and others
criticized XRs as “large loud sparking smelly devices prone to mishap and injury even when fully under the control of the physicians who in droves invested money and prestige in them”.
Some surgeons
doubted the image quality, felt bullet could be left safely in the body, and worried about patient privacy (seeing through clothes). The public was fascinated by this technology and studios offered the public “views of their bones” and “shoe fitting” images. These developments are expected of any new technology and necessary for its rapid adoption. data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕《侏罗纪公园》系列电影的评论和分析，包括电影制作的细节、科学性、情感共鸣以及与后续电影的对比。

不同观点：
• LeftHandPath认为，斯皮尔伯格的原作通过详尽的细节描绘，如琥珀的来源、多学科专家的参与、天气影响以及员工的互动和挫折，营造了一个更真实、有生命力的公园。而后的电影则缺乏这种深度，直接呈现一个已经运行的公园，缺少对创建过程的挣扎和 triumph 的刻画。

• nullhole引用了Ebert的观点，指出原作中对恐龙首次出现的场景充满了敬畏和奇迹感，而后续电影则更多地转向了标准的怪物电影模式，缺乏原作的宏伟感。

• conductr分享了个人经历，反映出公众对恐龙灭绝原因的认知随着时间推移发生了变化，强调了科学知识的不断更新。

• yeahboats指出，新的《侏罗纪》电影缺乏原作的灵魂和角色的深度，更多地依赖CGI技术，并认为原作因其开创性而成为标杆。

• csours赞赏《侏罗纪公园》的开场镜头和Mr. DNA的技术解说场景，认为这些是电影中出色的技术表现。

• OJFord认为，《侏罗纪》系列是唯一适合成年人的恐龙故事，因为其他可能的恐龙故事无法在现代电影制作中获得足够的预算和对话。

• Reason077讨论了电影中关于恐龙捕猎的科学准确性问题，指出古代捕食者的视觉和行为可能与现代鸟类不同。

• euparkeria质疑为何好的恐龙电影如此稀少，相比之下僵尸电影却很多，尽管概念简单。

• throw7怀念旧电影中的经典台词，认为现代电影缺乏这样的 memorable moments。

• bruce511对Ian Malcolm角色的复杂性和Jeff Goldblum的演绎表示赞赏，认为其在电影中的台词具有深刻的哲理。

• jtrn批评文章本身重复了陈词滥调，认为文章指责好莱坞失去创新能力的同时自己也缺乏新意。

• zhynn推荐了Abby Howard的《Earth Before Us》系列书籍，认为这些书籍在科学性和故事性上都非常出色。

• sdsd享受与孩子一起观看恐龙电影的体验，认为这种电影对孩子来说已经是巅峰之作，并反对将恐龙电影过度艺术化。

补充讨论：
• 科学知识的更新和公众认知的变化是一个值得注意的讨论点，conductr和jxjnskkzxxhx都提到了这一点。
• 原作与续作在情感共鸣和科学细节上的对比是讨论的核心，LeftHandPath和nullhole的观点最具代表性。
• 对电影技术的赞赏和批评，如csours和yeahboats的看法，也反映了观众对电影制作的不同期望。
• 对恐龙电影的个人体验和情感联结，如bruce511和sdsd的分享，提供了对观众多样化视角的洞察。

• OJFord认为，《侏罗纪》系列是唯一适合成年人的恐龙故事，因为其他可能的恐龙故事无法在现代电影制作中获得足够的预算和对话。

• Reason077讨论了电影中关于恐龙捕猎的科学准确性问题，指出古代捕食者的视觉和行为可能与现代鸟类不同。

• euparkeria质疑为何好的恐龙电影如此稀少，相比之下僵尸电影却很多，尽管概念简单。

• throw7怀念旧电影中的经典台词，认为现代电影缺乏这样的 memorable moments。

• bruce511对Ian Malcolm角色的复杂性和Jeff Goldblum的演绎表示赞赏，认为其在电影中的台词具有深刻的哲理。

• jtrn批评文章本身重复了陈词滥调，认为文章指责好莱坞失去创新能力的同时自己也缺乏新意。

• zhynn推荐了Abby Howard的《Earth Before Us》系列书籍，认为这些书籍在科学性和故事性上都非常出色。

• sdsd享受与孩子一起观看恐龙电影的体验，认为这种电影对孩子来说已经是巅峰之作，并反对将恐龙电影过度艺术化。

补充讨论：
• 科学知识的更新和公众认知的变化是一个值得注意的讨论点，conductr和jxjnskkzxxhx都提到了这一点。
• 原作与续作在情感共鸣和科学细节上的对比是讨论的核心，LeftHandPath和nullhole的观点最具代表性。
• 对电影技术的赞赏和批评，如csours和yeahboats的看法，也反映了观众对电影制作的不同期望。
• 对恐龙电影的个人体验和情感联结，如bruce511和sdsd的分享，提供了对观众多样化视角的洞察。

data.title: Show HN: I Got Tired of Calculator Sites, So I Built My Own
data.author: calculatehow
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：在线计算器的功能、用户界面（UI）设计、用户体验（UX）及其多样化应用

不同观点：
• kstrauser认为贷款计算器的上限设置在50%不合理，特别是对于那些需要简化界面但可能无法自己进行复杂计算的人来说。他举例说明了高风险贷款的危害，并强调这些人最需要看到明确的数字来避免被掠夺性贷款所害。
• flysand7关注计算器的多功能性，尤其是单位和进制转换功能。他建议通过侧边栏或类似UI设计来方便地切换不同类型的计算器，并保存状态，以便用户在多个计算之间轻松切换。
• zahirbmirza提出了一种UI设计建议，建议在页面顶部自动加载常用计算器，以减少用户导航的需求，从而提高使用便捷性。
• Workaccount2认为现代语音助手（如Google）已经使得在线计算器变得不再必要，特别是对于复杂的自定义计算。他们强调通过语音指令可以快速获得答案并生成动态小程序。
• t_mann对传统计算器UI在移动设备上的使用体验持积极态度，并认为许多功能可以合并到少数几个应用程序中，如科学计算、财务计算和单位转换等。
• lukaslukas赞赏该项目无广告和无追踪，并希望保持这种状态，同时提到自己因类似原因创建了一个字符串处理工具。
• divbzero提供了一个具体的UI反馈，建议在iPhone上使用时，即使显示数字键盘，页面也应可滚动，以改善用户体验。
• FerkiHN认为计算器功能过多，建议增加搜索功能和更直观的文档说明，以便新手更容易使用。
• darmon333简单地推荐了另一个时间计算器网站。
• forty提出了在Android上的一个用户体验问题，建议通过添加历史记录元素来使返回按钮能够隐藏键盘，以符合用户习惯。
• GuB-42赞赏网站的速度和优化，认为无广告和追踪器是快速加载的重要因素。
• Splizard请求添加对双工数（duplex numbers）的支持。
• pineaux以半开玩笑的方式建议完美的计算器应由大型语言模型（LLM）或类似Wolfram Alpha的工具实现，但同时也希望看到一个带有标签切换功能的常规计算器。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是计算器的功能数量和UI设计的便捷性。部分用户希望功能更加集中和简化，而另一些用户则希望看到更多高级功能。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是现代技术（如语音助手和LLM）对传统在线计算器的冲击和替代作用。
• 用户体验和界面设计是另一个被广泛讨论的主题，特别是如何在不同设备和情境下优化使用体验。

data.title: I am uninstalling AI coding assistants from my personal computer
data.author: ssutch3
data.article_summary: 作者描述了过去五个月依赖AI编程助手的经历。起初，这种借助AI快速生成代码的方式让他感到非常高效和兴奋，仿佛找到了“毒品”般的快感，尤其在开发自己创业项目Roam时。然而，几个月后，他开始感到不满和空虚，意识到自己已经很久没有亲手写代码了。对他来说，编码不仅是生产力工具，更是一种艺术表达和与他人连接的方式。虽然AI工具在职业环境中不可避免，但作者决定在个人项目中放弃使用AI，回归亲手 coding 的方式，以找回创作的满足感。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI工具在创作和编程中的使用及其影响

不同观点：
• Mouvelie认为，创造的核心在于创作者在创作过程中的参与和体验，而不仅仅是最终的结果。他强调了创作过程的重要性，并认为使用AI工具可能会让人感到空虚，因为创作者在作品中的直接贡献减少了。

• Macha指出，许多传统艺术家对AI工具持敌对态度，尤其是那些已经在艺术领域挣扎求生的艺术家。她认为，经济利益并不是这些艺术家采用AI的主要动力，因为他们关注的并不是提高生产量，而是创作本身的价值。

• Jotalea分享了自己对AI工具上瘾的个人经历，他表示过度依赖AI工具导致自己的编程技能退化，感到被困住且无用。他尝试过重新手动编程，但发现自己已经无法脱离AI工具。

• bluefirebrand表达了对AI工具的极度不满，他无法从这些工具中获得与他人相同的好处，每次使用生成的代码都需要大量修改，甚至无法运行。这让他感到极度沮丧，认为自己在职业生涯中正在落后。

• breckenedge描述了一个相对平衡的视角，他的工作环境中有管理者对AI工作流持怀疑态度，且同事间对AI工具的使用存在分歧。他本人广泛使用AI工具，但受限于工具的速率限制，有时仍需手动完成工作。

• randomNumber7认为，随着编程技能的提升，程序员会看到当前AI辅助工具的局限性。他建议，为了提升技能，编程和阅读书籍是必要的，但这也可能让编程工作变得不再那么有趣。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点在于AI工具是否真正提高了生产力以及其对个人技能发展的影响。一些人认为AI工具带来了便利和效率，而另一些人则认为这些工具导致技能退化和职业不满。
- 讨论中还涉及到经济因素对采用AI工具的影响，特别是在不同职业和技能水平的人群中，这种影响有所不同。
- 个人经验和感受在讨论中占据重要位置，不同用户对AI工具的体验和看法各异，反映出对技术工具的复杂态度。

44493503.article_content:
For the past five months I have been coding almost exclusively with AI coding assistants, and I am worried how it has affected my psychology. First, some quick backstory.
While taking an extended “break” from a 9-5 job, I started
Roam
, a social network focused on off road exploration in vehicles. It’s like Strava but for things you do in your car. This is an idea I had last winter and decided to dedicate a few months to hammering out a proof of concept. So from February until late June I have been working nearly every day on Roam, almost exclusively with AI assistance.
I’m not alone. Before I left Coinbase, the culture was already shifting to where we were expected to work this way. As I have kept up conversation with my developer friends, it has become essentially the norm, and everyone is being pressed to find greater productivity using AI coding tools.
Now, to a serial startup founder like myself, the velocity with which you can vomit out code with AI assistance is like a powerful, habit-forming drug. In February, when Claude Code beta was released, it was like I had found crack cocaine for the first time. My daily binge would consist of visualizing product features and then seeing it materialize in front of my eyes in record speed. I think the kids refer to this as vibe coding. The feeling of momentum propells you along in an unstoppable rage of coding.
If you’re an experienced coder, somewhat discerning, familiar with your language, framework, and intimately in touch with your goals, this working style can be surprisingly sustainable. The output is usable in production and not
total
garbage.
However, after a few months of working like this I began to get very discontent with coding. It was hard to debug exactly why, because from the outside I was living my dream: working on a startup, in a domain that I liked, at breakneck pace, able to grind through relatively immense scope without outside help.
Last week I realized that I had not actually written a line of code myself in weeks. If I wanted to I could go days without even opening an editor, instead just reviewing and refining diffs with Claude Code in the terminal. Iterating endlessly with a bot which would tirelessly generate the code for me for the low, low fee of $200 per month.
I have always held the belief, right or wrong, that coding is an expression of my inner world. In other words, art. It’s represents core values of my personality – curiosity, love of problem solving, belief in stewardship and craft. And, because I’m broken in certain ways, it’s also a way that I’ve learned to connect
with real people
. My very first online friend as a teen was someone with whom I practiced coding.
Fortunately for my career, at some point along the line, I was able to translate coding into “software engineering.” The concurrence of a sustainable living with the ability to produce art (if not every day, frequently enough to keep me sane) has kept my psychology content and happy for quite a while, until recently. It turns out that initial rush of being able to produce code at breakneck speeds was more of a bubble than real life. Now that the bubble has popped, it’s left me feeling a great emptiness.
I wonder if some “actual" artists (as in, those people who create the kind of art most people would recognize) have gone through a similar arc of realizing the emptiness of creating with AI tools. Certainly some writers have. Regardless, the lesson for people like myself is that, in order to feel happy with creating, we have to actually create. An artist would not call their work art if they had little to no role in creating it.
Therefore I am uninstalling Claude Code and its ilk from my personal computer. Of course, now that the genie is out of the bottle within the IT industry, and pretty much everywhere else, you and I have no choice but to utilize these tools in our professional lives. Adapt or die. There's no going back. But for personal projects—Roam, open source projects, personal utilities and scripts—those will continue to be written by hand like I always have.
From brain to fingers to compiler. Test, debug, and repeat.

data.title: AI cameras change driver behavior at intersections
data.author: sohkamyung
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了人工智能（AI）摄像头在交通路口对驾驶员行为的改变及其潜在影响。这些摄像头能够实时监控和分析交通状况，通过警示系统或罚款机制减少闯红灯和超速等违规行为。作者指出，这些AI技术的应用有望降低交通事故死亡率，尤其是在高风险路口。尽管技术带来隐私担忧，但其安全效益不可忽视。文章强调，随着技术进步，AI在交通安全中的角色将愈加重要。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：交通执法、滚停（rolling stop）的合法性和安全性、交通基础设施设计与技术应用

不同观点：
• **支持滚停的观点**：SoftTalker认为在视线良好且没有行人或交叉交通的情况下，滚停并无不妥。其核心论据是，交通标志的目的是确保安全有序的交通流动，如果司机减速并确认安全，即使没有完全停下，目的也已经达到。

• **交通执法与安全比较的观点**：maeln指出美国交通事故死亡率远高于欧盟，表明需要对交通执法、基础设施设计和司机心态进行改革，暗示严格执法可能是必要的。

• **交通灯和交通流量管理的观点**：hlws提到交通灯不仅是为安全设计，也是为交通流量管理服务。在其居住地，许多司机将红灯视为建议而非强制，导致其他街道的严重堵塞问题。

• **技术替代与交通设计的观点**：grogenaut建议利用技术，如车内提示灯或智能交通灯，以替代传统的停车标志，从而更有效地管理交通流量，并减少对司机的干扰。

• **执法公平性与社会问题的观点**：pj_mukh指出其城市对无牌车辆缺乏执法，导致社会问题如肇事逃逸频发，质疑交通执法摄像头的实际效果和社会公平性。

• **"零愿景"目标的现实性观点**：SoftTalker对"零愿景"（Vision Zero）持怀疑态度，认为完全消除交通死亡是不现实的目标，资源分配应更加合理。

• **自动化执法的可行性观点**：djoldman认为技术并非推行自动化交通执法的障碍，而是公众接受度和运营成本问题。

• **历史经验与执法成本的观点**：mullingitover提到过去加州因运营成本高而放弃自动化交通执法系统，指出人类参与审核可降低误报率，但增加运营费用。

• **执法动机与长期影响的观点**：thrill和JohnMakin都质疑执法背后的动机，认为一旦某种执法手段成为收入来源，其废除将面临困难，且可能被滥用于其他目的，如数据收集和监控。

• **交通控制设备的实际效果与安全问题观点**：mindslight批评严格执行交通控制设备的“安全”措施，认为其分散司机注意力，可能导致更多事故，并指出改造交叉路口的昂贵成本。

补充讨论：
• **执法对驾驶行为的影响**：webdevver提到警察在场时司机行为的变化，暗示执法可能导致不必要的交通减速。

• **执法设备的真实目的**：chasd00直接质疑执法设备的真实目的，认为其主要是为了增加罚单收入而非提升交通安全。

争议的焦点：
• **滚停的合法性与安全性**：是否在特定条件下允许滚停，以及如何平衡司机便利性和交通安全。

• **交通基础设施设计的成本与效果**：是否应投资改造现有交通基础设施以提升安全性与效率，还是依赖技术手段解决。

这些观点和讨论展示了交通执法、技术应用和基础设施设计之间的复杂关系，以及公众对交通安全和管理措施的不同看法。

data.title: My app charted on the App Store, and that sucked
data.author: isntThatSth
data.article_summary: 本文作者分享了自己开发的付费应用在丹麦App Store生活方式类别中获得第15名的心得，尽管仅获得了四次下载。这揭示了付费应用市场的低迷，特别是在较小的市场如丹麦。作者尝试了有机搜索和苹果广告等推广方式，但效果不佳。作者认为，四次下载就能上榜反映出付费应用下载量极低，对付费应用市场的可行性感到怀疑。尽管如此，作者仍认为付费应用更诚实透明，用户不必担心应用内购买或订阅。作者对是否应继续努力增加下载量持怀疑态度，但承认可能需要调整策略。最终，作者提问这种下载量是否在付费应用中常见，并邀请读者在Hacker News上讨论。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：应用程序的付费模式和应用商店的整体质量

不同观点：
• joshstrange 支持付费下载模式，认为这种模式更诚实和直接。他指出，提前收费可以让用户避免在使用过程中遇到付费升级或订阅的困扰。他还提到，内购（IAP）如果是用于解锁完整版、去除广告或一次性购买等明确选项，是可以接受的，但不应采用如100宝石或订阅等模糊方式。

• paxys 则支持免费试用后付费解锁的模式，认为这种模式更透明和诚实，可以让用户在付费前了解应用的内容和功能，避免盲目付费。

• andrewmcwatters 对整个应用商店的应用质量提出批评，认为大多数非大型企业的应用程序质量低劣，充斥着山寨产品。他引用Schiller的观点，认为应用商店本应提供高质量的体验，但实际上却像一个低质量的市场。他建议不要在应用商店发布应用。

补充讨论：
• joshstrange 强调了付费模式中内购选项的透明性，提出了用户对付费内容的期望。
• paxys 提出了免费试用后付费的模式，关注用户的知情权和选择权。
• andrewmcwatters 对整个应用商店生态系统提出了广泛的批评，认为即使是大型公司的应用程序质量也仅因为设计指南的遵循而勉强合格。

争议焦点：
• 不同付费模式的透明性和诚实性是讨论的焦点，joshstrange和paxys对此持不同看法。
• 整个应用商店的应用质量和生态系统的健康度也是争议的一个重要方面，andrewmcwatters对应用商店的批评引发了对应用程序质量的广泛讨论。

44493531.article_content:
My app charted on the App Store, and that sucked!
Reading the headline you're probably thinking that my app got popular and the backend couldn't
handle the pressure, leading to thousands of unsatisfied users.
I wish that were the case. In reality, my app got four downloads. Not 400,000. Not 4,000.
Four! And that, apparently, was enough to briefly get
the app
on the
App Store charts as #15.
Granted, this was in a specific category (paid apps in the Lifestyle category in the Danish version of the App Store).
However, the fact that just four downloads is enough to get to #15 in a specific category in Denmark seems to
suggest that the number of people who are willing to pay to download apps (as supposed to making an in-app purchase
in a "free" app) is shockingly low, even for the relatively small market that is Denmark.
It is of course entirely possible that the apps that are in the top ten in the Lifestyle category make bank - but
it's not likely if just four downloads is enough to get you to #15 on the chart.
So what's the lesson here for new app developers? Well, organic search in the App Store has yielded zero downloads
of the app. Same thing goes for Apple Ads Basic, and even a relatively large number of press releases has yielded
zero results.
So the lesson, of course, is to give up! Nah, maybe not, and I'm sure a ton of things could be tweaked
in order to increase the number of downloads. But the whole thing does make me sceptical as to whether it's
actually possible to get a decent number of downloads if you're going the paid-apps route. It's not so much
the fact that my app doesn't get that many downloads - that can probably be explained by my poor marketing skills.
It's the fact that just four downloads get you on the charts, which would suggest very, very few people download
paid apps.
The reason I chose
to make
Danish Names
a paid app from the beginning was simply that I think
it's a lot more honest and upfront to charge a small one-time fee before the download, as opposed to claiming your
app is free and then charging a high fee or even a subscription inside the app. There's an honesty and
straight-forwardness to paid apps that I like: You pay once, and then you don't get bothered with requests
for paid upgrades when you're using the app.
Are these kinds of download numbers for paid apps common?
Discuss on Hacker News
.

data.title: Jack Dorsey launches a WhatsApp messaging rival built on Bluetooth
data.author: rmason
data.article_summary: Twitter联合创始人杰克·多尔西推出了一款全新的点对点 messaging app，名为Bitchat，完全通过蓝牙运作，支持加密、消息阅后即焚，且不涉及账户、电话号码或服务器。该应用目前已在TestFlight上进行beta测试，未来更新将加入WiFi Direct以提升通信速度和范围。Bitchat旨在实现去中心化和抗审查，即使在没有互联网、Wi-Fi或手机服务的情况下，也能通过蓝牙网格网络传递消息。消息仅存储在设备上，不依赖中心化基础设施，体现了多尔西对隐私保护和去中心化通信的长期追求。未来还将支持群聊和密码保护等功能。

Key Points
Twitter co-founder Jack Dorsey announced a new peer-to-peer messaging app that works entirely over Bluetooth.
Chats are encrypted, ephemeral and stored only on-device — with no accounts, phone numbers, or servers involved.
The app is now live in beta on TestFlight, with future updates set to add WiFi Direct for faster, longer-range communication.
Twitter CEO Jack Dorsey testifies during a remote video hearing held by subcommittees of the U.S. House of Representatives Energy and Commerce Committee on "Social Media's Role in Promoting Extremism and Misinformation" in Washington, March 25, 2021.
CNBC
Block
CEO Jack Dorsey spent the weekend building Bitchat, a new decentralized, peer-to-peer messaging app that works entirely over Bluetooth mesh networks, with no internet, central servers, phone numbers or emails required.
The Twitter co-founder announced Sunday that the beta version is live on
TestFlight
, with a full white paper available on
GitHub
.
In a
post on X
Sunday, Dorsey called it a personal experiment in "bluetooth mesh networks, relays and store and forward models, message encryption models, and a few other things."
Bitchat enables ephemeral, encrypted communication between nearby devices. As users move through physical space, their phones form local Bluetooth clusters and pass messages from device to device, allowing them to reach peers beyond standard range — even without Wi-Fi or cell service.
Certain "bridge" devices connect overlapping clusters, expanding the mesh across greater distances. Messages are stored only on device, disappear by default and never touch centralized infrastructure — echoing Dorsey's long-running push for privacy-preserving, censorship-resistant communication.

The launch builds on his
support of Damus and Bluesky
and reflects a broader campaign to decentralize everything from social media to payments.
Like the Bluetooth-based apps used during
Hong Kong's 2019 protests
, Bitchat is designed to keep working even when the internet is blocked, offering a censorship-resistant way to stay connected during outages, shutdowns or surveillance.
The app also supports optional group chats, or "rooms," which can be named with hashtags and protected by passwords. It includes store and forward functionality to deliver messages to users who are temporarily offline.
A future update will add WiFi Direct to increase speed and range, pushing Dorsey's vision for off-grid, user-owned communication even further.

data.comments_summary:

不同观点：
• [paxys] 的观点：质疑将不发放股息的做法称为"避税手段"是否恰当。他认为不发放股息可能只是一种财务策略，未必等同于避税。
   
• [fred_is_fred] 的观点：他指出这种做法可能是将股息收入转换为资本收益（或损失）的一种方式，通过出售资产来实现。同时，他提到如果投资者持有S&P500成分股足够长的时间，很多股息已经是合格股息（qualified dividends），其税率可能低于普通收入税率。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：是否将不发放股息视为避税手段。paxys认为这种做法不一定与避税有关，而fred_is_fred则在探讨这种做法是否会改变收入性质，从而影响税负。
   
• 税收差异：fred_is_fred提到了合格股息的税收优惠，这表明他对比了股息收入和资本收益的税收待遇，并认为持有股票足够长时间可以享受较低的税率。

44493825.article_content:
Wall Street Builds S&P 500 ‘No Dividend’ Fund in New Tax Dodge
Vildana Hajric
Mon, Jul 7, 2025, 11:04 AM
4 min read
In This Article:
^GSPC
^SPX
(Bloomberg) -- Wall Street’s latest tax dodge doesn’t hide in the Cayman Islands or rely on complex derivatives. It’s engineered to turn a publicly traded fund into a tax-minimizing machine that hums quietly on autopilot.
Most Read from Bloomberg
Are Tourists Ruining Europe? How Locals Are Pushing Back
Foreign Buyers Swoop on Cape Town Homes, Pricing Out Locals
Trump’s Gilded Design Style May Be Gaudy. But Don’t Call it ‘Rococo.’
Denver City Hall Takes a Page From NASA
In California, Pro-Housing ‘Abundance’ Fans Rewrite an Environmental Landmark
While dividends have long been a defining feature of stock investing — a sign of corporate discipline and investor reward — Roundhill Investments plans to launch the S&P 500 No Dividend Target exchange-traded fund on July 10 with the ticker XDIV. Its ambition is simple but strategic: track the performance of the famous benchmark while dodging its payouts. The fund will sell holdings just before their dividend dates — steering income away from ETF shareholders and, in the process, away from their tax bills.
As stock benchmarks have climbed in recent years and tax bills have grown alongside them, asset managers are building products that give investors more control over when — and whether — they owe taxes. These rely on sophisticated mechanisms to reduce taxable events, essentially transforming the fund structure into a programmable tax-sensitive tool.
These strategies are executed through US-regulated ETFs that trade on public exchanges, offering investors easy access and the kind of fiscal flexibility once reserved for private wealth clients.
It’s “for people who are tax-aware — intended for people who want to have S&P 500 exposure without the downside of distributions,” said Dave Mazza, chief executive officer at Roundhill. “There hasn’t been a product in the market to meet the needs of investors for this.”
While most ETFs already sidestep capital gains by using a mechanism known as in-kind redemptions, XDIV’s strategy takes aim at a different category of tax exposure: ordinary income. The fund, which will charge a 0.0849% fee at the start, will invest in other S&P 500 ETFs, such as Vanguard’s VOO, but will exit positions just before ex-dividend dates. It will then rotate from one such index fund into another that isn’t about to pay a distribution.
That could appeal to clients who don’t reinvest payouts consistently — which can be a drag on performance — or high earners seeking to limit taxable income in brokerage accounts.
“There are certain investors who don’t want taxable income — there’s institutional investors who only want the total return for an investment,” Mazza said. “Then, there’s tax-aware mom-and-pop investors who are focused on long-term compounding, but they don’t want to receive current income because that means their total income — even if it’s modest compared to what they may be making from their compensation — is still going to be taxable.”
Story Continues
Skipping the dividend isn’t an own goal. When a company pays out cash to shareholders, its stock typically falls by the same amount, so by selling just before that moment, the ETF gives up the payout but also sidesteps the price dip. In other words, the value of the trade should net out, the thinking goes. What changes is how — and when — investors owe taxes.
XDIV joins a growing wave of tax-optimized offerings. Others, like the Burney US Factor Rotation ETF, convert entire portfolios into the wrapper without triggering a taxable event. Cambria’s Tax Aware ETF, meanwhile, seeded its portfolio with appreciated stocks, allowing investors to swap exposures without formally realizing gains.
And more products that hew to this idea could come to market soon. A firm named LionShares LLC in mid-June filed for an ETF that would invest in other ETFs tracking the large-cap US equity market, but would at the same time look to “minimize” distributions, according to its paperwork. Earlier, F/m Investments, a Washington DC-based asset manager with a growing ETF lineup, filed for a number of new bond products that would swap between different holdings in order to dodge dividend payouts, something that industry veteran Dave Nadig dubbed “clever.”
“The ability of ETFs to sidestep capital gains isn’t just a technical quirk anymore — it’s a core selling point, and issuers are leaning into this edge,” said Athanasios Psarofagis, ETF analyst at Bloomberg Intelligence.
--With assistance from Justina Lee.
