data.title: Get the location of the ISS using DNS
data.author: 8organicbits
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了如何利用DNS的LOC记录来获取国际空间站（ISS）的实时位置。作者通过一个自定义域名（where-is-the-iss.dedyn.io）和第三方API（N2YO）实现这一功能。每15分钟更新一次DNS记录，以确保位置信息的准确性。具体操作包括将ISS的经纬度和海拔高度转换为DNS LOC记录所需的格式，并使用deSEC提供的API进行更新。该项目展示了DNS可以用于存储和分发一些不太可能的数据，如ISS的位置信息。文章还提到目前Windows系统不支持通过PowerShell或命令提示符查询LOC记录。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过DNS记录查询国际空间站（ISS）位置的技术实现及其局限性

不同观点：
• [theobeers] 介绍了通过NAPTR记录查询ISS位置的具体技术实现，包括查询结果中包含的休斯顿约翰逊航天中心的电话号码。这展示了DNS记录的实际应用。
• [kmm] 提出ISS的轨道速度与数据更新频率（15分钟）之间的差距，认为这会导致位置误差大约为地球周长的十二分之一，约等于里斯本到伊斯坦布尔的距离。这指出了当前实现的潜在不足。
• [TMEHpodcast] 认为该技术非常聪明且具有教育意义，但指出由于DNS LOC记录的限制，无法用于表示像詹姆斯·韦伯太空望远镜（JWST）这样距离更远的物体，并建议考虑哈勃望远镜。
• [pul] 提出了一种更复杂但更高效的方法，通过设置NS记录并运行程序来动态响应DNS查询，以解决API限流问题。虽然不完全符合DNS规范，但足以满足此用例。
• [selcuka] 提到RFC 1876作为一个长期实验的标准，质疑其持续的适用性，并引用1996年的资料支持讨论。
• [pvtmert] 强调DNS基础设施本身通过TTL值进行缓存的功能，并指出大型公共DNS解析器（如Cloudflare和Google）的存在，认为DNS是一个全球数据库，具有最终一致性，适合存储临时数据。

补充讨论：
• [verytrivial] 和 [ygritte] 的评论带有幽默性质，[verytrivial] 提到对DNS内容的误读，[ygritte] 则用幽默方式提到了海森堡不确定性原理。
• [knadh] 和 [ritcgab] 提到了该技术在实际应用中的潜力，如[knadh] 提到的dns.toys项目和[ritcgab] 对DNS系统特性的总结。
• [jamesgill] 提供了另一个资源OpenNotify作为参考，指出其虽然功能有限，但也是一种可用的选择。
• [huslage] 建议通过实时计算星历数据来获取ISS位置，以提高数据的实时性。

争议焦点：
• 主要集中在数据更新频率（15分钟）是否足够及时以准确反映ISS的位置，以及DNS记录的局限性是否影响该技术的广泛应用。

这些观点展示了技术实现的多样性以及在应用DNS记录查询ISS位置时所面临的实际问题和解决方案。

44480223.article_content:
I love DNS esoterica. Weird little things that you can shove in the global directory to be distributed around the world instantly(ish).
Domain names, like
www.example.com
usually resolve to servers. As much as we think of "the cloud" as being some intangible morass of ethereal Turing-machines floating in probability space, the more prosaic reality is that they're just boxen in data centres. They have a physical location.
Got a tricky machine which is playing silly-buggers? Wouldn't it be nice to know exactly where it is? That way you can visit and give it some
percussive maintenance
.
Enter the DNS LOC record!
The snappily titled
RFC 1876
is an
experimental
standard. It allows you to create a DNS record which specifies the latitude and longitude of your server. Of course, some data-centres are very tall and some are underground. So it also contains an altitude parameter.
The standard allows for a minimum altitude of -100,000 metres - deep enough for any bunker! The maximum altitude is 42,849,672 metres which is high enough to allow it to be used on
satellites in geostationary orbit
.
So, as a bit of fun, I decided to create
where-is-the-iss.dedyn.io
It isn't a website. You can't ping it. There's no way to interact with it
except
by using DNS.  Yup! You can use a DNS query to get the (approximate) location of the International Space Station!
Linux and Mac users
0
can run:
dig where-is-the-iss.dedyn.io LOC
And receive back the latest position of the ISS:
;; ANSWER SECTION:
where-is-the-iss.dedyn.io. 1066 IN  LOC 47 24 53.500 N 66 12 12.070 W 430520m 10000m 10000m 10000m
The DNS records are updated every 15 minutes on a best-effort basis
1
.
How
The lovely people at
N2YO
have a website which allows you to track
loads
of objects in orbit.  They also have an
easy to use API
with a generous free tier.
Calling
https://api.n2yo.com/rest/v1/satellite/positions/25544/0/0/0/1/&apiKey=_____
gets back the latest position:
JSON
{
"info"
:
{
"satname"
:
"SPACE STATION"
,
"satid"
: 25544,
"transactionscount"
: 7
}
,
"positions"
:
[
{
"satlatitude"
: -21.25409321,
"satlongitude"
: 140.3335763,
"sataltitude"
: 420.09,
"azimuth"
: 292.92,
"elevation"
: -70.95,
"ra"
: 202.69300845,
"dec"
: -32.16097472,
"timestamp"
: 1751366048,
"eclipsed"
: true
}
]
}
Note that the altitude is in Km, whereas the LOC format requires m.
The latitude and longitude are in decimal format - they need to be converted to Degrees, Minutes, and Seconds.
There were only a few free domain name providers who offer an API for updating LOC records.  I went for
deSEC
a charity from Berlin. They have
comprehensive API documentation
.
Adding the initial LOC record is done with:
Bash
curl https://desec.io/api/v1/domains/where-is-the-iss.dedyn.io/rrsets/ \
--header "Authorization: Token _______" \
--header "Content-Type: application/json" --data @- <<< \
'{"type": "LOC", "records": ["40 16 25.712 S 29 32 36.243 W 427550m 0.00m 10000m 10m"], "ttl": 900}'
However, updating the record is a little trickier. it needs to be sent as an
HTTP PATCH
to a subtly different URl. The PATCH only needs to send the data which have changed.
Bash
curl -X PATCH https://desec.io/api/v1/domains/where-is-the-iss.dedyn.io/rrsets/@/LOC/ \
--header "Authorization: Token _______" \
--header "Content-Type: application/json" --data @- <<< \
'{"records": ["40 16 25.712 S 29 32 36.243 W 427550m 0.00m 10000m 10m"]}'
I set the
Time To Live
at 900 seconds. Every 15 minutes my code runs to update the record
2
. That keeps me well within the API limits for both services.  I could add TXT records showing when it was last updated, or other sorts of unstructured data, but I think this is enough for a quick proof-of-concept.
There you have it! A complex and silly way to demonstrate how DNS can be used to hold the most unlikely of records
3
.  Say, I wonder how you'd represent the co-ordinates of the Mars Rover…?
Further Reading
For more DNS weirdness, please see my other posts:
BIMI - SVG in DNS TXT WTF?!
Why you can't dig Switzerland
I don't think there's a way for Windows users to look up LOC records using PowerShell or the Command Prompt.
↩︎
Look, I'm not NASA, OK? If you're using this to help you dock then I cannot be held responsible.
↩︎
I suppose you could build an API with unlimited request limits by distributing data via DNS TXT records. Would best suit static or infrequently updating data. Push it once to DNS and let everyone query it semi-locally.
↩︎
See if you can find the other interesting record I've added to DNS!
↩︎

补充讨论：
• [verytrivial] 和 [ygritte] 的评论带有幽默性质，[verytrivial] 提到对DNS内容的误读，[ygritte] 则用幽默方式提到了海森堡不确定性原理。
• [knadh] 和 [ritcgab] 提到了该技术在实际应用中的潜力，如[knadh] 提到的dns.toys项目和[ritcgab] 对DNS系统特性的总结。
• [jamesgill] 提供了另一个资源OpenNotify作为参考，指出其虽然功能有限，但也是一种可用的选择。
• [huslage] 建议通过实时计算星历数据来获取ISS位置，以提高数据的实时性。

争议焦点：
• 主要集中在数据更新频率（15分钟）是否足够及时以准确反映ISS的位置，以及DNS记录的局限性是否影响该技术的广泛应用。

这些观点展示了技术实现的多样性以及在应用DNS记录查询ISS位置时所面临的实际问题和解决方案。

data.title: Take Two: Eshell
data.author: nanna
data.article_summary: 本文是Charles Choi对Emacs中的Eshell工具的回顾与使用心得。作者多年前初次接触Eshell时印象不佳，但随着对Emacs的熟悉，Eshell已成为其不可或缺的一部分。然而，作者发现Eshell的使用场景与传统shell不同。例如，文件管理方面，作者更偏好Emacs中的Dired模式，它能高效处理文件重命名等任务。对于运行简单命令，Dired也能胜任。源代码管理上，作者使用Magit和VC模式替代命令行git。对于编译和重复任务执行，Makefile和Emacs的compile功能更为实用。Eshell的真正优势在于结合Elisp使用，将其作为Elisp REPL，可以灵活地用Elisp函数替代shell命令，但掌握这一能力需要一定的Elisp知识。总体而言，Eshell适合那些愿意学习Elisp并希望在Emacs中实现更强大功能的用户。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Emacs中的Eshell及其他工具（如Dired）的使用体验和争议

不同观点：
• **支持Eshell的观点**（ndegruchy, xenodium）：
  - Eshell不是bash、zsh或fish，而是一个结合Emacs和命令行工具的环境。
  - 优点是可以将命令输出重定向到缓冲区，并利用Emacs的编辑功能处理这些输出。
  - Eshell的强大之处在于与Emacs的深度集成，如远程会话和文件操作。
  - 将Eshell视为一个用于处理外部工具数据的交互式Emacs会话，而不是传统的shell。

• **Dired和其他工具的偏好**（networked, augustfengd）：
  - Dired被视为文件管理的优雅工具，可以替代传统shell中的文件管理任务。
  - 提及了vidir和edir等工具，用于改进文件重命名等操作。
  - 一些用户发现Emacs中的工具如Dired非常有用，并愿意再次尝试Emacs。

• **反对使用Eshell的观点**（imiric, unixhero）：
  - 习惯于POSIX兼容的shell，其统一的接口和标准化的操作方式使得工作流在不同系统间可移植。
  - Eshell模仿POSIX shell的外观，但不遵循其惯例，导致使用上的困惑。
  - Emacs中不同模式有各自的 quirks 和交互方式，缺乏统一的用户界面。
  - 依赖Emacs配置可能限制了灵活性，尤其是在有更好替代工具出现时。

• **替代方案的建议**（triclops200）：
  - 使用xon.sh作为替代方案，它结合了Elisp的优势和传统shell的哲学。
  - xon.sh提供了类似Eshell的好处，但基于Python，更符合Unix“小程序做好一件事”的理念。

补充讨论：
• **对Emacs整体复杂性的抱怨**（log101, unixhero）：
  - Emacs的API复杂且难以记忆，用户希望有一本“精华部分”的指南。
  - 一些用户觉得Emacs功能过多，学习成本高，不如使用更简单的工具。

• **希望Emacs功能模块化**（cmrdporcupine）：
  - 希望Eshell和其他Emacs功能可以独立于Emacs环境使用。
  - 认为Emacs的“一体化”既是优势也是劣势，用户希望其功能能以组件形式存在。

争议焦点：
• Eshell是否能有效替代传统POSIX shell，尤其是在其界面和操作方式与传统shell相似但不完全相同的情况下。
• Emacs工具（如Eshell和Dired）的复杂性和学习曲线，以及其对用户工作流的影响。

总体来看，讨论围绕着Eshell和Emacs工具的优缺点展开，涉及其设计理念、与传统Unix工具的比较以及用户的实际使用体验。

by Charles Choi ìµë¯¼ì
Take Two: Eshell
30 Jun 2025  Charles Choi
This is a contribution to the
Emacs Carnival 2025-06: Take Two
collection of posts on Christian Tietzeâs blog.
My first take with
Eshell
many years back did not leave a good impression. My early expectations was that it should act like any other shell, only to be unpleasantly surprised by it. It took a long time for me to warm up to Eshell. Upon reflection, it was because I wasnât ready for it.
Now Eshell is an inseparable part of my Emacs experience. Paradoxically though, I find little occasion to use Eshell in the same way Iâve used shells in the past. Much of what I used to use the shell for, I do today with Emacs modes instead.
It was not always this way. Like so many users who started Unix computing in the 80âs, I started with the command line (for myself
ksh
and later
bash
), studiously internalizing command line tools and their arcane syntaxes to support file management, running programs, and systems administration. Overwhelmingly though, it was file management and running programs that I did through the command line.
For file management these days,
Dired
is my interface of choice. It is simply the more elegant tool for the job.
Case in point: renaming a bunch of files in a directory to arbitrary names. With a shell, my standard approach would have been to run some variant of
ls -1 > foo.sh
, edit
foo.sh
to insert
mv
on each line to a renamed target file,
chmod u+x foo.sh
to be executable, run
foo.sh
, delete
foo.sh
and call it a day.
With Dired, the above steps are replaced as such: make the buffer writable (via
Wdired
). Change the target filenames to a desired result, then commit the changes. This is even easier if there is a pattern you can use a regexp for. Unsurprisingly, all the basic file management operations that you would want are supported by Dired. Add
Casual Dired
to help make these operations discoverable and youâll soon consider how quaint using
mv
,
cp
,
rm
, and
ls
are.
Running a simple command on a file? Again, you can do that with Dired. Move the point to the Dired line containing the file. Type â!â and enter a command in the prompt. You can optionally reference the filename in the command with the â?â character if you want to redirect its output to a file (e.g.
cmd ? > outfile
).
Taking file management and running simple commands out of what you would use a shell for, whatâs left over? Source code management (SCM)?
Like for many others,
git
is my goto tool for SCM.  Much has been said about the terrible user experience of the
git
command line and for years I suffered with its design decisions. Thankfully for Emacs users, there is Magit and VC mode which both provide a saner experience for it.
Running a Makefile? Use Emacs
compile
, which provides command completion for the targets defined in the Makefile and error/warning navigation if needed. (Try out
Casual Make
for editing Makefiles in Emacs.)
Do you need to run a command with arcane arguments repeatedly? Again, Makefile +
compile
to the rescue where it can be used as a task runner for that command.
Need robust terminal emulation? Eshell will fail you here and you are likely better off using a dedicated terminal emulator app, separate from Emacs. That said, Iâve found the built-in
term
to be good enough for many curses-style utilities.
Mining data files with piped commands? Eshell is a power tool here: used wrongly and you could figuratively cut off a limb. But used cleverly, Eshell offers great value. More on this later.
So with all these use cases described, why even use Eshell?
Using Eshell becomes a win only if you know
Elisp
. With that, you can think of Eshell as an Elisp REPL that can secondarily act as a shell.
Letâs not mince words. For many users this is a high bar, as it takes into account
a lot
of prerequisite knowledge. That said, learning basic Elisp is trivial for readers already conversant with programming and manageable for those that arenât. Personally, I was very late (decades!) in taking the time to learn Elisp because I didnât see the reward in it and so, prioritized accordingly. That hesitancy turned out to be unfounded. Elisp is easy to learn and the reward (or punishment) for knowing it is having the ability to really
use
the full capabilities of Emacs. (Know Python? Hereâs a
cheatsheat for Elisp
that I wrote, hop in, the waterâs fineâ¦)
Once gained, bringing Elisp knowledge to using Eshell gives you a command line super power: the ability to improvise shell commands with Elisp functions.
Consider the following Eshell example where we wish to apply a command on a set of
png
files in a directory. Letâs start with a simple example that simply echoes filenames with suffix
.png
.
$
for
i
in
*.png
{
echo
$i
}
In Eshell, you can replace
echo $i
with an Elisp expression.
$
for
i
in
*.png
{
(
format
"%s"
i
)
}
You can also mix shell commands and Elisp via
dollar ($) expansion
. Note that

data.title: The Future of Forums Is Lies, I Guess
data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了一个小型Mastodon服务器在面对自动化垃圾信息和骚扰活动时的挑战。为了保持社区的专注性，新成员需要填写简短的申请，说明他们与酷儿皮革/恋物社区的联系。这种方法有效阻挡了大量垃圾账号，但也面临大型语言模型（LLM）带来的新威胁。文章描述了一个名为“mrfr”的用户，其申请看似完美，但最终被发现是市场研究公司Market Research Future的自动化垃圾活动。尽管这些申请看似由人类撰写，但内容和链接揭示了其自动化本质。作者指出，这种攻击既复杂又幼稚，虽然利用了LLM生成看似真实的申请，但因使用相同用户名和明显链接而易于识别。文章最后强调，面对这种新型垃圾信息，管理员难以有效防御而不误拒真实用户。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何应对新型威胁以及对多疑行为的看法

不同观点：
• [alganet] 认为应该将一些常被视为偏执的行为正常化。他提出，多问问题、对友好互动持怀疑态度、保持警惕等行为是积极的人类特质，有助于群体安全。这些行为不应被视为社交焦虑、精神病或反社会行为。他还指出，目前没有自动化检测或魔法般的方式可以防止新型威胁，因此需要更少脆弱性的人类来应对这些威胁。

• [praptak] 认为不存在纯粹的技术解决方案，问题需要政治化处理，最好是通过立法将滥用技术定为犯罪行为。他强调，这个问题的范围比一些小众论坛讨论的要广泛和危险得多，可能会严重影响社会政策讨论的能力。

补充讨论：
• [pvg] 提供的链接指向了一个先前的讨论（https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44130743），可能涉及相关主题或提供了背景信息，但未直接发表具体观点。

争议焦点：
• 对于如何有效应对新型威胁，[alganet] 强调个人行为的调整和适应，而 [praptak] 则主张通过政治和法律手段解决问题。两者在解决方案的路径上存在分歧。

• 对于多疑行为的看法，[alganet] 认为这些行为是积极且必要的，而潜在的争议点在于这些行为是否可能被过度正常化，从而导致不信任和社交障碍。

44492843.article_content:
The Future of Forums is Lies, I Guess
LLM
2025-07-07
In my free time, I help run a small Mastodon server for roughly six hundred queer leatherfolk. When a new member signs up, we require them to write a short application—just a sentence or two. There’s a small text box in the signup form which says:
Please tell us a bit about yourself and your connection to queer leather/kink/BDSM. What kind of play or gear gets you going?
This serves a few purposes. First, it maintains community focus. Before this question, we were flooded with signups from straight, vanilla people who wandered in to the bar (so to speak), and that made things a little awkward. Second, the application establishes a baseline for people willing and able to read text. This helps in getting people to follow server policy and talk to moderators when needed. Finally, it is
remarkably
effective at keeping out spammers. In almost six years of operation, we’ve had only a handful of spam accounts.
I was talking about this with Erin Kissane last year, as she and Darius Kazemi conducted research for their
report on Fediverse governance
. We shared a fear that Large Language Models (LLMs) would lower the cost of sophisticated, automated spam and harassment campaigns against small servers like ours in ways we simply couldn’t defend against.
Anyway, here’s an application we got last week, for a user named
mrfr
:
Hi! I’m a queer person with a long-standing interest in the leather and kink community. I value consent, safety, and exploration, and I’m always looking to learn more and connect with others who share those principles. I’m especially drawn to power exchange dynamics and enjoy impact play, bondage, and classic leather gear.
On the surface, this is a
great
application. It mentions specific kinks, it uses actual sentences, and it touches on key community concepts like consent and power exchange. Saying “I’m a queer person” is a tad odd. Normally you’d be more specific, like “I’m a dyke” or “I’m a non-binary bootblack”, but the Zoomers do use this sort of phrasing. It does feel slightly LLM-flavored—something about the sentence structure and tone has just a touch of that soap-sheen to it—but that’s hardly definitive. Some of our applications from actual humans read just like this.
I approved the account. A few hours later, it posted this:
It turns out
mrfr
is short for
Market Research Future
, a company which produces reports about all kinds of things from batteries to interior design. They actually have phone numbers on their web site, so I called
+44 1720 412 167
to ask if they were aware of the posts. It is remarkably fun to ask business people about their interest in queer BDSM—sometimes stigma works in your favor. I haven’t heard back yet, but I’m guessing they either conducting this spam campaign directly, or commissioned an SEO company which (perhaps without their knowledge) is doing it on their behalf.
Anyway, we’re not the only ones. There are also
mrfr
accounts purporting to be a
weird car enthusiast
, a
like-minded individual
, a
bear into market research on interior design trends
, and a
green building market research enthusiast in DC, Maryland, or Virginia
. Over on the seven-user
loud.computer
,
mrfr
applied with the text:
I’m a creative thinker who enjoys experimental art, internet culture, and unconventional digital spaces. I’d like to join loud.computer to connect with others who embrace weird, bold, and expressive online creativity, and to contribute to a community that values playfulness, individuality, and artistic freedom.
This too has the sheen of LLM slop. Of course a human
could
be behind these accounts—doing some background research and writing out detailed, plausible applications. But this is
expensive
, and a quick glance at either of our sites would have told that person that we have small reach and active moderation: a poor combination for would-be spammers. The posts don’t read as human either: the
4bear posting
, for instance, incorrectly summarizes a report on interior design
markets
as if it offered interior design
tips
.
I strongly suspect that Market Research Future, or a subcontractor, is conducting an automated spam campaign which uses a Large Language Model to evaluate a Mastodon instance, submit a plausible application for an account, and to post slop which links to Market Research Future reports.
In some sense, this is a wildly sophisticated attack. The state of NLP seven years ago would have made this sort of thing flatly impossible. It is now effective. There is no way for moderators to robustly deny these kinds of applications without also rejecting real human beings searching for community.
In another sense, this attack is remarkably naive. All the accounts are named
mrfr
, which made it easy for admins to informally chat and discover the coordinated nature of the attack. They all link to the same domain, which is easy to interpret as spam. They use Indian IPs, where few of our users are located; we could r

44463249.article_content:
Back to home
More than 1 in 5 Show HN posts are now AI-related, but get less than half the votes or comments.
_
The idea for this article didn't exist in my brain before this morning. But there I was, scrolling the New page and even more tired of all the AI-related Show HN posts than usual. I was confident that their numbers were multiplying and wanted proof. Exactly how much more AI crap is on my lawn compared to last year?
Full disclosure: I'm not a data guy. Everything below was off the top of my head. Not carefully structured or considered. I was grumpy, caffeinated, and avoiding work. I would love nothing more than for someone to show me some dumb error in my SQL queries that makes everything below meaningless.
I am NOT interested in debating the value of AI (LLMs, whatever). Mainly because I don't hate it/them nearly as much as this post suggests! I used Cursor + Claude to create the Chartjs visualizations in this article, dammit. What I hate is that a Show HN post used to represent someone's hard work or passion project. And that 100% justified the self-promotion IMO.
But since the introduction of coding chatbots, the New page has increasingly felt like an avalanche of low-effort crap. Make all of the "Chat with a PDF" nonsense you want, seriously! Just don't post it to HN.
With that out of the way, I used the
Hacker News BigQuery dataset
and some basic SQL queries to answer a few straightforward questions.
Is the number of Show HN posts increasing?
This is the broadest and least specific indicator of how coding chatbots have affected the frequency of Show HN posts. Coding bot make coding easy so number go up? Yes, the total number of Show HN posts looks to be trending upwards.
Here is the SQL query I ran:
SELECT
EXTRACT(YEAR FROM DATETIME(TIMESTAMP_SECONDS(time))) AS year,
COUNT(*) AS post_count,
AVG(score) AS avg_score,
AVG(descendants) AS avg_comments
FROM `bigquery-public-data.hacker_news.full`
WHERE
type = 'story'
AND REGEXP_CONTAINS(title, r'^Show HN:')
AND time >= UNIX_SECONDS(TIMESTAMP(DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 8 YEAR)))
AND deleted IS NULL
GROUP BY year
ORDER BY year DESC
And here is the output as of 10am Bangkok time on July 3, 2025:
Year
# of Show HN posts
2025
12,500 (so far)
2024
17,618
2023
14,062
2022
10,076
2021
12,644
2020
16,899
2019
5,831
2018
11,130
2017
5,526
Obviously, the 2025 data only represents 50.41% of the year. If we estimate the number of Show HN posts for the rest of 2025 (12,500*.9837), the graph looks like this:
A steeper trendline, sure. But I would have expected a bigger difference between 2018 (11,130 posts) and 2023 (14,062).
What's more, 2020, likely because of COVID externalities, had more posts (16,899) than 2023 (14,062) and almost as many as 2024 (17,618).
So I guess 2024 didn't feel like enough of a deluge for me to check the numbers and 2025 did. Maybe it wasn't the double shot. Maybe it's gotten worse very recently.
What % of Show HN posts mention AI?
At this point, I have to confront precisely what is bothering me about the perceived flood of Show HN posts. The core of the issue, to me, is that self-promotion without some sort of filtering function (i.e. having a working tool no longer infers significant labor and effort) is bad.
I am open to the idea of someone building a novel/interesting ChatGPT wrapper that required "real" work (i.e. without AI-generated code). But that's hard to judge from a Show HN post, so generalizing is the best I can do.
I am going out on a limb and assuming that Show HN posts with ' AI ', ' A.I. ', or 'GPT' in the title, as well as those with '.ai' or 'gpt' in the URL were built with less human elbow grease than those that do not include those keywords. Here is the SQL query that I used:
SELECT
EXTRACT(YEAR FROM DATETIME(TIMESTAMP_SECONDS(time))) as year,
COUNT(*) as ai_post_count,
AVG(score) as avg_score,
AVG(descendants) as avg_comments
FROM `bigquery-public-data.hacker_news.full`
WHERE
type = 'story'
AND REGEXP_CONTAINS(title, r'^Show HN:')
AND (
REGEXP_CONTAINS(UPPER(title), r'\bAI\b')
OR REGEXP_CONTAINS(UPPER(title), r'\bA\.I\.\b')
OR REGEXP_CONTAINS(UPPER(title), r'\bGPT\b')
OR REGEXP_CONTAINS(LOWER(url), r'\.ai/')
OR REGEXP_CONTAINS(LOWER(url), r'\.ai$')
OR REGEXP_CONTAINS(UPPER(url), r'\bGPT\b')
)
AND time >= UNIX_SECONDS(TIMESTAMP(DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 8 YEAR)))
AND deleted IS NULL
GROUP BY year
ORDER BY year DESC
I am Jack's total lack of surprise:
Mmmm it feels so good to justify one's own arguments.
Want more? Here is perhaps the best visualization of what's annoying me: a graph of [# of AI Show HN posts] / [total Show HN posts]:
This is not, as I have labeled it, a flood, deluge, or avalanche. It's an earthquake. A rupture. Quiet in 2022, five-alarm fire in 2023.
In 2018, one out of every 63 Show HN posts was AI-related. In 2025, it's shaping up to be more than one out of every 4.6. Nggghhhh.
But how does the community feel? Maybe there is a large cohort of HN users who want the AIs stomping all

44482405.article_content:
Collatz's Ant and Σ(n)
Relevant preceding posts
here
and
here
.
Consider the corresponding ant’s landscape development for $n = 500$:
with the last frame being:
Let’s also consider a score function $\Sigma(n)$ which returns the number of 1’s (or marked states) left by the ant on the corresponding landscape (regarding the last frame). With the prior example, we would have $\Sigma(500) = 54$. We might also want to normalize this by the corresponding stopping time $\tau_{n}$ characteristic of the collatz function dynamics for a given $n$. As such, given $\tau_{500} = 111$, we would have $\frac{\Sigma(500)}{\tau_{500}} ≈ 0.49$.
Additionally, let’s also consider some metrics relative to the ant’s (euclidean) distance to the origin. Say $α$ is the maximum distance reached relative to the origin over the whole development of the landscape, and $γ$ is the distance from the origin at the last frame (so where the ant ends up). For $n = 500$, we would have the ratio $\frac{\gamma}{\alpha} ≈ 0.87$.

data.title: Analysing Roman itineraries using GIS tooling
data.author: diodorus
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了利用地理信息系统（GIS）工具分析罗马道路网络的方法，特别是针对从Tude到Luco Augusti的第十九号道路。由于传统方法未能解决一些关键问题，如驿站位置、距离测量不一致、古典文献中的里程定义以及复杂的地形，文章提出了一种多代理方法，结合地形和非欧几里得相关性进行细致分析。通过GIS技术，研究能够计算最佳路径，并与历史数据和考古证据进行比较，以解决现有问题。本文强调了多学科研究的重要性，并展示了GIS在分析罗马道路网络中的应用潜力，包括优化路径计算和网络分析等功能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：使用现代技术（如GIS工具）重现和定位历史地点，尤其是面对历史变迁和地理变化时所遇到的困难。

不同观点：
• [jillesvangurp] 强调历史学家在制作地图时往往不够精确，历史事件的具体地点可能会因时间流逝而变得模糊。现代地图不一定能反映历史事件发生的地点，因为地理特征如河流、道路、建筑物和边界等都会发生变化。他引用了一个德国历史学者的例子，该学者使用GIS工具，通过将历史地图与现代地图对比，研究德国纳粹时期死亡行军的路线。结果显示许多道路已不复存在，集中营也被拆除，这使得精确定位历史事件发生的地点变得困难。

• [ggm] 从技术角度出发，提出使用IP网络中的往返时间（RTT）来地理定位端点，通过近似光速和位置圈的方法。这一观点虽然与历史地点定位主题相关性稍弱，但提出了一种现代技术在地理定位中的创新应用。

• [hjrnunes] 推荐Isaac Moreno的YouTube频道，强调其在使用GIS技术研究历史道路方面的贡献，尤其是罗马道路和渡槽的路线。Isaac Moreno不仅参与了西班牙Castilla-León省的罗马道路网站项目，还为西班牙公共电视台制作了关于罗马工程的纪录片系列。这表明现代技术与学术研究相结合，可以有效地研究和重现历史地理信息。

补充讨论：
• 历史地点的精确定位面临地理变化、时间流逝和人为改造等多重挑战。
• 使用现代GIS工具和技术可以有效帮助历史学者和研究者重现和定位历史事件发生的地点，但需要结合多种方法和数据来源。
• 不同领域的专家（如历史学者、工程师）通过合作和使用现代技术，能够更准确地理解和呈现历史地理信息。

争议焦点：
• 历史事件地点精确定位的困难：一方面是历史资料和地图的模糊性，另一方面是现代地理变化对历史地点定位的影响。

Abstract
Reconstruction of the Roman road network must be approached from different methodologies of multidisciplinary character. Once the traditional approaches have been exhausted without achieving a historiographical consensus, the problem may appear insurmountable. However, leveraging Geographic Information Systems (GIS) provides an avenue for re-evaluating existing proposals and suggesting more fitting layouts. This can be accomplished through a meticulous analysis that incorporates topographic and non-Euclidean correlations; allowing a more nuanced and accurate understanding of the subject matter than conventional methods might offer. In this context, the aim of this article is to discuss intriguing research points. But also emphasize the importance of multidisciplinary and multi-proxy studies in relation with the Roman terrestrial networks. We explore a case study in the Galician territory, where we have detected methodological shortcomings reconstructing the route of the XIX road:
Item Bracaram Asturicam
. One of the sections, from
Tude
to
Luco Augusti
, has aroused a greater debate, based on several basic problems: (1) the identification of the
mansions
, (2) the lack of consensus in the measurements of the distances, (3) the miles referred to in the classical sources, and (4) the complex orography of this territory. Thus, by applying Geographic Information Systems techniques, we will be able to calculate the optimal path, and compare the results with historical data and archaeological evidence.

Theoretical framework
Research on the Roman road network should adopt a multidisciplinary perspective, tailored to the specific needs of each case study. Identifying a Roman road, as distinct from movement corridors or later Medieval and Modern roads, as well as understanding the transformation of the territory itself, presents problems that remain consistent throughout any research on road networks.

data.article_summary: 《LookingGlass: Generative Anamorphoses via Laplacian Pyramid Warping》一文介绍了一种生成变形图像的新方法。传统变形图像（anamorphosis）需从特定视角观察才能显现真实形态，而该文通过使用潜在校正流模型（latent rectified flow models）和拉普拉斯金字塔扭曲（Laplacian Pyramid Warping）技术，使得生成的图像即使直接观看也具有有效的视觉解释。该方法提升了图像的生成质量，并将视觉谜题（Visual Anagrams）扩展到潜在空间模型和更广泛的空间变换中，创造出新颖的生成感知错觉。文章发表于CVPR 2025。

LookingGlass: Generative Anamorphoses via Laplacian Pyramid Warping
In this work, we revisit these famous optical illusions with a generative twist. With the help of latent rectified flow models, we propose a method to create anamorphic images that still retain a valid interpretation when viewed directly.
June 10, 2025
CVPR 2025
Authors
Pascal Chang (DisneyResearch|Studios/ETH Joint PhD)
Sergio Sancho (DisneyResearch|Studios/ETH Joint PhD)
Jingwei Tang (DisneyResearch|Studios)
Markus Gross (DisneyResearch|Studios)
Vinicius Azevedo (DisneyResearch|Studios)
LookingGlass: Generative Anamorphoses via Laplacian Pyramid Warping
Download Publication PDF
Download Supplemental PDF
Abstract
Anamorphosis refers to a category of images that are intentionally distorted, making them unrecognizable when viewed directly. Their true form only reveals itself when seen from a specific viewpoint, which can be through some catadioptric device like a mirror or a lens. While the construction of these mathematical devices can be traced back to as early as the 17th century, they are only interpretable when viewed from a specific vantage point and tend to lose meaning when seen normally. In this paper, we revisit these famous optical illusions with a generative twist. With the help of latent rectified flow models, we propose a method to create anamorphic images that still retain a valid interpretation when viewed directly. To this end, we introduce Laplacian Pyramid Warping, a frequency-aware image warping technique key to generating high-quality visuals. Our work extends Visual Anagrams to latent space models and to a wider range of spatial transforms, enabling the creation of novel generative perceptual illusions.

data.title: What Microchip doesn't (officially) tell you about the VSC8512
data.author: ahlCVA
data.article_summary:
本文是关于作者在开源1U可管理以太网交换机项目（LATENTRED）中使用VSC8512 PHY芯片的经历。作者最初选择VSC8512是因为其QSGMII接口和 supposedly 完全公开的 datasheet，但在尝试调整SERDES TX均衡器设置时发现需要访问“机密参考手册”，该手册受NDA限制。由于无法签署NDA，作者只能依赖公开文档解决问题。

公开文档包括VSC8512 datasheet、硬件设计清单、IBIS-AMI模型和参考设计指南等。通过分析，作者发现VSC8512像是精简版交换机ASIC，并确认了一些SERDES参数（如OB_LEV、OB_PREC等），尽管不完全知道如何设置这些参数。作者还提到MESA API是一个有价值的信息来源，但文档不完善。最终，作者依靠有限的信息和实验解决了信号完整性问题。

不同观点：
• ACCount36认为，嵌入式工作中最令人厌恶的是与硅谷厂商打交道，他们拒绝发布完整的文档和工具，这让人 frustration。
• 0xTJ指出，Microchip没有公开发布Atmel ATF16V8、ATF22V10 SPLD和ATF15xx CPLD的编程算法和EE位图，虽然这些算法部分已被逆向工程，但官方公开会更好。同时提到ATF15xx的BSDL文件已发布，但仅用于测试/旁路。
• anitil赞同硬件厂商在设备能力上不够透明，导致开发过程中遇到困难，并赞扬文中的研究工作深入。
• gregfjohnson对Microchip的IDE MPLAB X IDE v6.20中对gcc优化级别收费表示不满，质疑是否违反gcc的copyleft许可证，考虑向EFF举报。
• userbinator认为Microchip在公开收购公司的技术资料方面做得不错，例如Atmel的安全IC现在有完整的资料可免费下载。

补充讨论：
• lttlrck提到令牌环技术在1996年已经过时，但猜测某些工业系统可能仍需与遗留系统接口，因此该技术仍在“暗硅”中存在。
• kragen对文章的全面和无畏表示赞赏，认出作者是Andrew Zonenberg。
• nemo8551表达对该系列文章的喜爱，并请求推荐类似的深度技术文章。
• Taniwha和jpm_sd提到在购买Ethernet硬件组件时缺乏支持的问题，特别是对于小客户。
• RainyDayTmrw以幽默的方式指出serdes命名上的巧合。

44468718.article_content:
Switch project, part 3 - what Microchip doesn't (officially) tell you about the VSC8512
2025-07-04 08:00
This is part 3 of my ongoing series about LATENTRED, my project to create an open source 1U managed Ethernet switch
from scratch.
Hereâs a quick, or maybe not-so-quick, update about the PHY on the line card and some of my troubles (and solutions).
And probably more internal details than you want to know, but hey - maybe this will be useful to somebody. Not a lot of pretty pictures either. One day I do want to decap one for fun, but I have better things to do with my time than try to fully netlist-extract a large 65nm IC just to figure out some undocumented registers.
Background
I chose the VSC8512 as the PHY for the line card because it had a QSGMII interface (which used much less pins than SGMII), but also (so I thought) had a fully open datasheet with no NDAs required.
Typically Iâm used to seeing parts that are either fully NDAâd (with a trivial product brief and no register info etc, or sometimes not even pinout info, public), or fully open. Sometimes I find components with specific documents restricted, but itâs almost always clear that âthis document/ref design exists, you canât get it without an NDA, but we are openly telling you weâre holding it backâ.
In my previous post I mentioned that there was no documentation for how to change the SERDES TX equalizer settings on the PHY side of the QSGMII. I opened a support case and Microchip responded saying that additional info was available in the âconfidential reference manualâ for the part which required an NDA. The rest of the reply was pretty generic and mentioned indirect register access but no specifics.
I was quite annoyed at this, as I had specifically chosen the part believing there was no restricted documentation. Since signing an NDA wasnât an option, it seemed I had the choice of suboptimal signal integrity or figuring things out from the limited public information. The eye was still reasonably open as-is and my cables and boards didnât have a ton of insertion loss, so worst case things would probably work with the default TX config.
But why would I settle for bad SI when I could read a bunch of poorly documented code and datasheets deliberately missing details?
What we have to go on
So, we know there is a confidential reference manual. But thereâs a lot of docs available to the public - after all, I was able to make a board, bring up the PHY, and pass packets without it.
VSC8512 datasheet (VMDS-10396). This is 139 pages of meat including what I thought was a complete set of registers.
VSC8512 hardware design checklist (DS00004697A)
VSC8504 Serdes6G IBIS-AMI model. This is for the 4-port version of the same PHY but is linked on the product web page; presumably the 04 and 12 use the same IP.
VSC742x / 85x2 reference design guide (UG1037). This describes a 24-port switch reference design using a SparX-III / Caracal switch ASIC (including 12 integrated PHYs) paired with a VSC85x2. Not a ton interesting here.
Microchip Ethernet Switch API (MESA), MIT licensed HAL for Microchip/Vitesse PHYs and switches available on GitHub. As youâll see in a bit, this is an absolute gold mine of information but itâs (perhaps intentionally) not well documented what a lot of the bitfields and APIs do.
Initial observations
Itâs pretty easy to see that the VSC8512 is a nerfed switch ASIC. Thereâs an entire DDR I/O controller thatâs unused (over a dozen VDD_IODDR pins youâre instructed to ground, plus a large group of NC pins in the surrounding area). So docs for the un-crippled switch ASIC, which I suspected and later confirmed was the VSC742x, are potentially of interest too.
The IBIS-AMI model included the magic name âSerdes6Gâ. Searching for this turned up some additional docs, most notably AN3743 (DS00003743A) which purports to be about the VSC74xx / 84xx but seems to be describing something very similar to whatâs on the 8512.
Between the various documents I was able to conclude that the VSC8512 is made on an unspecified 65nm process (I should decap one at some point and figure out whose / see what it looks likeâ¦ Luton first stepping is mentioned as being fabbed at TSMC in
vtss_phy_do_page_chk
so I suspect the rest are as well).
The SERDES macro was developed by the âGerman Design Centerâ (in the Dortmund area, according to some LinkedIn hits from a google search) - interesting to know, but not particularly useful in this context.
The IBIS model describes some very useful parameters. We donât know how to actually set them yet, but we know they exist, their ranges, and (most importantly) their names:
OB_LEV
: amplitude / main cursor tap, 0 to 63
OB_PREC
: pre-cursor FFE tap, -15 to +15
OB_POST0
: post cursor 0 FFE tap, -31 to +31
OB_POST1
: post cursor 1 FFE tap, -15 to +15
OB_POL
: output invert
OB_SER_H
: coarse slew rate adjust (slow/fast)
OB_SER
: fine slew rate adjust, 0 to 15
These were all critical key wo

data.title: Charles Babbage and deciphering codes (1864)
data.author: pncnmnp
data.article_summary: 查尔斯·巴贝奇（Charles Babbage）在1864年出版的自传《一个哲学家的生命历程》（*Passages from the Life of a Philosopher*）中，讨论了破译密码的艺术。他从小就对解码感兴趣，在学生时代就能破解高年级学生制作的简单密码。巴贝奇认为，破译密码是一项需要时间、创造力和耐心的工作，很少有密码值得花费精力去破解。他提到，许多人都相信自己能创造出无法被破解的密码，但往往这种信念是错误的。巴贝奇曾与皇家学会主席戴维斯·吉尔伯特（Davies Gilbert）讨论过不可破解的密码，然而他们设想的密码最终都被成功破译。巴贝奇描述了一种基于同心圆的密码系统，内圈和外圈的字母排列不同，但通过仔细分析和推理，他依然能够破解此类密码。这表明，即便是复杂的密码，也难以做到完全不可破译。

Charles Babbage and deciphering codes
Charles Babbage wrote an autobiography
Passages from the Life of a Philosopher
which was published in London in
1864
. In our biography of Babbage we have quoted several passages from the book which tell us about his life and the analytical engine. Here we quote from Chapter XVIII of the book where Babbage writes about deciphering. What we present here is only an extract. In fact we omit a more technical part which describes the considerable effort that he had put in constructing dictionaries with particular properties to assist in deciphering:-
Deciphering is, in my opinion, one of the most fascinating of arts, and I fear I have wasted upon it more time than it deserves. I practised it in its simplest form when I was at school. The bigger boys made ciphers, but if I got hold of a few words, I usually found out the key. The consequence of this ingenuity was occasionally painful: the owners of the detected ciphers sometimes thrashed me, though the fault really lay in their own stupidity.
There is a kind of maxim amongst the craft of decipherers ..., that every cipher can be deciphered.
I am myself inclined to think that deciphering is an affair of time, ingenuity, and patience; and that very few ciphers are worth the trouble of unravelling them.
One of the most singular characteristics of the art of deciphering is the strong conviction possessed by every person, even moderately acquainted with it, that he is able to construct a cipher which nobody else can decipher. I have also observed that the cleverer the person, the more intimate is his conviction. In my earliest study of the subject I shared in this belief, and maintained it for many years.
In a conversation on that subject which I had with the late Mr Davies Gilbert, President of the Royal Society, each maintained that he possessed a cipher which was absolutely inscrutable. On comparison, it appeared that we had both imagined the same law, and we were thus confirmed in our conviction of the security of our cipher.
Many years after, the late Dr Fitton, having asked my opinion of the possibility of making an inscrutable cipher, I mentioned the conversation I had had with Davies Gilbert, and explained the law of the cipher, which we both thought would baffle the greatest adept in that science. Dr Fitton fully agreed in my view of the subject; but even whilst I was explaining the law, an indistinct glimpse of defeating it presented itself vaguely to my imagination. Having mentioned my newly-conceived doubt, it was entirely rejected by my friend. I then proposed that Dr Fitton should write a few sentences in a cipher constructed according to this law, and that I should make some attempts to unravel it. I offered to give a few hours to the subject; and if I could see my way to a solution, to continue my researches; but if not on the road to success, to tell him I had given up the task.
Late in the evening of that day I commenced a preparatory inquiry into the means of unravelling this new cipher, and I soon arrived at a tolerable certainty that I should succeed. The next night, on my return from a party, I found Dr Fitton's cipher on my table. I immediately commenced my attempt. After some time I found that it would not yield to my means of treating it; and on further examination I succeeded in proving that it was not written according to the law agreed upon. At first my friend was very positive that I was mistaken; and having taken it to his sister, by whose aid it was composed, he returned and told me that it was constructed upon the very law I had proposed. I then assured him that they must have made some mistake, and that my evidence was so irresistible, that if my life depended upon the result I should have no hesitation in making my election.
Dr Fitton again retired to consult his sister; and after the lapse of a considerable interval of time again returned, and informed me that I was right - that his sister had inadvertently mistaken the enunciation of the law. I now remarked that I possessed an absolute demonstration of the fact I had communicated to him; and added that, having conjectured the origin of the mistake, I would decipher the cipher with the erroneous law before he could send me the new cipher to be made according to the law originally proposed. Before the evening of the next day both ciphers had been translated.
This cipher was arranged upon the following principle: - Two concentric circles of cardboard were formed, each divided into twenty-six or more divisions.
On the outer were written in regular order the letters of the alphabet. On the inner circle were written the same twenty-six letters, but in any irregular manner.
In order to use this cipher, look for the first letter of the word to be ciphered on the outside circle. Opposite to it, on the inner circle, will be another letter, which is to be written as the cipher for the former.

data.title: Artist in Residence on a Satellite
data.author: thenthenthen
data.article_summary: 2024年2月3日，由中国艺术家徐冰主导的“艺术链计划”首颗艺术卫星“SCA-1”成功发射升空。该卫星由长征三号B运载火箭在广东阳江附近海域发射，太阳能板正常展开，初步遥测正常。这是全球首颗艺术卫星，旨在将空间科技与当代艺术结合，邀请国内外艺术家参与创作，利用卫星平台进行艺术探索。卫星配备显示屏、自拍相机、AI程序等，支持艺术家在太空环境中创作并记录过程。该项目由徐冰工作室与多家科技公司合作实施，目标是降低艺术界进入航天领域的门槛，促进太空艺术的发展。首批参与艺术家包括Joseph Kosuth、Eduardo Kac、曹斐等国际知名艺术家。项目旨在通过太空艺术反映科技对人类认知的影响，探索新的哲学视角和艺术形式。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：艺术与航天科技的结合，特别是通过卫星项目展示艺术作品

不同观点：
• axus认为，与2014年俄罗斯发射的带有Hello Kitty自拍和预载信息的日本小卫星类似，艺术与航天技术的结合已经取得了显著进展。他提到了SCA-1项目作为一个例子，该项目通过在太空中展示图像和自拍来表现艺术。

• patrickwalton指出，Planet Labs曾有过类似的艺术家驻场项目。他提到，艺术家为卫星的太阳能电池板设计了贴花，这表明艺术与航天技术的融合并不仅限于一种形式，而是可以有多种表现方式。

• gnabgib对艺术卫星的概念表达了兴趣，但同时对其实际意义和目的提出了疑问。他认为，一个在太空中展示图像并自拍的卫星项目虽然“有趣”，但可能缺乏更深的实用价值或目的。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于艺术卫星的实际意义和价值。gnabgib对项目的实用性提出了质疑，而axus和patrickwalton则更多地关注技术进步和艺术表达的可能性。

• 讨论中提到了两个具体项目：Hello Kitty自拍卫星和SCA-1艺术卫星，展示了艺术与航天技术结合的多样化方式。

Xu Bing leads the way: The first satellite of the "Star Chain of Arts Project," "SCA-1," successfully launched into orbit
Xu Bing leads the way: The first satellite of the "Star Chain of Arts Project," "SCA-1," successfully launched into orbit
On February 3, 2024, at 11:06 a.m., the first Chinese art satellite, "SCA-1" (The first satellite of the Star Chain of Arts Project), was successfully launched into orbit near the sea area of Yangjiang, Guangdong, using the Long March 3B carrier rocket. The satellite's solar panels deployed normally, and the initial telemetry is normal. Among the thousands of satellites now orbiting above us, including scientific, meteorological, communication, and military satellites, there was a missing category - the "art satellite."
▲Video footage of the launch of the art satellite "SCA-1," 2024, © Xu Bing Studio.
"SCA-1," led by artist Xu Bing, is the first satellite of the " Star Chain of Art Project." Adhering to the principles of participation and sharing, Xu Bing has defined the concept of this satellite as follows: "By inviting artists from China and abroad to participate in the 'Xu Bing Art Satellite Creative Residency Project,' sharing the rights to use this satellite, and creating their own works. The attempt is to intertwine space technology with contemporary art, extending our cognitive reach into a broader space, collectively exploring this highly futuristic domain."
▲ "SCA-1" Art Satellite at Work, 2023, © Xu Bing Studio.
The "Xu Bing Art Satellite Creative Residency Project" aims to invite (and solicit) artists and professionals with a cosmic perspective and outstanding thinking abilities, providing them with an artistic creation platform beyond the Karman Line. The project's pursuit is to extend perspectives into outer space through art, with the aim of looking back at Earth from a unique vantage point, seeking new and effective philosophical views or methods to address issues on Earth, and providing predictions and experiments for artistic creations of humanity or future interstellar races. The project is organized and implemented by Xu Bing Studio in collaboration with Beijing Wanhu Chuangshi Cultural Media Co., Ltd., and is technically supported by Beijing Xingyilianxin Technology Co., Ltd., and Chengdu Guoxing Aerospace Technology Co., Ltd.
The satellite's structure includes a display screen facing the starry sea and a selfie camera. Through ground control stations, various electronic information such as videos and images can be uploaded to the satellite. The onboard selfie camera captures photos or images of the satellite in the space environment. The satellite is equipped with AI programs, onboard computers, and other functions, enabling interaction with artists or recording their entire creative process in space.
▲
Installation Diagram of the "SCA-1" Art Satellite, 2023, © Xu Bing Studio.
We all know that the aerospace industry has high entry barriers, making it challenging for the art world to access space resources and utilize space technology for artistic creation. However, this phenomenon has seen a change in the "New Space Era" following the emergence of private space technology companies. This is one of the reasons why the "Xu Bing Art Satellite Creative Residency Project" has come into existence. We aim to share accessible space resources with more artists, especially young artists and individuals from various fields outside the art industry. By reducing entry barriers, gathering collective wisdom, we hope to accelerate the development of space art initiatives.
▲ Model Diagram of the "SCA-1" Art Satellite, 2023, © Xu Bing Studio.
The first phase of artists participating in this project includes internationally renowned conceptual artist Joseph Kosuth, globally acclaimed bio-artist Eduardo Kac known for works such as "Fluorescent Rabbits" and space art, Israeli artist Haim Steinbach, who has had solo exhibitions at MoMA, Chinese artist Cao Fei active in the international art scene, Miri Park, a Korean artist focusing on geopolitical issues, aerospace engineer and space artist Liu Xin, technology artist Zhang Wenchao, encryption art specialist Liu Jiaying, artist duo Geng Xue + Wang Jiyu, young artists Ge Yulu, Yue Luping, Gao Zhenpeng, Miao Ying, and many more. Additionally, there is eighth-grade middle school student Cao Zheng, who submitted an independent proposal...(More participants will be announced as the project progresses). They will utilize this dedicated art satellite in the unique environment of outer space, within a legal space transcending national borders, to create new space art distinct from traditional forms.
▲ Real Shot of the "SCA-1" Art Satellite, 2023, © Xu Bing Studio.

data.author: giuliomagnifico
data.article_summary: 研究人员开发了一种新技术，称为WeGeFT，显著提升了大型语言模型在特定任务（如常识推理、算术推理、指令跟随、代码生成和视觉识别）上的表现，且无需增加微调所需的计算能力。传统上，大型语言模型经过预训练后能够处理广泛的任务，但在特定领域表现欠佳，需要微调。WeGeFT基于2022年推出的LoRA技术，通过识别模型已熟悉的参数和需要学习的参数，重点调整后者，从而提高效率。实验证明，WeGeFT在多个任务上的表现优于或等于LoRA及其变体，同时不增加计算需求。研究团队还计划利用WeGeFT改进模型的安全性。该研究将在国际机器学习大会上发表。

44492970.article_content:
News Releases
Researchers Found a Better Way to Teach Large Language Models New Skills
July 7, 2025
Matt Shipman
3-min. read
Image credit: Growtika.
For Immediate Release
Tianfu Wu
tianfu_wu@ncsu.edu
Matt Shipman
matt_shipman@ncsu.edu
Researchers have developed a technique that significantly improves the performance of large language models without increasing the computational power necessary to fine-tune the models. The researchers demonstrated that their technique improves the performance of these models over previous techniques in tasks including commonsense reasoning, arithmetic reasoning, instruction following, code generation, and visual recognition.
Large language models are artificial intelligence systems that are pretrained on huge data sets. After pretraining, these models predict which words should follow each other in order to respond to user queries. However, the nonspecific nature of pretraining means that there is ample room for improvement with these models when the user queries are focused on specific topics, such as when a user requests the model to answer a math question or to write computer code.
“In order to improve a model’s ability to perform more specific tasks, you need to fine-tune the model,” says Tianfu Wu, co-corresponding author of a paper on the work and an associate professor of computer engineering at North Carolina State University. “However, these models are so large that it is not feasible to re-train the entire model. Instead, you want to determine the smallest number of changes necessary to improve the model’s performance. We’ve developed a technique, called WeGeFT (pronounced
wee-gift
), that represents a significant advance for fine-tuning these large models.”
The big break-through for fine-tuning these large models was called LoRA, which came out in 2022. LoRA works by using mathematical tools to identify a small subset of key parameters that are most likely to improve a model’s performance on a specific task. There have been many attempts to improve upon LoRA, but Wu and his collaborators found these previous efforts either required significantly more computational power to improve performance, or used the same amount of computing power without improving performance.
“WeGeFT builds on LoRA, but incorporates additional mathematical tools that allow us to determine which of the key parameters the model is already familiar with and which parameters the model would need to ‘learn,’” says Wu. “By placing more weight on the truly novel parameters, we are able to improve model performance compared to LoRA without incorporating significant new computational demands.”
In proof-of-concept testing, the researchers found that WeGeFT performed as well as or better than LoRA and its many variants across a variety of downstream tasks: commonsense reasoning, arithmetic reasoning, instruction following, code generation, and visual recognition.
“We think this is a valuable step forward,” Wu says. “We are now exploring ways that WeGeFT could also be used to identify elements of the model that are responsible for harmful outputs, with the goal of improving AI alignment and ‘surgery’ to improve model safety and outputs. We expect that work to be forthcoming.”
The paper, “
WeGeFT: Weight-Generative Fine-Tuning for Multi-Faceted Efficient Adaptation of Large Models
,” will be presented July 17 at the International Conference on Machine Learning, being held in Vancouver, Canada. Co-corresponding author of the paper is Chinmay Savadikar, a Ph.D. student at NC State. The paper was co-authored by Xi Song, an independent researcher.
This work was done with support from the National Science Foundation under grants 1909644, 2024688 and 2013451; and from the Army Research Office under grants W911NF1810295 and W911NF2210010.

data.title: China is increasingly a home to major brands
data.author: anigbrowl
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：全球市场中的中国品牌影响力、消费者行为变化、以及中美之间的经济竞争

不同观点：
• **中国智能手机品牌的崛起与消失**：
   - **userbinator** 提到，尽管苹果和三星在全球及美国市场占据主导地位，但像小米、Oppo、Realme和华为等中国品牌在全球市场也占有相当大的份额。同时指出，许多曾经的中国安卓品牌（如Ainol、Cubot等）已经消失，而存活下来的品牌也逐渐变得对用户不友好。
   - 该评论强调了中国品牌的市场份额和历史变化，并暗示中国品牌逐渐走向高端市场，类似于苹果和三星的策略。

• **旅游业和奢侈品市场对中国市场的依赖**：
   - **budududuroiu** 指出，依赖旅游业的国家如泰国和马来西亚，已经开始迎合中国游客市场，并在机场等公共场所使用中文标示。同时，奢侈品牌如Louis Vuitton在美国关闭门店，但在上海开设大型店铺，显示出对中国市场的重视。
   - 该评论突出了中国消费者在全球市场中的重要性，以及西方市场对中国经济依赖的增加。

• **经济实惠产品的可获得性**：
   - **rsanek** 提到在美国难以找到15,000美元的新车，但提供了Nissan Versa作为接近这一价格的选择。
   - **hollerith** 补充说，在美国，15,000美元的预算更多地面临的是二手车市场，且二手车在美 abundance。
   - **alexjplant** 进一步解释，美国消费者更倾向于购买昂贵车辆以展示财富和个人价值观，因此便宜车在美国市场需求较少。

• **中国品牌的技术产品与数据安全**：
   - **WarOnPrivacy** 提到，尽管作者认为Huawei手表是Apple Watch的优秀替代品，但更广泛的问题是美国和西方在全球市场的主导地位受到中国企业的挑战。评论还指出，数据安全风险主要来自美国实体，而非中国。
   - 该评论强调了中美之间在技术和数据安全领域的竞争，以及消费者对中国产品的依赖性增加。

• **消费者行为与购买决策**：
   - **breve** 批评了消费者购买不必要的高价产品的倾向，并建议购买更便宜、环保的Casio数字手表。
   - **supportengineer** 提到过去在亚马逊上购买到质量惊人的中国品牌产品，但这些品牌很快消失，强调了品牌对消费者的重要性。

补充讨论：
• **政治与市场竞争**：
   - **blibble** 提到，美国忽视其盟友的利益，导致这些国家转向与中国合作，从而失去市场份额。同时提到，通过简单的社交媒体广告，美国可能已经失去了未来的市场主导地位。
   
• **社会经济不平等与财富分配**：
   - **markus_zhang** 指出，要赶上中国的竞争力，美国需要更加努力，并通过财富再分配来缓解经济不平等问题。

• **标题和文章风格的建议**：
   - **pimlottc** 建议将文章的标题改为更不具点击诱饵性质的“My journey to a Huawei watch”。

争议焦点：
• 中美经济竞争及数据安全：讨论中涉及到的中美技术产品竞争及数据安全问题，尤其是对美国实体与中国企业之间的数据处理方式的不同看法，构成了一个争议焦点。

data.title: Anyone Could Forget a Kid in a Hot Car, Research Shows
data.author: mhb
data.article_summary: 文章指出，许多孩子被遗忘在热车中导致的死亡并非由于疏忽，而是因为常见的记忆失误。自1998年以来，已有约1,011名儿童因此死亡，其中超过一半是被看护人无意中留下的。研究表明，父母的日常压力可能增加这种记忆失误的可能性。南佛罗里达大学心理学教授David Diamond解释，这并非因为父母 negligent，而是工作记忆问题。当工作记忆失败时，例如因分心或压力，可能会导致严重后果。他强调，这种悲剧可能发生在任何人身上，尤其是当日常 routine 改变时，例如度假期间。为了防止此类事件，需采取预防措施，如设置提醒等。文章还提醒，即使在温和气温下，车内温度也可能快速升高，对儿童构成威胁。

Anyone Could Forget a Kid in a Hot Car, Research Shows
Most hot car deaths don't happen because of negligence. They're the result of a common memory failure that can lead to tragic consequences. Here's what parents need to know.
By
Emily A. Thomas, PhD
Associate Director, Auto Safety
Updated by
Jessica D’Argenio Waller, MS, CNS, LDN
Updated April 30, 2025
Photo Illustration: John Ritter
No parent thinks they’d forget their child in a hot car. But the tragic truth is that it can happen to anyone.
Since 1998, about 1,011 children have died in hot cars—and more than half of them were left behind unknowingly by their caregiver, according to
NoHeatStroke.org
.
But
recent research
shows that the daily stresses parents face can make these memory lapses more likely. Forgetting a child isn’t a negligence problem but a working memory problem, says David Diamond, PhD, a professor of psychology at the University of South Florida in Tampa. Diamond, a leading expert in cognitive neuroscience, has studied the role of memory in such tragedies.
“The most common response is that only bad or negligent parents forget kids in cars,” Diamond says. “It’s a matter of circumstances. It can happen to everyone.”

Deciding When It's Time to Upgrade Your Child's Car Seat
Best Booster Seats for Kids
During the summer, many families change their daily routines because of vacations or other reasons, and that disruption is a common factor in these tragic incidents, Diamond’s research has found.
Janette Fennell, founder and president of KidsAndCars.org, a group that tracks these incidents, says, “The worst thing any parent or caregiver can ever do is to think that something like this could never happen to them or someone in their family.”
These tragedies occur at an alarming rate, and they involve a range of circumstances. NoHeatStroke.org reports that deaths have spanned from 5-day-old babies to 14-year-olds. And deaths from heatstroke can happen any time of year, even as early as February and as late as November.
KidsAndCars.org’s heatstroke fact sheet
(PDF) highlights that caregivers involved in these incidents come from many walks of life. They include teachers, dentists, social workers, law enforcement officers, nurses, clergymen, military officers, and even a rocket scientist. These tragic cases can happen to anyone, regardless of their education or socioeconomic status.
And it’s not just a summertime problem. Even on days with mild temperatures, the heat inside a closed vehicle can reach dangerous levels within an hour, posing major health risks to small children or pets left inside, Consumer Reports’
testing shows
.
In this article
Arrow link
When Working Memory Fails
Tips to Help Prevent It
Video: We Tested How Hot Cars Get
When Working Memory Fails
Diamond says the problem involves two parts of a person’s working memory: prospective and semantic. Prospective memory helps us remember to do something in the future, while semantic memory allows drivers to make the trip from work to home on autopilot, where they arrive without remembering clear details of how they got there.
Prospective and semantic memories work together to help us make changes to our routines; these changes can include things such as “drop off the baby at day care” or “stop for groceries on the way home.” When our working memory fails, such as when we’re distracted or stressed, there can be catastrophic implications, Diamond says. He gave examples of situations where critical safety steps were overlooked, such as a surgeon leaving tools in a patient, a pilot not setting the wing flaps for landing, and caregivers forgetting that there’s a baby in the car.
“The habit brain system is a great convenience that allows us to go into autopilot,” Diamond says. “The beauty of it is that we don’t have to remember every turn, but the problem is that it’s actually guiding our behavior. When it guides our behavior, it suppresses the other part of the brain that is supposed to remind us of additional information.”
“We have to accept the fact that our brain multitasks. And as a part of that multitasking, the awareness of a child can be lost,” Diamond says. “We have to accept that the human memory is flawed. That includes when loving, attentive parents lose awareness of their children when they are in a car.”
Diamond has studied many heatstroke cases and points to common factors: stress, sleep deprivation, and change in routine.
Many times when a child died in this situation, there was a change in the day’s routine, Diamond says. For example, a parent who wouldn’t usually be responsible for day-care drop-off may have had the task that day. Because our brains recognize a pattern for the day, this person would drive to work as usual, even though the baby was along for the ride. data.title: Photography 'Rules' That Social Media Destroyed
data.author: patrakov
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了摄影规则在社交媒体时代的巨变。过去，摄影有严格的规则，这些规则经过多年实践和暗房实验形成，代表了专业与业余的区别。然而，随着Instagram、TikTok等社交媒体平台的兴起，这些规则在不到二十年内被彻底颠覆。社交媒体强调吸引注意力，鼓励打破传统规则，如三分法则、对称构图和技术完美，转而推崇引人注目的、甚至有缺陷的图像。平台算法更倾向于推送引发争议和意外的内容，而非遵循传统构图的精美照片。这种变化让许多资深摄影师感到不适，但也反映了摄影从技术艺术向注意力经济的转变。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：摄影规则的应用与突破

不同观点：
• **codingdave** 认为，摄影中的所谓“规则”其实是设计原则，而非硬性规定。这些原则在摄影入门课程中教授，帮助学生在学习初期掌握基础，但随着经验积累，摄影师应学会何时遵循、何时打破这些规则以实现更具创意的作品。这些规则被视为陈词滥调，仅在学习初期有指导意义。

• **sherdil2022** 强调规则的目的是为了被打破。他引用了一句格言：“了解规则才能打破规则。” 他个人不喜欢竖直或正方形的照片和视频，但如果消费需求如此（如社交媒体的格式要求），摄影师应根据需求进行创作，即使这意味着打破常规。

• **lofaszvanitt** 对 fstoppers 网站的内容持批评态度，认为其内容没有价值或不真实，但没有深入讨论具体摄影规则。

补充讨论：
• **codingdave** 提到了摄影规则的历史背景，指出这些规则在社交媒体兴起前后都被视为基础指导原则，且与艺术教育（如美术学位）中的教学内容有关联。

• **sherdil2022** 进一步讨论了规则在实际应用中的灵活性，强调了适应市场需求的重要性，即使这意味着要打破传统的摄影美学规则。

争议焦点：摄影规则应被视为指导原则还是必须遵循的标准。codingdave 和 sherdil2022 都认为规则是为了帮助初学者，并应在适当时候被打破以实现创意，但 lofaszvanitt 对相关讨论平台持怀疑态度，未直接参与规则本身的讨论。

44495591.article_content:
Remember when photography had rules? Not guidelines or suggestions, but actual rules that separated the pros from the amateurs, the trained from the untrained, the serious from the snapshot-happy masses. These weren't arbitrary dictates from some photography ivory tower—they were hard-won principles developed over more than a century of image-making, refined through decades of darkroom experimentation, and codified in countless photography textbooks that gathering dust on our shelves. Then social media happened.
In less than two decades, platforms like Instagram, TikTok, and Pinterest didn't just bend these rules—they obliterated them entirely. What took photographers generations to establish as visual law was dismantled by algorithms, engagement metrics, and the relentless pursuit of the double-tap. The result? A complete inversion of photographic values that would make Ansel Adams roll over in his grave and send Henri Cartier-Bresson reaching for his Leica in protest.
The most shocking part isn't that these rules changed, it's how completely and how quickly they were abandoned. Traditional photography education emphasized technical mastery, compositional discipline, and subtle artistry. Social media rewards the exact opposite: rule-breaking compositions, technically "flawed" images, and anything that stops the endless scroll. The photographers who spent years mastering zone systems, color temperature, and the mathematics of composition suddenly found themselves competing with teenagers wielding smartphones and Facetune.
But here's the uncomfortable truth that many veteran photographers refuse to acknowledge: social media didn't just break these rules randomly. It systematically destroyed the ones that didn't serve its core function—capturing and holding attention in an infinitely scrollable feed. The rules that survived did so because they adapted to screens, algorithms, and attention spans measured in milliseconds rather than minutes.
Rule 1: The Rule of Thirds — From Mathematical Precision to Algorithmic Rebellion
The Golden Age of Grid-Based Composition
For over a century, the rule of thirds stood as photography's most fundamental compositional principle. Derived from the classical "golden ratio" and refined through Renaissance painting techniques, this rule divided every frame into nine equal sections, creating four intersection points where the eye naturally gravitated. Photography schools built entire curricula around it. Camera manufacturers literally built it into their viewfinders.
The rule wasn't arbitrary. Extensive eye-tracking studies throughout the 1970s and 1980s consistently demonstrated that viewers' eyes moved in predictable patterns, dwelling longest at those mathematical intersection points. Professional photographers internalized this so completely that placing subjects on the thirds became as automatic as checking exposure settings.
The Square Format Revolution
Then Instagram launched in 2010 with a 1:1 aspect ratio that immediately broke the rule of thirds' fundamental assumption. The original rule was designed for rectangular frames—3:2 from 35mm film, 4:3 from medium format, 5:4 from large format view cameras. These proportions created natural thirds divisions that guided the eye through hierarchical compositions.
But Instagram's square format created an entirely different visual dynamic. Suddenly, centered compositions didn't just work—they dominated. The square's inherent symmetry made central placement feel balanced rather than static. The eye no longer needed to travel through the frame in the predictable patterns that rectangular compositions encouraged.
Early Instagram success stories built massive followings with aggressively centered compositions that would have been marked "incorrect" in any traditional photography course. These weren't accidental successes—they were responding to how people actually consumed images on mobile screens.
Vertical Video Supremacy and the Death of Landscape Orientation
The arrival of TikTok and Instagram Stories introduced the 9:16 vertical format, which completely demolished traditional compositional wisdom. The rule of thirds, designed for horizontal exploration of space, became nearly impossible to apply meaningfully in ultra-tall vertical frames.
Studies show that vertical video content receives far more engagement than horizontal content across all social platforms. After all, how do we hold phones?
Algorithm-Driven Composition: Chaos as Strategy
Perhaps the most devastating blow to the rule of thirds came from platform algorithms themselves. Facebook's internal research revealed that their algorithm actively promoted content that generated "meaningful social interactions"—comments, shares, and extended engagement. What drives these interactions? Controversy, surprise, and visual elements that violate expectations. Images that followed traditional compositional rules, no matter how beautifully executed, were algorithmically deprioritized

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Ralphie运行演示及其相关的随机性生成问题

不同观点：
• Cshelton认为Ralphie运行演示非常有趣，并提到可以用Ralphie过去一年的实际运行作为真正的随机性示例。这表明他对这种随机性生成方式持调侃和娱乐态度。
• CaliforniaKarl关注技术实现，表示希望该演示使用与NIST信标相同的API（v1或v2 API），显示出对技术标准和互操作性的关注。
• Octokat和tonnydourado的回复较为简短，主要以幽默和轻松的态度回应，没有深入讨论技术问题。
• ribcage持批评态度，认为所有计算机设备本身就能生成随机性，因此没必要信任一个随机网站。他的观点强调了对网络上随机性生成器的不信任。
• ntnsndr提出一个不同的角度，询问这是否是区块链的一个用例，暗示区块链技术可能在这一场景中发挥作用。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中存在对随机性生成方式的调侃与批评，有人认为实际设备本身就能提供足够的随机性，质疑在线随机性演示的可信度。
• 技术细节上，有人关心API的标准化问题，希望不同系统之间能够有更好的互操作性。
• 争议焦点在于网络上的随机性生成是否可信，以及是否有必要使用特定的技术（如区块链）来解决这一问题。

data.title: Epanet-JS
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: EPANET-js是一款结合现代网络地图和行业标准EPANET液压模拟算法的网页应用，旨在帮助规划和更新供水系统。该工具由Iterating团队开发，利用了Tom MacWright之前发布的开放源代码工具Placemark，并对其进行了改进，甚至将核心库也进行了开源。EPANET-js与传统昂贵且局限于Windows的软件形成鲜明对比，提供了更便捷、成本更低的解决方案。通过使用WASM引擎，用户可以在浏览器中进行完整的模拟。这一项目不仅展示了开放源代码的价值，还为液压模拟领域提供了创新工具。

44464628.article_content:
epanet-js
epanet-js
is a new web application that combines modern web maps with the industry-standard
EPANET
hydraulic simulation algorithm. It’s for people planning and updating water utility systems: connecting pipes and pressures and figuring out what will happen. It’s a problem area that I’m totally fascinated by and know very little about. It’s made by the folks from
Iterating
- Luke Butler and Sam Payá, who are experts in the field.
If you’ve been following along with my blog and projects, you might notice something familiar about this screenshot of epanet-js:
Yep! A lifetime ago, I built a company and product called
Placemark
, which was a tool for creating and editing map data. When the business part didn’t work out, I published a
free-to-use version of Placemark
and
made the code open source
. I chose a very permissive license for the code:
the MIT license
. I wanted to let
anything
happen, including -
especially
- people creating paid products with the code.
It’s hard to explain to people outside of the world of open source that folks building a business with the help of my code is
the dream
.
Partly it’s that ‘being helpful’ is one of the goals in life that never gets old. The other part is that
most software becomes obsolete and abandoned quickly
. Creating software with any legacy is rare and something to celebrate.
Plus, Placemark was a general purpose tool in search of a successful niche: I never figured out what that niche was. I had a lot of learning to do about product-market-fit. But hydraulic simulation is a real market, and these folks are real experts.
There are other markets like this, I’m sure, and using Placemark code as a base could be a good way to jumpstart those companies - it’s not perfect, as I’ve documented extensively, but it could be good as a first step.
And the folks at Iterating have even
contributed changes upstream to the open source Placemark
codebase, but that isn’t required by the MIT license at all: that’s just because they’re cool folks.
They’ve also
open sourced the core epanet-js library
, and released the web application
under the Functional Source License
, which
makes new code contributions open source after two years
.
</source>
And epanet-js is a tool that you can run in a browser - full simulations with a WASM-based engine. It’s competing with expensive old-school software that costs $16,000 a year, runs exclusively on Windows, is
priced by “pipes”
, and uses the same engine, EPANET. This is so much better in comparison. A radical improvement.
Congrats to Luke and Sam for creating
epanet-js
. It’s super cool. If you speak hydraulic simulation or know someone who does, try it out!
July 3, 2025
Tom MacWright
@macwright.com on Bluesky
,
@tmcw@mastodon.social on Mastodon
44464628.article_summary: EPANET-js是一款结合现代网络地图和行业标准EPANET液压模拟算法的网页应用，旨在帮助规划和更新供水系统。该工具由Iterating团队开发，利用了Tom MacWright之前发布的开放源代码工具Placemark，并对其进行了改进，甚至将核心库也进行了开源。EPANET-js与传统昂贵且局限于Windows的软件形成鲜明对比，提供了更便捷、成本更低的解决方案。通过使用WASM引擎，用户可以在浏览器中进行完整的模拟。这一项目不仅展示了开放源代码的价值，还为液压模拟领域提供了创新工具。

data.title: BBC staff: we're forced to do pro-Israel PR
data.author: mhga
data.article_summary: 超过100名BBC员工联名写信投诉，指责公司在报道以色列和巴勒斯坦问题时成为以色列的传声筒。信中指出，BBC管理层拒绝播出纪录片《加沙：战火中的医护人员》，尽管该片内容已符合BBC的编辑政策。员工认为这是政治决策，反映出BBC因害怕被视为批评以色列政府而做出的自我审查。信中还提到，BBC没有对英国政府在巴勒斯坦战争中的角色进行重要分析，也未报道武器销售及其法律影响。员工强调，这不是要求BBC选边站，而是允许记者透明报道事实。信中特别提到BBC董事会成员罗比·吉布（Sir Robbie Gibb），他与犹太纪事报有密切联系，该报曾多次发表反巴勒斯坦内容。此外，文章还批评了吉布的政治背景及其对BBC新闻输出的影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：BBC在报道以巴冲突新闻中的偏见问题，以及更广泛的媒体操控与政治影响问题。

不同观点：
• **观点一（topspin）**：认为BBC在报道以色列相关新闻时，存在明显的反以色列偏见，大量报道以色列对巴勒斯坦人的袭击，并将来自哈马斯控制部门的消息作为主要来源，质疑这是否属于客观报道。
• **观点二（hliyan）**：提出更广泛的政治经济背景，认为现代社会通过媒体操控和经济手段（如学生债务、租金、健康保险）来实现对大众的控制，类似于过去的君主制和封建制度。
• **观点三（gruez）**：对有关BBC偏见的公开信表示怀疑，认为信中缺乏具体证据，特别是关于纪录片《Gaza: Medics Under Fire》被撤下的原因不明，呼吁更可靠的信息来源。
• **观点四（jaek）**：认为这种偏见不仅限于BBC，还存在于其他公共媒体中，如澳大利亚的ABC，担心这些媒体被外国势力操控。
• **观点五（engine_y）**：基于个人经验，认为BBC实际上持反战立场，不认为其有明显的亲以色列倾向。
• **观点六（molteanu）**：批评欧洲禁止RT（俄罗斯今日）的做法，认为这是对个人判断能力的否定，并指出许多本地政府资助的媒体同样可能存在偏见。
• **观点七（epja）**：提出BBC也被指控过有反以色列的偏见，包括播出与哈马斯有关联的个人制作的纪录片。
• **观点八（jjangkke）**：引用一句名言，暗示对权力的批评受限，反映了媒体偏见问题背后的权力结构。
• **观点九（swoorup）**：认为全球自新冠疫情以来，强权者通过胁迫和宣传来实现领土扩张，任何反对者都会被贴上标签，反映了更广泛的政治操控问题。
• **观点十（iceKirin）**：质疑在强弱冲突中的所谓“中立”是否真的中立，暗示媒体的中立性可能只是表面。
• **观点十一（fyurule）**：质疑BBC员工是否是最后才意识到偏见问题的人。
• **观点十二（chvid）**：认为这种偏见在整个西方媒体中普遍存在，不仅仅是BBC。

补充讨论：
• 一些评论提到具体的新闻事件和来源链接，例如topspin列出的BBC新闻标题，以及epja和jaek提供的补充链接，试图通过外部来源支持各自的观点。
• 关于纪录片《Gaza: Medics Under Fire》被撤下的争议，gruez和其他评论质疑是否存在真正的 censorship（审查）或偏见。
• molteanu和jjangkke的评论扩展了讨论，将媒体偏见问题与更广泛的权力结构和信息操控联系起来。

争议焦点：BBC在以巴冲突报道中是否存在亲以色列或反以色列的偏见，以及更广泛的媒体操控和政治影响问题。

A devastating letter signed by over 100 BBC journalists underlines one of the great scandals of our age

This is a devastating intervention. More than a hundred BBC employees
have written a letter
to the director general, Tim Davie, complaining that the Corporation has become a mouthpiece for Israel.
It was also signed by 300 other journalists and media professionals: one of them was yours truly. The BBC employees, as you would expect, are all anonymous, because otherwise they would face grave consequences to their careers.
The letter says:
We’re writing to express our concerns over opaque editorial decisions and censorship at the BBC on the reporting of Israel/Palestine. We believe the refusal to broadcast the documentary ‘Gaza: Medics Under Fire’ is just one in a long line of agenda driven decisions. It demonstrates, once again, that the BBC is not reporting “without fear or favour” when it comes to Israel.
It goes on to note that the decision not to broadcast the investigation was taken by BBC management despite the content being signed off in accordance with BBC guidelines and editorial policy, which it says “Appears to be a political decision”, adding that the BBC response shows the organisation “is crippled by the fear of being perceived as critical of the Israeli government.”
BattleLines with Owen Jones is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.
Subscribe
This is a letter which passed every single BBC internal check. No factual errors are alleged. The only other BBC documentary which focused on the apocalyptic plight of the Palestinian people in Gaza was taken down as a result of a hysterical pro-Israel campaign - because the father of the child narrator’s son had a junior technocratic position in the Hamas administration. Irrelevant, given the narrator’s words were written for him by the documentary producers.
The letter emphasises that the signatories are not “asking the BBC to take a side”, but just to allow BBC journalists to “do their jobs in delivering facts transparently and with due context”. They note one striking failure:
As an organisation we have not offered any significant analysis of the UK government's involvement in the war on Palestinians. We have failed to report on weapons sales or their legal implications. These stories have instead been broken by the BBC’s competitors.
This is, by the way one of many striking scandalous failures on the part of the BBC, which is a public service broadcaster which is duty bound to hold the British government to account and has failed to do so.
And this is the really crucial allegation. The letter says:
This hasn’t happened by accident, rather by design. Much of the BBC’s coverage in this area is defined by anti-Palestinian racism.
This is exactly it. There hasn’t even been a pretence by the BBC that Palestinian life has even the fraction of the worth of an Israeli life. When I did my detailed investigation into BBC coverage for
Drop Site News
at the end of the last year, I worked with data journalists who used incontrovertible statistics to show how this is the case.
The letter mentions a crucial name. It says:
The inconsistent manner in which guidance is applied draws into focus the role of Sir Robbie Gibb, on the BBC Board and BBC’s Editorial Standards Committee. We are concerned that an individual with close ties to the Jewish Chronicle, an outlet that has repeatedly published anti-Palestinian and often racist content, has a say in the BBC's editorial decisions in any capacity, including the decision not to broadcast ‘Gaza: Medics Under Fire’.
Sir Robbie Gibb is a striking case study. The brother of a Tory minister, he joined the BBC as a political researcher after he graduated, before becoming chief of staff for Tory Shadow Chancellor Francis Maude. He then returned to the BBC as deputy editor of the flagship current affairs programme Newsnight, then became the editor for BBC political programmes such as Daily Politics, where he worked closely with its main presenter, Andrew Neil, then chairman of the hard right Spectator magazine. He then went off in 2017 to become director of communications for the Tory prime minister Theresa May. He then returned to the BBC, joining its Board.
Share
You can be forgiven if this revolving door between the Tories and BBC has left you dizzy.
He was singled out
by the likes of former Newsnight presenter Emily Maitlis who said he was an “active agent of the Conservative party” who was shaping the Corporation’s news output by acting “as the arbiter of BBC impartiality”.

data.title: What is going on in Unix with errno's limited nature
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary: 本文解释了为何一些用户在访问作者博客（Wandering Thoughts）或相关wiki（CSpace）时被阻止。原因在于，作者的反爬虫措施会拦截使用过旧浏览器（尤其是旧版Chrome）的访问者，以应对2025年初大量使用旧浏览器用户代理的高流量爬虫。这些爬虫常用于收集数据训练语言模型。如果用户确实在使用新版浏览器却被误拦，可联系作者。此外，使用archive.*（如archive.today）的用户也会被误认为恶意爬虫，建议改用更为规范的archive.org进行存档。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Linux内核中errno的使用及其问题，包括错误处理的透明性、调试困难和设计上的局限性。

不同观点：
• [rwmj] 认为当前Linux内核中errno的最大问题是无法记录错误发生的位置，导致调试困难，尤其是在错误是在底层系统调用或异步任务中设置的情况下。他还提到，在Linux中实现详细的错误记录非常困难，因为错误通常是通过返回负值的副作用来设置的，且很多代码中并没有明确的错误记录。
• [userbinator] 则认为errno的行为并不奇怪，并将其与Windows的GetLastError()进行比较，指出在调用成功时错误码并不重要。同时，他认为在每次成功调用时将errno设为0是多余的，尤其在资源受限的历史背景下更是如此。
• [jezze] 提出了一种不同的设计思路，建议将错误信息和返回值分离到不同的寄存器中，以避免返回值的歧义和类型混淆问题，从而提高代码的清晰度。
• [toast0] 认为C语言本身的局限性导致了当前错误处理方式的存在，因为C语言难以处理CPU标志等其他返回方式，因此采用当前这种通过返回值和errno结合的方式。
• [badc0ffee] 补充了一些libc函数中通过检查errno来判断调用是否成功的具体例子，如strtol函数，强调了在某些情况下必须手动检查errno。
• [0xbadcafebee] 从更广泛的软件设计角度出发，讨论了系统中缺乏可见性的问题，认为理想的设计应具有良好的内聚性和松散耦合，同时能够在出现问题时提供足够的错误信息。他还提到了分布式追踪和可观察性工具的重要性，认为现有的软件设计模式在这方面存在不足。

补充讨论：
• [tptacek] 提供了一个与错误处理相关的历史文档链接，可能涉及一些过时但相关的技术细节。
• [amelius] 简单提出了线程相关的问题，但未展开讨论。

争议焦点：
• 当前Linux内核中errno机制的调试困难和透明性问题。
• 是否需要在每次成功调用时将errno设为0，以及这种做法是否多余。
• 错误信息和返回值是否应该分离到不同寄存器中以提高清晰度。
• 如何在更大范围的软件系统中实现更好的错误追踪和可观察性。

44461666.article_content:
You're using a suspiciously old browser
You're probably reading this page because you've attempted to access
some part of
my blog (Wandering Thoughts)
or
CSpace
, the wiki thing it's part of. Unfortunately
you're using a browser version that my anti-crawler precautions consider
suspicious, most often because it's too old (most often this applies to
versions of Chrome). Unfortunately, as of early 2025 there's a plague
of high volume crawlers (apparently in part to gather data for LLM
training) that use a variety of old browser user agents, especially
Chrome user agents. To reduce the load on
Wandering Thoughts
I'm experimenting with
(attempting to) block all of them, and you've run into this.
If this is in error and you're using a current version of your
browser of choice, you can contact me at
my current place at the
university
(you should be able to work out the email address
from that). If possible, please let me know what browser you're
using and so on, ideally with its exactl User-Agent string.
A special note for people using archive.*
You may be seeing this through archive.today, archive.ph, archive.is,
and so on. Unfortunately, archive.* crawls pages to archive in a way that
is impossible to distinguish from malicious actors. They use old Chrome
User-Agent values, crawl from IP address blocks that are widely distributed
and not clearly identified as theirs, and some of their IP addresses have
falsified reverse DNS entries that claim they are googlebot IP addresses
(which is something that is normally done only by quite bad actors). I
suggest that you use archive.org, which is a better behaved archival
crawler and can crawl
my blog (Wandering Thoughts)
.
Chris Siebenmann, 2025-02-17

data.title: Trying to find meaning in owning an old Mac
data.author: decryption
data.article_summary: 文章讲述了作者与父亲在不同年代对经典物品的怀旧情感。作者的父亲热爱经典汽车，这些车代表了他年轻时的主流科技和社会变革。作者则对经典电脑感兴趣，尤其是1989年发布的Apple Macintosh SE/30。尽管作者在孩童时期并未接触过这类电脑，但他对那个时代的科技怀有探索兴趣，类似于他对音乐溯源的过程。作者意识到，自己正像中年时的父亲一样，回顾并珍惜属于他们各自时代的“经典”——父亲是汽车，而作者是电脑。作者计划像父亲修复汽车一样，修复这台Mac，并从中获得乐趣和怀旧感。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：老旧计算机及其应用程序的价值与怀旧情感

不同观点：
• LarryMade2 列举了一系列老旧Mac应用程序，如WriteNow、ClarisWorks、FoxBase+/Mac、SuperPaint、HyperCard等，强调了这些程序在功能性和易用性上的优点，并提及它们在特定领域的出色表现。
• pbohun 认为老旧计算机和老旧汽车一样，更容易被普通人理解和修改，强调了现代技术和设备在“拥有权”和“可理解性”上的缺失，呼吁重拾所有权的概念。
• ferguess_k 表示自己拥有一台vintage iBook G4，但对其用途感到迷茫，虽然最初有兴趣了解PowerPC架构和Apple的68K模拟器，但最终因工作疲劳和缺乏编程兴趣而放弃。
• zdw 强调老旧计算机的简单性，并指出通过一些现代项目和工具可以增强这些计算机的功能，如BlueSCSI项目，同时认为修复老旧计算机的工具成本低且易于获取。
• whartung 描述了通过升级老旧计算机如SE/30来实现现代用途的可能性，如通过添加网络适配器和Raspberry Pi来实现电子邮件和网络浏览功能。
• jnaina 分享了自己丰富的Apple产品收藏，包括Apple ][e、Lisa、NeXT Cube等，但表示孩子们对继承这些“古董”没有兴趣，认为可以通过模拟器体验旧软件而不必保留实物。

• JSR_FDED 表示对Apple ][ 的怀旧情感，认为无需为这种复古计算热情找借口，强调了那个时代技术和社区的理想主义和匠心。
• keyle 对现代技术感到“一切都已解决”且难以修复表示不满，幻想重温386 DX 33等老旧计算机的时光，并对孩子们对iPad的未来感受表示怀疑。
• rcarmo 分享了自己通过3D打印和设计复刻早期Mac体验的经历，强调了对早期Mac的怀旧和兴趣，同时指出早期互联网和基本工具时代的乐趣。
• threeio 提醒SE/30存在电池和电容问题，建议尽快清理。
• ggm 认为怀旧情感有时会被时间蒙骗，老旧设备的键盘和鼠标对手感不如记忆中友好。
• kaonwarb 回忆了自己超频50 MHz Pentium到75 MHz的经历，感到非常神奇。
• jdkee 分享了自己对8到15岁期间使用的技术设备的怀旧情感，包括Radio Shack电子套件、Commodore Amiga 500等，认为当前大学生未来会对Minecraft、Angry Birds等产生类似的怀旧情感。

• 老旧计算机和应用程序的怀旧价值与实际使用之间的矛盾。
• 现代技术和设备在拥有权、可理解性和可修复性上的问题。
